title: Supply-chain integrity & authenticity
applies_when: always (anything downloaded and executed by users)
---

# Supply-chain integrity & authenticity

Integrity (checksums) proves the bytes weren't corrupted. Authenticity (signatures / provenance) proves
**who** built them. Checksums from the same origin as the binary give integrity only.

### SEC-01 · MUST · Checksums for every asset, verified by installer AND updater
SHA-256, looked up by **exact filename equality** (not grep substring), exactly one entry required,
tool fallback `sha256sum` → `shasum -a 256` → `openssl dgst -sha256` / `Get-FileHash`.

### SEC-02 · SHOULD · Keyless signing + provenance
`cosign sign-blob --bundle <asset>.sigstore.json` (keyless, OIDC), `actions/attest-build-provenance`,
SBOM per platform (Syft SPDX) attested to its archive. **Verify inside the release job** before upload
with the exact certificate identity `…/release.yml@refs/tags/vX` and `gh attestation verify`.

### SEC-03 · SHOULD · Signature verification degrades loudly, can be required
If `cosign` present → verify. If absent → print the exact verify command and say "checksum verified;
signature NOT checked". `<APP>_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=1` makes it mandatory.

### SEC-04 · MUST · Download hardening
HTTPS only (`--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2`), refuse non-HTTPS base URLs, connect + **wall-clock** timeouts
(curl `--max-time`; wrap wget in `timeout`, its `--timeout` is idle-only), per-asset byte caps
(`--max-filesize`).

### SEC-05 · MUST · Archive extraction is safe
Reject absolute paths, `..`, drive letters, symlinks, hardlinks, device files. Expect an exact layout
(e.g. exactly one regular file named `<bin>`).

### SEC-06 · SHOULD · Dependency policy in CI
Rust `cargo deny check advisories bans sources`; Go `govulncheck`; Node `npm audit --omit=dev` / lockfile
lint. Fail the release on known advisories.

### SEC-07 · MAY · Content-addressed release identity
Release identity = digest of a canonical manifest (sorted keys) of all files (digest, mode, class).
Enables `verify` (re-hash installed tree), quarantine, and exact-digest pins. (forgent)

### SEC-08 · MAY · OS code signing
Windows Authenticode (avoids SmartScreen), macOS codesign + notarization (avoids Gatekeeper). If not
done, document the workaround in troubleshooting.

id_prefix: PRN
title: Cross-cutting principles
applies_when: always
---

# Cross-cutting principles

These hold for every area. Each later rule is an application of one of these.

### PRN-01 · MUST · One source of truth per fact
Version, asset naming, install paths, default config, and the list of supported targets each live in
exactly one place. Everything else reads or is generated from it, or a test proves they agree.
- Why: every bug found across the four studied projects was drift between two copies (installer vs.
  binary paths, release archive vs. updater, plugin manifest vs. product version).
- Seen: forgent `include_str!(package.json)`; herdr-go `--internal-print-default-config`;
  skillstation installer/binary purge-path drift (counter-example).

### PRN-02 · MUST · Fail closed, say why, name the fix
Missing checksum, mismatched hash, unreadable config, unknown platform → stop. Every error prints
**what** failed, **why**, and the **exact next command** (Error / Why / Fix).

### PRN-03 · MUST · Idempotent and re-runnable
Installer, `doctor --fix`, setup, update can be run any number of times. A second run with nothing to
do says so and changes nothing.

### PRN-04 · MUST · Atomic changes, with rollback
Write to a temp file in the **same directory** → fsync → rename. Keep the previous version until the
new one has been proven (smoke-run / health check). On failure, restore.

### PRN-05 · MUST · Never clobber what you don't own
Only modify files/blocks you can prove you created: ownership marker files, fenced
`START/END` blocks, digests of everything you ever shipped. Unknown content = user's = leave it.

### PRN-06 · MUST · Plan → preview → confirm → apply for anything destructive or outside your own dirs
`--dry-run` shows the plan. Non-TTY without `--yes` refuses. Re-read files at apply time.

### PRN-07 · SHOULD · Test what users actually run
The literal one-liner, from published (or about-to-be-published) assets, outside the checkout, on every
supported OS, including upgrade-from-previous and uninstall.

### PRN-08 · SHOULD · Same behaviour for humans and machines
Every user-facing command has `--json`; exit codes are meaningful and documented.

### PRN-09 · SHOULD · Least surprise with the user's environment
Don't edit dotfiles, PATH, global agent configs or services silently. Either print the exact command or
write a clearly fenced, removable block, and report every change made.

### PRN-10 · SHOULD · Respect privilege boundaries
Refuse to run user-scoped steps as root (or skip them under `sudo` and print what the user must run).
Never widen file permissions; secrets are 0600 / owner-only ACL.

### VER-02 · MUST · Release gate: tag == source version
The release workflow's first job fails if `vX.Y.Z` ≠ the SoT version. (forgent `check-version`)

### VER-03 · MUST · Every extra manifest is synced or tested
Plugin manifests (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `herdr-plugin.toml`, `marketplace.json`), lockfiles,
installer default versions. A test or hook fails on drift.

- Linux: prefer **static** binaries (musl / CGO off). If you must link glibc, build on the oldest
  supported image and enforce a **glibc ceiling** check (`objdump -T`, forgent `check-glibc-ceiling.sh`).

### REL-02 · MUST · One deterministic asset-naming rule, defined in one place
`<name>-<version>-<os>-<arch>.<tar.gz|zip>` or `<name>-<target-triple>[.exe]`. Installer, updater,
release workflow and docs derive from the same rule; a test (or static contract script) cross-checks them.
- Decide **archive vs. bare binary** once. Archives let you ship LICENSE, README, completions, service
  files; bare binaries are simpler. Whatever you choose, installer and updater must handle **the same
  format** (herdr-go's updater wrote the tar.gz over the exe).

### REL-03 · MUST · Release is gated by the full CI
The release workflow calls CI as a reusable workflow (`uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml`) or `needs:` it.
Nothing ships that wouldn't pass on `main`.

### REL-04 · MUST · Packaging is tested on every PR, publishing only on tag
A reusable "build release assets" workflow runs on PRs/pushes (build + package + consumer proof, no
upload). The tag workflow calls the same workflow then publishes. (forgent `release-assets.yml`)

### REL-05 · MUST · One packaging script used by local dry run, CI and release
No asset name / layout / checksum logic duplicated in YAML. (forgent `package-release-assets.mjs`)

### REL-06 · MUST · Checksums published only when every target built
A final job `needs:` all build jobs, merges, sorts and writes `checksums.txt` / `SHA256SUMS` (outside
the hashed dir), re-verifies with `sha256sum --check`, and asserts the expected asset count.
Include the installers in the checksum file.

### REL-07 · SHOULD · Draft → smoke → publish
Create the release as a **draft** (or upload to a staging location), run post-build smoke tests against
those exact assets, then un-draft. Avoids a public broken release (gap in herdr-go and skillstation).

### REL-08 · SHOULD · Stamp the version into release-attached installers
Installer contains `DEFAULT_VERSION='@VERSION@'`; release job `sed`s and greps to confirm. Then
`releases/latest/download/install.sh` installs exactly its own release; the raw repo copy refuses to run
without `--version` (skillstation). Alternatively, if installer is served from raw `main`, it must
resolve the version itself — never assume.

### REL-09 · SHOULD · Reproducible builds
Commit-time timestamps (`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`), path trimming, deterministic archives
(`tar --sort=name --mtime=@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --owner=0 --numeric-owner | gzip -n`), sorted checksum
files. MAY: independent rebuild job + digest compare (forgent).

### REL-10 · SHOULD · Hardened workflow
`permissions: {}` at top, grant per job; pin actions by **commit SHA**; pin runner images
(`ubuntu-22.04`, not `-latest`); hash-pin any third-party binary downloaded in CI; `fail-fast: false`
on the build matrix; per-target cache keys.

### REL-11 · SHOULD · Embedded front-end assets never break a clean build
Either commit the built bundle, or have the build script create the embed dir so the code compiles
without Node — **and** have CI fail if a release binary ships with an empty bundle.

### REL-12 · SHOULD · Release profile tuned for distribution
Strip symbols, LTO, size optimisation where startup/size matter (see language guide).

### REL-13 · MAY · Manual dispatch produces a clearly-marked non-installable draft

### REL-14 · SHOULD · Release notes generated
`generate_release_notes: true` or from CHANGELOG; `fail_on_unmatched_files: true`.

id_prefix: SEC
title: Supply-chain integrity & authenticity
applies_when: always (anything downloaded and executed by users)
---

# Supply-chain integrity & authenticity

Integrity (checksums) proves the bytes weren't corrupted. Authenticity (signatures / provenance) proves
**who** built them. Checksums from the same origin as the binary give integrity only.

### SEC-01 · MUST · Checksums for every asset, verified by installer AND updater
SHA-256, looked up by **exact filename equality** (not grep substring), exactly one entry required,
tool fallback `sha256sum` → `shasum -a 256` → `openssl dgst -sha256` / `Get-FileHash`.

### SEC-02 · SHOULD · Keyless signing + provenance
`cosign sign-blob --bundle <asset>.sigstore.json` (keyless, OIDC), `actions/attest-build-provenance`,
SBOM per platform (Syft SPDX) attested to its archive. **Verify inside the release job** before upload
with the exact certificate identity `…/release.yml@refs/tags/vX` and `gh attestation verify`.

### SEC-03 · SHOULD · Signature verification degrades loudly, can be required
If `cosign` present → verify. If absent → print the exact verify command and say "checksum verified;
signature NOT checked". `<APP>_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=1` makes it mandatory.

### SEC-04 · MUST · Download hardening
HTTPS only (`--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2`), refuse non-HTTPS base URLs, connect + **wall-clock** timeouts
(curl `--max-time`; wrap wget in `timeout`, its `--timeout` is idle-only), per-asset byte caps
(`--max-filesize`).

### SEC-05 · MUST · Archive extraction is safe
Reject absolute paths, `..`, drive letters, symlinks, hardlinks, device files. Expect an exact layout
(e.g. exactly one regular file named `<bin>`).

### SEC-06 · SHOULD · Dependency policy in CI
Rust `cargo deny check advisories bans sources`; Go `govulncheck`; Node `npm audit --omit=dev` / lockfile
lint. Fail the release on known advisories.

### SEC-07 · MAY · Content-addressed release identity
Release identity = digest of a canonical manifest (sorted keys) of all files (digest, mode, class).
Enables `verify` (re-hash installed tree), quarantine, and exact-digest pins. (forgent)

### SEC-08 · MAY · OS code signing
Windows Authenticode (avoids SmartScreen), macOS codesign + notarization (avoids Gatekeeper). If not
done, document the workaround in troubleshooting.

title: Install scripts (install.sh / install.ps1)
applies_when: always (binary distributed outside a package manager)

# Install scripts

Reference implementation: `templates/install.sh` (POSIX sh skeleton applying these rules).

### INS-01 · MUST · One-liners for each OS family
`curl -fsSL <url>/install.sh | sh` and `irm <url>/install.ps1 | iex`. Prefer the URL
`https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/latest/download/install.sh` (version-stamped, REL-08) over raw `main`.

### INS-02 · MUST · Truncation-safe script structure
POSIX `sh` (not bash-only unless you require bash), `set -eu`, everything inside functions,
**`main "$@"` as the very last line** so a cut-off download can't execute a partial script.

### INS-03 · MUST · Platform detection with allow-list
`uname -s`/`uname -m` → mapped through the single naming rule (REL-02). Windows: check
`PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` before `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` (32-bit shell on 64-bit OS). Unsupported →
error that names the fallback (`cargo install --git …`, `go install …`, build-from-source doc).
Redirect Windows shells (MSYS/Cygwin) to `install.ps1`.

### INS-04 · MUST · Every knob is both env var and flag, all prefixed
`<APP>_VERSION`, `<APP>_INSTALL_DIR` (or `PREFIX`), `<APP>_RELEASE_BASE` / `ASSET_BASE_URL`
(mirror, air-gap, test fixtures — one meaning only!), `<APP>_DRY_RUN`, `<APP>_NO_MODIFY_PATH`,
`<APP>_YES`, `<APP>_UNINSTALL`. Document them in a table.

### INS-05 · MUST · Resolve "latest" without the GitHub API
Use `releases/latest/download/<asset>` or follow the `/releases/latest` redirect
(`curl -w '%{url_effective}'`). No API call → no rate limit, no token.

### INS-06 · MUST · Download to a temp dir, verify, then atomically activate
`mktemp -d` + `trap 'rm -rf …' EXIT INT TERM`; verify checksum (SEC-01), optional signature (SEC-03),
archive shape (SEC-05); **run `<candidate> --version` before activation**; copy to
`<dir>/.<bin>.new.$$` in the **target dir**, `chmod 755`, `mv -f` over target.
- Renaming (not writing in place) avoids "Text file busy" when a daemon runs from the binary.
- Windows: rename the running exe to `.old`, move new in; the binary deletes `.old*` on next start.

### INS-07 · SHOULD · Ownership marker next to the binary
`.<app>-managed` (`<app>-managed-v1\nversion=X`, mode 0600). Refuse to overwrite or uninstall a binary
without it; same-version + marker → no-op (only re-check PATH). The updater uses it too (UPD-02).

### INS-08 · SHOULD · Rollback on post-activation failure
Keep `.rollback` copy; if the activated binary fails `--version`, restore binary + marker.

### INS-09 · MUST · Sensible install dir, no root by default
Default `~/.local/bin` (Unix), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\bin` (Windows). Refuse to run as root unless
`<APP>_ALLOW_ROOT=1`. MAY pick first writable of a candidate list.

### INS-10 · MUST · PATH handling is explicit — choose one policy and document it
- Policy A (conservative): never edit rc files; detect missing PATH entry and print the exact
  `export PATH=…` / `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(...)` line.
- Policy B (convenient): write a **fenced** block `# >>> <app> >>>` … `# <<< <app> <<<` into the right
  rc files (`.bashrc`, `.bash_profile` on macOS, `${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zshrc`,
  `~/.config/fish/conf.d/<app>.fish`, fallback `.profile`); skip read-only files; `--no-modify-path`
  opt-out; uninstall removes the blocks. Windows: `HKCU\Environment` preserving `REG_EXPAND_SZ`
  and broadcast `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`.

### INS-11 · SHOULD · Network fallbacks are precise
Missing asset (HTTP 404) → MAY fall back to source build; **any other error → hard fail** (never hide a
network problem behind a 10-minute compile). Support `curl` and `wget`.

### INS-12 · MUST · Installer and binary agree on every path
If the installer creates config/state (default config, tokens, service files), the paths come from the
binary (`<bin> paths --json` or `--internal-print-default-config`), or a comment "MUST match
src/…" plus a contract test.

### INS-13 · SHOULD · Bootstrap through the binary, not the script
After placing the binary, delegate everything else (default config, secrets, service, agent
integration) to the binary (`<bin> setup` / `doctor --fix`) so logic exists once, in tested code.
The script stays small and rarely changes.

### INS-14 · MUST · Finish with verification and next steps
Run `<bin> --version`, then print 1–3 "Next:" commands (`<bin> init`, `<bin> doctor --fix`).
Print secrets (generated tokens) only on first creation.

### INS-15 · SHOULD · Testable offline
`--local-fixture DIR` (and a fake signature verifier env) lets CI run the full lifecycle — install,
upgrade, idempotent re-run, rollback, refuse unmanaged, size caps, uninstall — without network.

### INS-16 · MAY · Preflight before touching anything
If the install registers a service, check the service manager is reachable first
(`systemctl --user show-environment`, `launchctl` exists).

---
id_prefix: UPD
title: Self-update
applies_when: binary distributed via GitHub Releases / direct download (skip if only via package manager)
---

# Self-update (`<bin> update`)

### UPD-01 · MUST · CLI surface
`<bin> update [--check] [--version vX.Y.Z] [--force] [--json] [--yes]`.
`--check` exits non-zero (e.g. 10) when an update is available, for scripts.

### UPD-02 · MUST · Only update what we installed
Refuse when the binary is managed by a package manager (brew, scoop, npm, cargo) or lacks the
ownership marker (INS-07); print the right command instead (`brew upgrade <app>`, the one-liner).

### UPD-03 · MUST · Same verification as the installer
Same naming rule, same checksum/signature/size-cap/extraction checks (ideally the installer and the
updater share constants generated from one place — PRN-01). Honest result text: say whether the
signature was checked.

### UPD-04 · MUST · Update source from build metadata
Repo URL comes from build metadata (`CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`, ldflags, package.json `repository`) — forks
update from themselves. Overridable base URL env for tests/mirrors.

### UPD-05 · MUST · Version policy is a pure, unit-tested function
`latest` never downgrades; explicit `--version` may; `--force` reinstalls same version only; `dev`
builds read the marker version. Fetch latest **once** and use that same resolved release for compare
and download (no race).

### UPD-06 · MUST · Download matches the release format
If releases are archives, extract (safely) before swapping. Test the updater against **real release
assets** in CI (herdr-go wrote the .tar.gz over the binary).

### UPD-07 · MUST · Stage → smoke → swap → rollback
Stage next to the real binary (resolve symlinks; same filesystem) → run `<staged> --version` and require
the exact target version (with timeout) → back up → atomic rename (Windows: rename running exe to
`.old-<pid>`) → on any failure restore. Clean `.old*` / `.bak-*` leftovers on next start (cap retained
backups).

### UPD-08 · SHOULD · Post-swap work runs in the NEW binary
Spawn the new binary by path for migrations and template refreshes (`<new> doctor --after-update`,
`<new> --internal-merge-config <path>`): the running process still holds old embedded defaults.

### UPD-09 · SHOULD · Services: stop → swap → migrate → start → health → auto-rollback
For daemons: poll a health endpoint (version must equal target); if unhealthy, restore binary **and**
config and restart the old one. Running daemon older than CLI → auto-restart (ask the live process its
version; never downgrade).

### UPD-10 · SHOULD · sudo-aware
Under sudo/root, skip user-scoped steps (daemon, skills, agent configs) and print what to run as the user.

### UPD-11 · SHOULD · Rate limits handled
Prefer redirect-based latest resolution; if using the API, honour `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `<APP>_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

### UPD-12 · MAY · Update notice
Background, cached (≤ once/day), opt-out (`<APP>_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, auto-off in CI / non-TTY)
"new version available" hint. Prerelease channel flag if you ship prereleases.

### UPD-13 · MAY · Pinned per-project runtime instead of global update
For tools whose behaviour must be identical across a team: tiny global bootstrap + per-project pin
(exact digest committed), `upgrade` / `repair` (rollback) / `verify` (re-hash, quarantine) verbs,
stable shim reading an activation file (forgent `fgctl`).

id_prefix: CFG
title: Config, state, secrets & migrations
applies_when: tool has any persistent config, data, cache or secrets
---

# Config, state, secrets & migrations

### CFG-01 · MUST · Separate config / data / state / cache, using OS conventions
| | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| config | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/<app>` | `~/Library/Application Support/<app>` | `%APPDATA%\<app>` |
| data/state | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/<app>` (or `XDG_DATA_HOME`) | same as config dir | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>` |
| cache | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/<app>` | `~/Library/Caches/<app>` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\cache` |
Honour XDG vars only when absolute. A single `~/.<app>/` is acceptable for simple tools but provide
the override below.

### CFG-02 · MUST · One override env var per root, one meaning each
`<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`, `<APP>_STATE_DIR` (or `<APP>_HOME`). Never reuse one name for two things.
Tests/smoke runs set these so they never touch the real user's files.

### CFG-03 · MUST · `<bin> paths [--json]` (or in `doctor`)
Prints resolved config/state/cache/binary paths. Installers, uninstallers and docs consume this
instead of re-deriving paths (fixes skillstation macOS purge bug class).

### CFG-04 · MUST · Documented precedence
`CLI flag > env var > project config > user config > built-in default`. Print it in `--help` /
`config explain <key>` (shows which layer won).

### CFG-05 · MUST · Zero-config start; defaults come from the binary
Missing file → defaults. The binary can print its default config (`config default` /
`--internal-print-default-config`) — installer, `config init` and update-merge all use it; no separate
`config.example.*` that drifts (or generate it in CI and diff).

### CFG-06 · MUST · Atomic writes preserving mode; secrets 0600
Temp in same dir → fsync → rename → (dir fsync). Keep the existing file's permissions (never widen a
0600 file). Config dir 0700 when it holds anything sensitive.

### CFG-07 · MUST · Secrets are not in the main config
Separate file (`<app>.env`, `private/`) with 0600 / owner-only DACL; the binary **refuses** to read a
secret file with loose permissions; env var override (`<APP>_TOKEN`). Service unit files and agent
configs reference the secret **path**, never the value. Generate with a CSPRNG; print once.

### CFG-08 · MUST · Corrupt config = clear error, not silent defaults
Report file, line, problem and fix (`<bin> config edit`, `doctor`). Collect all validation errors at
once. Cap read size.

### CFG-09 · SHOULD · Forward/backward compatible schema
Either preserve unknown keys on rewrite (round-trip raw map) **or** `deny_unknown_fields` with clear
errors — choose consciously: preserve for user-edited files shared across versions; deny for
security-sensitive config. Support renamed keys via aliases.

### CFG-10 · SHOULD · Upgrades merge new defaults without touching user values
Add-missing-keys-only merge, back up first, validate before writing, executed by the **new** binary
(UPD-08).

### CFG-11 · SHOULD · Versioned migrations for data
Numbered migrations (`migration/v3..v7`), `<bin> maintain migrate`; or version in the filename
(`registry-v4.db`) so old and new binaries coexist during upgrade, doctor cleans legacy. Legacy
directory migration fails closed if both old and new exist.

### CFG-12 · SHOULD · Config verbs
`config show | get | set | unset | edit | explain | check | path`. `edit` uses
`$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → `vi`/`notepad`, re-validates after save.

### CFG-13 · MAY · Diff-only config files with reasons
Ship a bundled "standard"; user/project files store only overrides, each annotated with why
(`# @app:why …`); flag redundant values. Schema scopes (`global-only`, `project-only`, `secret`) so a
committed project file can't set machine or secret keys (forgent).

### CFG-14 · SHOULD · Dangerous overrides are loud
Binding to non-loopback, disabling auth, insecure defaults → print a security notice. Never ship a
fixed default token.

id_prefix: DOC
title: Doctor / diagnostics / setup
applies_when: always (any tool with config, integrations, services or external deps)
---

# Doctor (`<bin> doctor`)

### DOC-01 · MUST · Read-only by default
`doctor` diagnoses only — never creates or modifies files (open DBs read-only). Changes only with
`--fix`. Non-TTY never prompts.

### DOC-02 · MUST · CLI surface and exit codes
`doctor [--fix [--dry-run]] [--json] [--strict|--check] [--verbose]`.
Exit `0` healthy (or only warnings), `1` problems remain, `2` invalid invocation. Doctor that always
exits 0 is useless in CI.

### DOC-03 · MUST · Check model
Each check: stable `code` (e.g. `config_missing`, `client_entry_outdated`), `status`
(`ok|warn|fail|skip|info`), `critical` bool, human `detail`, `fix` hint (exact command) and optional
automatic fix action. JSON output is a stable, documented schema.

### DOC-04 · MUST · `--fix` then re-check
Apply fixes, re-run all checks (loop ≤ N rounds), exit code reflects **post-fix** state. Report each
change (`FIXED +`).

### DOC-05 · SHOULD · Pluggable check registry
`registerCheck` / `registerFix` / `RegisterProvider` so each module owns its checks. Run each check
panic/exception-safe with a timeout.

### DOC-06 · SHOULD · Standard check catalogue
- binary on PATH and is the one being run; version (+ newer available?)
- config present & valid; paths writable; secret file permissions
- data schema version (read-only)
- running daemon/service: registered, running, **live version == binary version**
- external dependencies present with min versions (git, node, runtime CLIs)
- network endpoints reachable (without sending secrets unasked)
- agent integration: skill/instruction block/MCP entry/hooks present and **in sync** (byte-exact with
  embedded template) — and **actually executes** (run hook with harmless input + timeout)
- only check/configure third-party tools that are installed (else `skip`)
- leftovers: legacy files, `.old`/`.bak` binaries, legacy dirs

### DOC-07 · SHOULD · Guided fixes in TTY
Interactive mode offers fixes one by one; `--yes` applies all; never auto-sends credentials to remote
services — print the command instead.

### DOC-08 · SHOULD · `status` = fast subset ending with exactly one next command

### DOC-09 · SHOULD · `setup` / `init` is fill-only and idempotent
Creates only what's missing, never overwrites customisation, reports exactly what changed or "nothing
to do". Works from worktrees (resolve main checkout when relevant).

### DOC-10 · MAY · `--after-update` hidden mode
Invoked by the updater via the new binary to refresh templates/skills that already exist.

---
id_prefix: INS
title: Install scripts (install.sh / install.ps1)
applies_when: always (binary distributed outside a package manager)
---

# Install scripts

Reference implementation: `templates/install.sh` (POSIX sh skeleton applying these rules).

### INS-01 · MUST · One-liners for each OS family
`curl -fsSL <url>/install.sh | sh` and `irm <url>/install.ps1 | iex`. Prefer the URL
`https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/latest/download/install.sh` (version-stamped, REL-08) over raw `main`.

### INS-02 · MUST · Truncation-safe script structure
POSIX `sh` (not bash-only unless you require bash), `set -eu`, everything inside functions,
**`main "$@"` as the very last line** so a cut-off download can't execute a partial script.

### INS-03 · MUST · Platform detection with allow-list
`uname -s`/`uname -m` → mapped through the single naming rule (REL-02). Windows: check
`PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` before `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` (32-bit shell on 64-bit OS). Unsupported →
error that names the fallback (`cargo install --git …`, `go install …`, build-from-source doc).
Redirect Windows shells (MSYS/Cygwin) to `install.ps1`.

### INS-04 · MUST · Every knob is both env var and flag, all prefixed
`<APP>_VERSION`, `<APP>_INSTALL_DIR` (or `PREFIX`), `<APP>_RELEASE_BASE` / `ASSET_BASE_URL`
(mirror, air-gap, test fixtures — one meaning only!), `<APP>_DRY_RUN`, `<APP>_NO_MODIFY_PATH`,
`<APP>_YES`, `<APP>_UNINSTALL`. Document them in a table.

### INS-05 · MUST · Resolve "latest" without the GitHub API
Use `releases/latest/download/<asset>` or follow the `/releases/latest` redirect
(`curl -w '%{url_effective}'`). No API call → no rate limit, no token.

### INS-06 · MUST · Download to a temp dir, verify, then atomically activate
`mktemp -d` + `trap 'rm -rf …' EXIT INT TERM`; verify checksum (SEC-01), optional signature (SEC-03),
archive shape (SEC-05); **run `<candidate> --version` before activation**; copy to
`<dir>/.<bin>.new.$$` in the **target dir**, `chmod 755`, `mv -f` over target.
- Renaming (not writing in place) avoids "Text file busy" when a daemon runs from the binary.
- Windows: rename the running exe to `.old`, move new in; the binary deletes `.old*` on next start.

### INS-07 · SHOULD · Ownership marker next to the binary
`.<app>-managed` (`<app>-managed-v1\nversion=X`, mode 0600). Refuse to overwrite or uninstall a binary
without it; same-version + marker → no-op (only re-check PATH). The updater uses it too (UPD-02).

### INS-08 · SHOULD · Rollback on post-activation failure
Keep `.rollback` copy; if the activated binary fails `--version`, restore binary + marker.

### INS-09 · MUST · Sensible install dir, no root by default
Default `~/.local/bin` (Unix), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\bin` (Windows). Refuse to run as root unless
`<APP>_ALLOW_ROOT=1`. MAY pick first writable of a candidate list.

### INS-10 · MUST · PATH handling is explicit — choose one policy and document it
- Policy A (conservative): never edit rc files; detect missing PATH entry and print the exact
  `export PATH=…` / `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(...)` line.
- Policy B (convenient): write a **fenced** block `# >>> <app> >>>` … `# <<< <app> <<<` into the right
  rc files (`.bashrc`, `.bash_profile` on macOS, `${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zshrc`,
  `~/.config/fish/conf.d/<app>.fish`, fallback `.profile`); skip read-only files; `--no-modify-path`
  opt-out; uninstall removes the blocks. Windows: `HKCU\Environment` preserving `REG_EXPAND_SZ`
  and broadcast `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`.

### INS-11 · SHOULD · Network fallbacks are precise
Missing asset (HTTP 404) → MAY fall back to source build; **any other error → hard fail** (never hide a
network problem behind a 10-minute compile). Support `curl` and `wget`.

### INS-12 · MUST · Installer and binary agree on every path
If the installer creates config/state (default config, tokens, service files), the paths come from the
binary (`<bin> paths --json` or `--internal-print-default-config`), or a comment "MUST match
src/…" plus a contract test.

### INS-13 · SHOULD · Bootstrap through the binary, not the script
After placing the binary, delegate everything else (default config, secrets, service, agent
integration) to the binary (`<bin> setup` / `doctor --fix`) so logic exists once, in tested code.
The script stays small and rarely changes.

### INS-14 · MUST · Finish with verification and next steps
Run `<bin> --version`, then print 1–3 "Next:" commands (`<bin> init`, `<bin> doctor --fix`).
Print secrets (generated tokens) only on first creation.

### INS-15 · SHOULD · Testable offline
`--local-fixture DIR` (and a fake signature verifier env) lets CI run the full lifecycle — install,
upgrade, idempotent re-run, rollback, refuse unmanaged, size caps, uninstall — without network.

### INS-16 · MAY · Preflight before touching anything
If the install registers a service, check the service manager is reachable first
(`systemctl --user show-environment`, `launchctl` exists).

---
id_prefix: UPD
title: Self-update
applies_when: binary distributed via GitHub Releases / direct download (skip if only via package manager)
---

# Self-update (`<bin> update`)

### UPD-01 · MUST · CLI surface
`<bin> update [--check] [--version vX.Y.Z] [--force] [--json] [--yes]`.
`--check` exits non-zero (e.g. 10) when an update is available, for scripts.

### UPD-02 · MUST · Only update what we installed
Refuse when the binary is managed by a package manager (brew, scoop, npm, cargo) or lacks the
ownership marker (INS-07); print the right command instead (`brew upgrade <app>`, the one-liner).

### UPD-03 · MUST · Same verification as the installer
Same naming rule, same checksum/signature/size-cap/extraction checks (ideally the installer and the
updater share constants generated from one place — PRN-01). Honest result text: say whether the
signature was checked.

### UPD-04 · MUST · Update source from build metadata
Repo URL comes from build metadata (`CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`, ldflags, package.json `repository`) — forks
update from themselves. Overridable base URL env for tests/mirrors.

### UPD-05 · MUST · Version policy is a pure, unit-tested function
`latest` never downgrades; explicit `--version` may; `--force` reinstalls same version only; `dev`
builds read the marker version. Fetch latest **once** and use that same resolved release for compare
and download (no race).

### UPD-06 · MUST · Download matches the release format
If releases are archives, extract (safely) before swapping. Test the updater against **real release
assets** in CI (herdr-go wrote the .tar.gz over the binary).

### UPD-07 · MUST · Stage → smoke → swap → rollback
Stage next to the real binary (resolve symlinks; same filesystem) → run `<staged> --version` and require
the exact target version (with timeout) → back up → atomic rename (Windows: rename running exe to
`.old-<pid>`) → on any failure restore. Clean `.old*` / `.bak-*` leftovers on next start (cap retained
backups).

### UPD-08 · SHOULD · Post-swap work runs in the NEW binary
Spawn the new binary by path for migrations and template refreshes (`<new> doctor --after-update`,
`<new> --internal-merge-config <path>`): the running process still holds old embedded defaults.

### UPD-09 · SHOULD · Services: stop → swap → migrate → start → health → auto-rollback
For daemons: poll a health endpoint (version must equal target); if unhealthy, restore binary **and**
config and restart the old one. Running daemon older than CLI → auto-restart (ask the live process its
version; never downgrade).

### UPD-10 · SHOULD · sudo-aware
Under sudo/root, skip user-scoped steps (daemon, skills, agent configs) and print what to run as the user.

### UPD-11 · SHOULD · Rate limits handled
Prefer redirect-based latest resolution; if using the API, honour `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `<APP>_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

### UPD-12 · MAY · Update notice
Background, cached (≤ once/day), opt-out (`<APP>_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, auto-off in CI / non-TTY)
"new version available" hint. Prerelease channel flag if you ship prereleases.

### UPD-13 · MAY · Pinned per-project runtime instead of global update
For tools whose behaviour must be identical across a team: tiny global bootstrap + per-project pin
(exact digest committed), `upgrade` / `repair` (rollback) / `verify` (re-hash, quarantine) verbs,
stable shim reading an activation file (forgent `fgctl`).

---
id_prefix: CFG
title: Config, state, secrets & migrations
applies_when: tool has any persistent config, data, cache or secrets
---

# Config, state, secrets & migrations

### CFG-01 · MUST · Separate config / data / state / cache, using OS conventions
| | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| config | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/<app>` | `~/Library/Application Support/<app>` | `%APPDATA%\<app>` |
| data/state | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/<app>` (or `XDG_DATA_HOME`) | same as config dir | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>` |
| cache | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/<app>` | `~/Library/Caches/<app>` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\cache` |
Honour XDG vars only when absolute. A single `~/.<app>/` is acceptable for simple tools but provide
the override below.

### CFG-02 · MUST · One override env var per root, one meaning each
`<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`, `<APP>_STATE_DIR` (or `<APP>_HOME`). Never reuse one name for two things.
Tests/smoke runs set these so they never touch the real user's files.

### CFG-03 · MUST · `<bin> paths [--json]` (or in `doctor`)
Prints resolved config/state/cache/binary paths. Installers, uninstallers and docs consume this
instead of re-deriving paths (fixes skillstation macOS purge bug class).

### CFG-04 · MUST · Documented precedence
`CLI flag > env var > project config > user config > built-in default`. Print it in `--help` /
`config explain <key>` (shows which layer won).

### CFG-05 · MUST · Zero-config start; defaults come from the binary
Missing file → defaults. The binary can print its default config (`config default` /
`--internal-print-default-config`) — installer, `config init` and update-merge all use it; no separate
`config.example.*` that drifts (or generate it in CI and diff).

### CFG-06 · MUST · Atomic writes preserving mode; secrets 0600
Temp in same dir → fsync → rename → (dir fsync). Keep the existing file's permissions (never widen a
0600 file). Config dir 0700 when it holds anything sensitive.

### CFG-07 · MUST · Secrets are not in the main config
Separate file (`<app>.env`, `private/`) with 0600 / owner-only DACL; the binary **refuses** to read a
secret file with loose permissions; env var override (`<APP>_TOKEN`). Service unit files and agent
configs reference the secret **path**, never the value. Generate with a CSPRNG; print once.

### CFG-08 · MUST · Corrupt config = clear error, not silent defaults
Report file, line, problem and fix (`<bin> config edit`, `doctor`). Collect all validation errors at
once. Cap read size.

### CFG-09 · SHOULD · Forward/backward compatible schema
Either preserve unknown keys on rewrite (round-trip raw map) **or** `deny_unknown_fields` with clear
errors — choose consciously: preserve for user-edited files shared across versions; deny for
security-sensitive config. Support renamed keys via aliases.

### CFG-10 · SHOULD · Upgrades merge new defaults without touching user values
Add-missing-keys-only merge, back up first, validate before writing, executed by the **new** binary
(UPD-08).

### CFG-11 · SHOULD · Versioned migrations for data
Numbered migrations (`migration/v3..v7`), `<bin> maintain migrate`; or version in the filename
(`registry-v4.db`) so old and new binaries coexist during upgrade, doctor cleans legacy. Legacy
directory migration fails closed if both old and new exist.

### CFG-12 · SHOULD · Config verbs
`config show | get | set | unset | edit | explain | check | path`. `edit` uses
`$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → `vi`/`notepad`, re-validates after save.

### CFG-13 · MAY · Diff-only config files with reasons
Ship a bundled "standard"; user/project files store only overrides, each annotated with why
(`# @app:why …`); flag redundant values. Schema scopes (`global-only`, `project-only`, `secret`) so a
committed project file can't set machine or secret keys (forgent).

### CFG-14 · SHOULD · Dangerous overrides are loud
Binding to non-loopback, disabling auth, insecure defaults → print a security notice. Never ship a
fixed default token.

---
id_prefix: DOC
title: Doctor / diagnostics / setup
applies_when: always (any tool with config, integrations, services or external deps)
---

# Doctor (`<bin> doctor`)

### DOC-01 · MUST · Read-only by default
`doctor` diagnoses only — never creates or modifies files (open DBs read-only). Changes only with
`--fix`. Non-TTY never prompts.

### DOC-02 · MUST · CLI surface and exit codes
`doctor [--fix [--dry-run]] [--json] [--strict|--check] [--verbose]`.
Exit `0` healthy (or only warnings), `1` problems remain, `2` invalid invocation. Doctor that always
exits 0 is useless in CI.

### DOC-03 · MUST · Check model
Each check: stable `code` (e.g. `config_missing`, `client_entry_outdated`), `status`
(`ok|warn|fail|skip|info`), `critical` bool, human `detail`, `fix` hint (exact command) and optional
automatic fix action. JSON output is a stable, documented schema.

### DOC-04 · MUST · `--fix` then re-check
Apply fixes, re-run all checks (loop ≤ N rounds), exit code reflects **post-fix** state. Report each
change (`FIXED +`).

### DOC-05 · SHOULD · Pluggable check registry
`registerCheck` / `registerFix` / `RegisterProvider` so each module owns its checks. Run each check
panic/exception-safe with a timeout.

### DOC-06 · SHOULD · Standard check catalogue
- binary on PATH and is the one being run; version (+ newer available?)
- config present & valid; paths writable; secret file permissions
- data schema version (read-only)
- running daemon/service: registered, running, **live version == binary version**
- external dependencies present with min versions (git, node, runtime CLIs)
- network endpoints reachable (without sending secrets unasked)
- agent integration: skill/instruction block/MCP entry/hooks present and **in sync** (byte-exact with
  embedded template) — and **actually executes** (run hook with harmless input + timeout)
- only check/configure third-party tools that are installed (else `skip`)
- leftovers: legacy files, `.old`/`.bak` binaries, legacy dirs

### DOC-07 · SHOULD · Guided fixes in TTY
Interactive mode offers fixes one by one; `--yes` applies all; never auto-sends credentials to remote
services — print the command instead.

### DOC-08 · SHOULD · `status` = fast subset ending with exactly one next command

### DOC-09 · SHOULD · `setup` / `init` is fill-only and idempotent
Creates only what's missing, never overwrites customisation, reports exactly what changed or "nothing
to do". Works from worktrees (resolve main checkout when relevant).

### DOC-10 · MAY · `--after-update` hidden mode
Invoked by the updater via the new binary to refresh templates/skills that already exist.

id_prefix: UNI
title: Uninstall
applies_when: always
---

# Uninstall

### UNI-01 · MUST · An uninstall path exists and is documented
`<bin> uninstall` (preferred, knows everything it created) and/or `install.sh --uninstall` /
`install.ps1 -Uninstall`. The documented command must actually resolve (no 404 URLs — herdr-go gap).

### UNI-02 · MUST · Exact inverse of install + setup + doctor --fix
Every artifact created by install/setup/fix has a matching removal step: binary, marker, PATH blocks,
service registration, agent skills/MCP entries/hooks/instruction blocks, permissions entries,
symlinks on PATH pointing to the binary.

### UNI-03 · MUST · Plan → confirm → apply
Print the plan; `--dry-run`; non-TTY refuses without `--yes`. Re-read third-party configs at apply time
(they change often, e.g. `~/.claude.json`); timestamped backups before editing.

### UNI-04 · MUST · Remove only what is still exactly ours
Unwire hooks only if the value still equals what we set; remove only fenced blocks / marker-owned
binaries / digest-known files. Report things we won't delete (rc lines we didn't fence, other projects
still containing our block) instead of editing them.

### UNI-05 · MUST · User data kept by default
Config, data, tokens are kept and the output **says so** with their paths. `--purge` (requires `--yes`
after preview) removes them; refuse to delete `/`, `$HOME`, paths with `..`. Paths come from the
binary (CFG-03), not re-derived.

### UNI-06 · SHOULD · Irreversible steps last
Binary and data dir removal run only if all reversible steps succeeded, so the user can fix and re-run.

### UNI-07 · SHOULD · Platform realities
Windows: running exe can't delete itself → hand off to a detached deferred delete. Refuse under sudo
for user-scoped uninstall. Package-manager installs → print `brew uninstall …` etc. (and verify the
package manager actually owns it — npm exits 0 even when nothing was removed).

id_prefix: AGT
title: AI-agent integration (skills, MCP, hooks, instruction blocks, plugins)
applies_when: the tool is meant to be used by coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, …)
---

# AI-agent integration

### AGT-01 · MUST · Integration is installed by the binary, opt-in and reversible
`<bin> connect [--global|-g] [--dry-run]` / `doctor --fix [--mcp]` writes it; `connect --remove` /
`uninstall` reverses it. Only touch hosts that are actually installed (detect first; else `skip`).

### AGT-02 · MUST · Per-host adapter table
For each host: project vs user scope, MCP config file, permissions file, skills dir. E.g.
| Host | Project MCP | User MCP | Permissions | Skills |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `~/.claude.json` | `.claude/settings(.local).json` | `.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | `.codex/config.toml` | `~/.codex/config.toml` | in config | `.agents/skills/` |
| Gemini | `.gemini/settings.json` | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | in config | — |
Keep the table in code **and** docs; gate features on a verified compatibility matrix.

### AGT-03 · MUST · Surgical, safe edits of other tools' config
Plan-then-apply with a preimage digest (compare-and-swap); format-preserving editors (TOML:
`toml_edit`-style; JSON: keep key order/indent); **malformed file → refuse, never overwrite as `{}`**;
backup first; preserve file mode (0600 `~/.claude.json`).

### AGT-04 · MUST · Register absolute paths, never secrets
MCP `command` = absolute path of the current binary (or the stable shim); args only. Pass a token
**file path**, never the token.

### AGT-05 · SHOULD · Managed instruction blocks
`<!-- <app>:START -->…<!-- <app>:END -->` in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: upsert idempotently, write
through symlinks, leave surrounding content alone, in-sync = byte-exact with embedded template
(templates embedded in the binary, LF enforced via `.gitattributes`). Remove block on uninstall; delete
the file only if it contained nothing else.

### AGT-06 · SHOULD · Skills shipped from one canonical source
Canonical skill source in repo → generated per-host wrappers (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`,
plugin dir) → CI/doctor fails on wrapper drift. Embedded in the binary for install.

### AGT-07 · SHOULD · Ownership of installed skill files via known digests
Keep SHA-256 of every version ever shipped; on update: known digest → upgrade silently; unknown →
user-edited, leave alone and report. CI test asserts table covers released bundles. Refresh on update
only if previously installed.

### AGT-08 · SHOULD · Hooks project-local, through a stable entry point
Hooks call a stable path (`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.<app>/bin/<app> hook <kind>` or the absolute
binary) that survives upgrades; fill-only merge preserving user hooks; exact migration of our old hook
commands; doctor executes the hook with harmless input + timeout.

### AGT-09 · SHOULD · MCP server survives upgrades
Make the MCP server a thin proxy that shells out to the CLI per call (or re-execs), so a binary update
applies without client reconnect.

### AGT-10 · SHOULD · Cross-environment reach
WSL → Windows desktop clients via `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e <abs-binary> mcp`, detected with
`WSL_DISTRO_NAME` / `/proc/version`.

### AGT-11 · SHOULD · Plugin / marketplace manifests are thin and versioned
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`, host plugin manifests: thin launchers over the CLI,
expose read-only actions unless control is intended, `min_<host>_version`, version synced by VER-03.

### AGT-12 · MAY · Permissions entry for the CLI
Add a narrow allow rule (`Bash(<app> open:*)`) rather than broad ones; remove on uninstall.

applies_when: the tool runs a long-lived process (server, watcher, gateway)

# Background service / daemon

### SVC-01 · MUST · User-level service per OS, installed by the binary
Linux `systemd --user` unit (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user/<app>.service`, `loginctl enable-linger`
when it must survive logout), macOS LaunchAgent (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/<rdns>.plist`, `launchctl
bootstrap gui/<uid>`), Windows per-user Scheduled Task (`AtLogOn`, `RunLevel Limited`, restart policy).
No root/admin.

### SVC-02 · MUST · `<bin> service install|uninstall|start|stop|restart|status|logs`
Thin pass-through to the native manager; print the native commands for transparency.

### SVC-03 · MUST · Idempotent registration
`bootout` before `bootstrap`; unregister before register; disable conflicting legacy/dev units.

### SVC-04 · MUST · No secrets in unit files
The binary reads its own secret file (CFG-07).

### SVC-05 · SHOULD · Hardening & restart policy
systemd: `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths=<state> <config>`,
`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=3`. launchd: `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`, `ThrottleInterval`.
Windows: `-RestartCount 3 -RestartInterval 1min` (1 min is the minimum).

### SVC-06 · MUST · Safe defaults for network listeners
Bind `127.0.0.1` by default, random/generated auth token, loud notice for non-loopback binds.

### SVC-07 · SHOULD · Version handshake
Health endpoint returns the build fingerprint (VER-04). CLI detects an older running daemon and
restarts it; never downgrades. Lock files are hints — ask the live process.

### SVC-08 · SHOULD · Survive binary replacement
On Linux `current_exe()` may end with ` (deleted)` after a swap — strip it before re-spawning.

### SVC-09 · MAY · Separate dev service
`dev-deploy.sh` installs `<app>-dev.service` from a template with placeholders, stopping prod — never
hand-edit the prod unit while developing.

applies_when: always

# Testing the distribution

### TST-01 · MUST · Consumer proof before publish
CI installs from the **built assets** outside the checkout (sh, PowerShell 5.1 and 7), with a local
fixture / `ASSET_BASE_URL` pointing at the build output.

### TST-02 · MUST · Post-publish smoke on every OS (against draft if possible)
Literal one-liner → `<bin> --version` in a **new login shell** (`bash -l -c`, proves PATH) → basic
command / `doctor --strict` → service start + health (if any) → uninstall → command gone.

### TST-03 · MUST · Upgrade-from-previous test
Install the previous stable tag (resolved dynamically, never hard-coded), run `<bin> update`, assert
the reported version/fingerprint changed and config survived.

### TST-04 · SHOULD · Offline installer lifecycle tests
Via `--local-fixture`: install, idempotent re-run, upgrade, rollback on broken candidate, refuse
unmanaged binary, checksum mismatch, size cap, signature matrix, uninstall, purge guards.

### TST-05 · SHOULD · Static contract test
A script cross-checks: asset names in workflow == installer == updater == docs; paths in installer ==
binary; README links resolve; packaged doc files exist; retired names are gone. **Wired into CI.**

### TST-06 · SHOULD · Unit tests for pure policies
Version compare / downgrade policy, platform → asset mapping (asserted against the release naming
rule), config precedence, merge, path resolution per OS (driveable for any OS).

### TST-07 · SHOULD · Isolation
Tests set `<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`/`STATE_DIR`/`HOME` to temp dirs; never touch the real user.

# Docs & CLI UX

### UX-01 · MUST · README "Install" section
Per-OS one-liner; supported platforms + what's not; pin example (`<APP>_VERSION=vX`); prerelease note;
fallback (build from source); then short **Upgrade**, **Uninstall**, **Doctor**, **Configuration**
subsections linking to `docs/installation.md`.

### UX-02 · MUST · `docs/installation.md`
Env-var table (name, flag, default, purpose), "where things live" table per OS (from CFG-03),
signature verification commands, upgrade, uninstall/purge, troubleshooting (SmartScreen, Gatekeeper,
PATH, glibc too old).

### UX-03 · SHOULD · `docs/release-runbook.md`
How to cut a release, verify signatures/attestations manually, roll back / yank a bad release.

### UX-04 · MUST · Errors: Error / Why / Fix
Same structure in human and `--json` output; fix is a copy-pasteable command.

### UX-05 · SHOULD · Next-step guidance
Installer, `init`, `status` end with 1–3 concrete "Next:" commands. `--help` is task-ordered
("Get started: 1. 2. 3.").

### UX-06 · SHOULD · `--json` everywhere with schemas
Machine output for `version`, `status`, `doctor`, `update --check`, `paths`, `config show`; JSON
schemas in `schemas/`.

### UX-07 · SHOULD · Shell completions & man page
`<bin> completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>`; ship them in archives and package-manager formulas.
(None of the studied projects did this — a common gap.)

### UX-08 · SHOULD · Renames are migrations, not breaks
If the product/binary is renamed: keep the old name as an alias/shim for a deprecation window,
auto-migrate dirs/env vars/agent entries, fail closed if both exist.

### UX-09 · SHOULD · Shipped docs free of internal jargon
No ticket ids or internal decision codes in user-facing text; specs may cite decisions.

id_prefix: UNI
title: Uninstall
applies_when: always
---

# Uninstall

### UNI-01 · MUST · An uninstall path exists and is documented
`<bin> uninstall` (preferred, knows everything it created) and/or `install.sh --uninstall` /
`install.ps1 -Uninstall`. The documented command must actually resolve (no 404 URLs — herdr-go gap).

### UNI-02 · MUST · Exact inverse of install + setup + doctor --fix
Every artifact created by install/setup/fix has a matching removal step: binary, marker, PATH blocks,
service registration, agent skills/MCP entries/hooks/instruction blocks, permissions entries,
symlinks on PATH pointing to the binary.

### UNI-03 · MUST · Plan → confirm → apply
Print the plan; `--dry-run`; non-TTY refuses without `--yes`. Re-read third-party configs at apply time
(they change often, e.g. `~/.claude.json`); timestamped backups before editing.

### UNI-04 · MUST · Remove only what is still exactly ours
Unwire hooks only if the value still equals what we set; remove only fenced blocks / marker-owned
binaries / digest-known files. Report things we won't delete (rc lines we didn't fence, other projects
still containing our block) instead of editing them.

### UNI-05 · MUST · User data kept by default
Config, data, tokens are kept and the output **says so** with their paths. `--purge` (requires `--yes`
after preview) removes them; refuse to delete `/`, `$HOME`, paths with `..`. Paths come from the
binary (CFG-03), not re-derived.

### UNI-06 · SHOULD · Irreversible steps last
Binary and data dir removal run only if all reversible steps succeeded, so the user can fix and re-run.

### UNI-07 · SHOULD · Platform realities
Windows: running exe can't delete itself → hand off to a detached deferred delete. Refuse under sudo
for user-scoped uninstall. Package-manager installs → print `brew uninstall …` etc. (and verify the
package manager actually owns it — npm exits 0 even when nothing was removed).

plugin dir) → CI/doctor fails on wrapper drift. Embedded in the binary for install.

### AGT-07 · SHOULD · Ownership of installed skill files via known digests
Keep SHA-256 of every version ever shipped; on update: known digest → upgrade silently; unknown →
user-edited, leave alone and report. CI test asserts table covers released bundles. Refresh on update
only if previously installed.

### AGT-08 · SHOULD · Hooks project-local, through a stable entry point
Hooks call a stable path (`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.<app>/bin/<app> hook <kind>` or the absolute
binary) that survives upgrades; fill-only merge preserving user hooks; exact migration of our old hook
commands; doctor executes the hook with harmless input + timeout.

### AGT-09 · SHOULD · MCP server survives upgrades
Make the MCP server a thin proxy that shells out to the CLI per call (or re-execs), so a binary update
applies without client reconnect.

### AGT-10 · SHOULD · Cross-environment reach
WSL → Windows desktop clients via `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e <abs-binary> mcp`, detected with
`WSL_DISTRO_NAME` / `/proc/version`.

### AGT-11 · SHOULD · Plugin / marketplace manifests are thin and versioned
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`, host plugin manifests: thin launchers over the CLI,
expose read-only actions unless control is intended, `min_<host>_version`, version synced by VER-03.

### AGT-12 · MAY · Permissions entry for the CLI
Add a narrow allow rule (`Bash(<app> open:*)`) rather than broad ones; remove on uninstall.

---
id_prefix: SVC
title: Background service / daemon
applies_when: the tool runs a long-lived process (server, watcher, gateway)
---

# Background service / daemon

### SVC-01 · MUST · User-level service per OS, installed by the binary
Linux `systemd --user` unit (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user/<app>.service`, `loginctl enable-linger`
when it must survive logout), macOS LaunchAgent (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/<rdns>.plist`, `launchctl
bootstrap gui/<uid>`), Windows per-user Scheduled Task (`AtLogOn`, `RunLevel Limited`, restart policy).
No root/admin.

### SVC-02 · MUST · `<bin> service install|uninstall|start|stop|restart|status|logs`
Thin pass-through to the native manager; print the native commands for transparency.

### SVC-03 · MUST · Idempotent registration
`bootout` before `bootstrap`; unregister before register; disable conflicting legacy/dev units.

### SVC-04 · MUST · No secrets in unit files
The binary reads its own secret file (CFG-07).

### SVC-05 · SHOULD · Hardening & restart policy
systemd: `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths=<state> <config>`,
`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=3`. launchd: `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`, `ThrottleInterval`.
Windows: `-RestartCount 3 -RestartInterval 1min` (1 min is the minimum).

### SVC-06 · MUST · Safe defaults for network listeners
Bind `127.0.0.1` by default, random/generated auth token, loud notice for non-loopback binds.

### SVC-07 · SHOULD · Version handshake
Health endpoint returns the build fingerprint (VER-04). CLI detects an older running daemon and
restarts it; never downgrades. Lock files are hints — ask the live process.

### SVC-08 · SHOULD · Survive binary replacement
On Linux `current_exe()` may end with ` (deleted)` after a swap — strip it before re-spawning.

### SVC-09 · MAY · Separate dev service
`dev-deploy.sh` installs `<app>-dev.service` from a template with placeholders, stopping prod — never
hand-edit the prod unit while developing.

---
id_prefix: TST
title: Testing the distribution
applies_when: always
---

# Testing the distribution

### TST-01 · MUST · Consumer proof before publish
CI installs from the **built assets** outside the checkout (sh, PowerShell 5.1 and 7), with a local
fixture / `ASSET_BASE_URL` pointing at the build output.

### TST-02 · MUST · Post-publish smoke on every OS (against draft if possible)
Literal one-liner → `<bin> --version` in a **new login shell** (`bash -l -c`, proves PATH) → basic
command / `doctor --strict` → service start + health (if any) → uninstall → command gone.

### TST-03 · MUST · Upgrade-from-previous test
Install the previous stable tag (resolved dynamically, never hard-coded), run `<bin> update`, assert
the reported version/fingerprint changed and config survived.

### TST-04 · SHOULD · Offline installer lifecycle tests
Via `--local-fixture`: install, idempotent re-run, upgrade, rollback on broken candidate, refuse
unmanaged binary, checksum mismatch, size cap, signature matrix, uninstall, purge guards.

### TST-05 · SHOULD · Static contract test
A script cross-checks: asset names in workflow == installer == updater == docs; paths in installer ==
binary; README links resolve; packaged doc files exist; retired names are gone. **Wired into CI.**

### TST-06 · SHOULD · Unit tests for pure policies
Version compare / downgrade policy, platform → asset mapping (asserted against the release naming
rule), config precedence, merge, path resolution per OS (driveable for any OS).

### TST-07 · SHOULD · Isolation
Tests set `<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`/`STATE_DIR`/`HOME` to temp dirs; never touch the real user.

---
id_prefix: UX
title: Docs & CLI UX for distribution
applies_when: always
---

# Docs & CLI UX

### UX-01 · MUST · README "Install" section
Per-OS one-liner; supported platforms + what's not; pin example (`<APP>_VERSION=vX`); prerelease note;
fallback (build from source); then short **Upgrade**, **Uninstall**, **Doctor**, **Configuration**
subsections linking to `docs/installation.md`.

### UX-02 · MUST · `docs/installation.md`
Env-var table (name, flag, default, purpose), "where things live" table per OS (from CFG-03),
signature verification commands, upgrade, uninstall/purge, troubleshooting (SmartScreen, Gatekeeper,
PATH, glibc too old).

### UX-03 · SHOULD · `docs/release-runbook.md`
How to cut a release, verify signatures/attestations manually, roll back / yank a bad release.

### UX-04 · MUST · Errors: Error / Why / Fix
Same structure in human and `--json` output; fix is a copy-pasteable command.

### UX-05 · SHOULD · Next-step guidance
Installer, `init`, `status` end with 1–3 concrete "Next:" commands. `--help` is task-ordered
("Get started: 1. 2. 3.").

### UX-06 · SHOULD · `--json` everywhere with schemas
Machine output for `version`, `status`, `doctor`, `update --check`, `paths`, `config show`; JSON
schemas in `schemas/`.

### UX-07 · SHOULD · Shell completions & man page
`<bin> completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>`; ship them in archives and package-manager formulas.
(None of the studied projects did this — a common gap.)

### UX-08 · SHOULD · Renames are migrations, not breaks
If the product/binary is renamed: keep the old name as an alias/shim for a deprecation window,
auto-migrate dirs/env vars/agent entries, fail closed if both exist.

### UX-09 · SHOULD · Shipped docs free of internal jargon
No ticket ids or internal decision codes in user-facing text; specs may cite decisions.

# Rust

Rules here **implement** common rules (referenced in brackets) with Rust specifics.

### RS-01 · MUST · Version from Cargo, workspace-wide  [VER-01]
`[workspace.package] version = "X.Y.Z"` + `version.workspace = true` in members. Binary uses
`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`; repo for updates from `env!("CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY")` [UPD-04].
Polyglot: `include_str!("…/package.json")` + parse at build time, or `build.rs` reading the SoT.

### RS-02 · SHOULD · Build fingerprint via `build.rs`  [VER-04]
Emit `cargo:rustc-env=<APP>_FINGERPRINT=X.Y.Z (sha[-dirty], commit-time)`; fall back to `nogit`.
Note: emitting no `rerun-if-*` lines reruns on every package change (fresh dirty flag) at the cost of
rebuilding the build script output; choose deliberately.

### RS-03 · MUST · Release profile  [REL-12]
```toml
[profile.release]
strip = true
lto = "thin"          # or true + codegen-units = 1 for smallest/fastest
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"       # only if you don't rely on unwinding
opt-level = 3         # or "s" for size-sensitive CLIs
```

### RS-04 · MUST · Targets  [REL-01]
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` (via `cross` or `cargo-zigbuild`; static, any
distro), `aarch64-apple-darwin` (`macos-14`), `x86_64-apple-darwin` if needed (cross-compile from
arm runner rather than waiting for scarce Intel runners), `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.
If glibc is unavoidable (napi, some C deps): build on oldest image + glibc ceiling check.
Use `rustls` instead of OpenSSL to keep musl builds simple; `rusqlite` with `bundled`.

### RS-05 · SHOULD · Pin toolchain
`rust-toolchain.toml` with channel + components + targets.

### RS-06 · MUST · Supply-chain gates  [SEC-06]
`cargo deny check advisories bans sources` (or `cargo audit`) in CI; `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` on Linux + Windows.

### RS-07 · SHOULD · Exclude heavy crates from default build
Desktop/GUI crates (Tauri) out of `default-members` so the CLI never needs webview libs.

### RS-08 · SHOULD · Embedded assets  [REL-11]
`include_str!` / `include_bytes!` for templates (skills, instruction blocks) with LF enforced in
`.gitattributes`; `rust-embed` for web UIs with `build.rs` creating the folder; CI asserts
`index.html` is present in release builds.

### RS-09 · SHOULD · Self-update implementation  [UPD-*]
Crates: `self_update` or `self-replace` (handles Windows running-exe), `reqwest` (rustls),
`flate2` + `tar` / `zip` if archives, `sha2`, `semver`. Resolve `current_exe()` → `canonicalize`;
stage in the same directory; `std::fs::rename`. Strip Linux ` (deleted)` suffix before re-spawn
[SVC-08]. Clean `.old-*` at start of `main`.

### RS-10 · SHOULD · Config  [CFG-*]
`directories` / `etcetera` / `dirs` for OS paths; `serde` with `#[serde(default)]`, `#[serde(alias)]`,
or `deny_unknown_fields` (choose per CFG-09); `toml_edit` for comment-preserving edits of TOML (own and
third-party, e.g. Codex `~/.codex/config.toml`); `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist` for atomic writes;
keep permissions via `std::fs::set_permissions` from old metadata.

### RS-11 · SHOULD · CLI  [UX-07]
`clap` derive; `clap_complete` for `completions <shell>`; `clap_mangen` for man page; generate both in
release and ship in archives.

### RS-12 · MAY · Fallback install channel
`cargo install --git <repo> --locked` (or crates.io `cargo install <crate>`; `cargo binstall` metadata
`[package.metadata.binstall]` pointing at release assets). Installer falls back to it only on 404
[INS-11]; mind `--root` puts binaries in `<root>/bin`.

### RS-13 · MAY · Reproducibility
`--remap-path-prefix`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`; Windows `-C link-arg=/Brepro`.

---
id_prefix: GO
language: go
title: Go-specific packaging & distribution
detect: go.mod
sources: [skillstation]
---

# Go

### GO-01 · MUST · Version via ldflags  [VER-01, VER-04]
```
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false \
  -ldflags "-s -w -X <mod>/internal/version.Version=$VERSION \
            -X <mod>/internal/version.Commit=$SHA \
            -X <mod>/internal/version.Date=$(git show -s --format=%cI HEAD) \
            -X <mod>/internal/version.Dirty=$DIRTY"
```
Package defaults `dev` / `none` / `unknown`. Fallback to `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` for `go install`
builds. SoT = git tag (validated SemVer in the workflow, with a self-tested validator).

### GO-02 · MUST · Static, cross-compiled  [REL-01]
`CGO_ENABLED=0`; pure-Go deps (`modernc.org/sqlite`, `go-git`). Matrix `GOOS ∈ {linux,darwin,windows}`
× `GOARCH ∈ {amd64,arm64}` from a single Linux runner.

### GO-03 · SHOULD · Use goreleaser — or one generated list
goreleaser handles archives, checksums, SBOM (syft), cosign, Homebrew tap, Scoop, nfpm (deb/rpm)
from one config, avoiding the "asset list repeated 3× in YAML" problem. If you hand-roll, generate the
asset list from one matrix definition.

### GO-04 · MUST · Quality gates  [SEC-06, REL-03]
`gofmt`/`go vet` (also `GOOS=windows go vet`), `golangci-lint` (new issues vs `origin/main`),
`deadcode`, `govulncheck`, `go test -race`, fuzz targets for parsers.

### GO-05 · SHOULD · Deterministic archives  [REL-09]
`tar --sort=name --mtime=@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --owner=0 --numeric-owner --pax-option=delete=atime,delete=ctime | gzip -n`;
zip with fixed timestamps and `external_attr = 0o100755<<16`. (goreleaser `mod_timestamp`.)

### GO-06 · SHOULD · Paths  [CFG-01]
`os.UserConfigDir()` = `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS (not `~/.config`) — installers and
docs must use the same value (skillstation purge bug). Honour `XDG_STATE_HOME` only if absolute.
Expose `<bin> paths --json`.

### GO-07 · SHOULD · Self-update  [UPD-*]
Use `github.com/minio/selfupdate` or `creativeprojects/go-selfupdate`, or hand-roll: follow
`/releases/latest` redirect manually (≤5 hops, `CheckRedirect` returning `http.ErrUseLastResponse`),
`io.LimitReader` byte caps, `archive/tar` with header type checks, `os.Rename`; Windows rename running
exe to `.old` and delete on next start.

### GO-08 · SHOULD · Config round-trip
Preserve unknown keys by decoding into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and re-encoding [CFG-09];
`os.WriteFile` to temp + `os.Rename`, `0600` files in `0700` dir.

### GO-09 · SHOULD · Embedding  [REL-11]
`//go:embed` for web UI (`web/dist`) and skill templates; CI builds the UI before `go build`; a
placeholder `dist/.keep` lets `go build` succeed without Node in dev, CI asserts real bundle in release.

### GO-10 · SHOULD · CLI  [UX-07]
cobra (built-in `completion` command) or a hand-written dispatcher + explicit `completions` command.
Typed errors `{Summary, Why, Fix}` rendered for human and `--json`.

### GO-11 · MAY · `go install` channel
Works only if `main` package path is stable and version falls back to `ReadBuildInfo`.

# Node.js / TypeScript

Two cases: (a) the product **is** a Node CLI; (b) Node is only a build tool for an embedded web UI
(then see REL-11 and the host language guide).

### NODE-01 · MUST · Version SoT = `package.json`  [VER-01]
Read at runtime via `createRequire(import.meta.url)('../package.json').version` or injected at bundle
time. `npm version` / release script updates `package.json` + `package-lock.json` together.

### NODE-02 · MUST · Choose the channel deliberately
- npm registry (`npm i -g <pkg>`, `npx <pkg>`) — best for Node CLIs; use `files` allow-list,
  `engines.node`, `bin` entries with `#!/usr/bin/env node`; `npm publish --provenance` from CI.
- npm-from-GitHub (`npm i -g github:o/r#vX`) — no registry, but runs `prepare` on user machines;
  treat as legacy/compat only.
- Single binary (`bun build --compile`, Node SEA, `pkg`) — then follow the common install/update rules
  like a compiled language.
Don't keep two primary channels; mark one as legacy in README (forgent gap).

### NODE-03 · MUST · No surprising install scripts
Avoid `postinstall` that downloads or writes outside the package; if needed (native binary), verify
checksums and support `--ignore-scripts` with a clear fallback. Prefer optionalDependencies per
platform (`@scope/pkg-linux-x64`) for native addons.

### NODE-04 · MUST · Engines & runtime check  [DOC-06]
`engines.node` in package.json + a doctor check (`node-version`) with fix hint.

### NODE-05 · SHOULD · Native addons (napi)
Prebuilt per target, loaded with a clear error naming the missing target; glibc ceiling [REL-01];
reproducibility check by independent rebuild (forgent).

### NODE-06 · SHOULD · Uninstall verifies ownership  [UNI-07]
Before `npm uninstall -g <pkg>`, check `npm root -g` actually contains it (npm exits 0 even if nothing
was removed).

### NODE-07 · SHOULD · Quality gates
`npm ci` (lockfile enforced), `npm audit --omit=dev`, typecheck, tests, `npm pack --dry-run` content
check in CI.

### NODE-08 · SHOULD · Front-end bundles for embedding
Vite/esbuild with deterministic output dir consumed by the host language embed; pin Node version
(`.nvmrc` / `engines`) in CI; either commit the bundle or have CI build it before the host build
(and fail if empty).

### NODE-09 · MAY · Shell completions
`omelette` / `tabtab`, or generate static scripts from the command definition.

# Polyglot products

Load this **in addition to** each language guide involved.

### POLY-01 · MUST · Exactly one version SoT, others derived  [VER-01]
Pick one manifest; others use workspace inheritance or are rewritten by the release script; the
compiled language embeds the SoT file (`include_str!`, `//go:embed`) so it cannot disagree.

### POLY-02 · MUST · Drift test in the normal test suite
e.g. `findVersionDrift(root, version)` must be empty; covers every manifest, lockfile, plugin manifest.
Skip vendored third-party manifests explicitly.

### POLY-03 · MUST · One release-prep script for all ecosystems  [VER-05]
Rewrites all manifests + lockfiles in one pass, rolls CHANGELOG, prints git commands.

### POLY-04 · SHOULD · Shared contracts as data files
Things both runtimes must agree on (doctor rows, config schema, error codes) live in one JSON/YAML
contract consumed by both, with a test on each side.

### POLY-05 · SHOULD · Single owner per concern
E.g. config merge/validation implemented once (Rust), the other runtime goes through a facade/CLI —
never two implementations of the same rule.

### POLY-06 · SHOULD · Release tree with manifest
Ship one archive containing all runtimes' pieces + a `manifest.json` (file digests, modes, required
runtime versions, target) — enables verify/repair (SEC-07).

---
id_prefix: RS
language: rust
title: Rust-specific packaging & distribution
detect: Cargo.toml
sources: [mdview, herdr-go, forgent]
---

# Rust

Rules here **implement** common rules (referenced in brackets) with Rust specifics.

### RS-01 · MUST · Version from Cargo, workspace-wide  [VER-01]
`[workspace.package] version = "X.Y.Z"` + `version.workspace = true` in members. Binary uses
`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`; repo for updates from `env!("CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY")` [UPD-04].
Polyglot: `include_str!("…/package.json")` + parse at build time, or `build.rs` reading the SoT.

### RS-02 · SHOULD · Build fingerprint via `build.rs`  [VER-04]
Emit `cargo:rustc-env=<APP>_FINGERPRINT=X.Y.Z (sha[-dirty], commit-time)`; fall back to `nogit`.
Note: emitting no `rerun-if-*` lines reruns on every package change (fresh dirty flag) at the cost of
rebuilding the build script output; choose deliberately.

### RS-03 · MUST · Release profile  [REL-12]
```toml
[profile.release]
strip = true
lto = "thin"          # or true + codegen-units = 1 for smallest/fastest
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"       # only if you don't rely on unwinding
opt-level = 3         # or "s" for size-sensitive CLIs
```

### RS-04 · MUST · Targets  [REL-01]
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` (via `cross` or `cargo-zigbuild`; static, any
distro), `aarch64-apple-darwin` (`macos-14`), `x86_64-apple-darwin` if needed (cross-compile from
arm runner rather than waiting for scarce Intel runners), `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.
If glibc is unavoidable (napi, some C deps): build on oldest image + glibc ceiling check.
Use `rustls` instead of OpenSSL to keep musl builds simple; `rusqlite` with `bundled`.

### RS-05 · SHOULD · Pin toolchain
`rust-toolchain.toml` with channel + components + targets.

### RS-06 · MUST · Supply-chain gates  [SEC-06]
`cargo deny check advisories bans sources` (or `cargo audit`) in CI; `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` on Linux + Windows.

### RS-07 · SHOULD · Exclude heavy crates from default build
Desktop/GUI crates (Tauri) out of `default-members` so the CLI never needs webview libs.

### RS-08 · SHOULD · Embedded assets  [REL-11]
`include_str!` / `include_bytes!` for templates (skills, instruction blocks) with LF enforced in
`.gitattributes`; `rust-embed` for web UIs with `build.rs` creating the folder; CI asserts
`index.html` is present in release builds.

### RS-09 · SHOULD · Self-update implementation  [UPD-*]
Crates: `self_update` or `self-replace` (handles Windows running-exe), `reqwest` (rustls),
`flate2` + `tar` / `zip` if archives, `sha2`, `semver`. Resolve `current_exe()` → `canonicalize`;
stage in the same directory; `std::fs::rename`. Strip Linux ` (deleted)` suffix before re-spawn
[SVC-08]. Clean `.old-*` at start of `main`.

### RS-10 · SHOULD · Config  [CFG-*]
`directories` / `etcetera` / `dirs` for OS paths; `serde` with `#[serde(default)]`, `#[serde(alias)]`,
or `deny_unknown_fields` (choose per CFG-09); `toml_edit` for comment-preserving edits of TOML (own and
third-party, e.g. Codex `~/.codex/config.toml`); `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist` for atomic writes;
keep permissions via `std::fs::set_permissions` from old metadata.

### RS-11 · SHOULD · CLI  [UX-07]
`clap` derive; `clap_complete` for `completions <shell>`; `clap_mangen` for man page; generate both in
release and ship in archives.

### RS-12 · MAY · Fallback install channel
`cargo install --git <repo> --locked` (or crates.io `cargo install <crate>`; `cargo binstall` metadata
`[package.metadata.binstall]` pointing at release assets). Installer falls back to it only on 404
[INS-11]; mind `--root` puts binaries in `<root>/bin`.

### RS-13 · MAY · Reproducibility
`--remap-path-prefix`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`; Windows `-C link-arg=/Brepro`.

id_prefix: GO
language: go
title: Go-specific packaging & distribution
detect: go.mod
sources: [skillstation]
---

# Go

### GO-01 · MUST · Version via ldflags  [VER-01, VER-04]
```
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false \
  -ldflags "-s -w -X <mod>/internal/version.Version=$VERSION \
            -X <mod>/internal/version.Commit=$SHA \
            -X <mod>/internal/version.Date=$(git show -s --format=%cI HEAD) \
            -X <mod>/internal/version.Dirty=$DIRTY"
```
Package defaults `dev` / `none` / `unknown`. Fallback to `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` for `go install`
builds. SoT = git tag (validated SemVer in the workflow, with a self-tested validator).

### GO-02 · MUST · Static, cross-compiled  [REL-01]
`CGO_ENABLED=0`; pure-Go deps (`modernc.org/sqlite`, `go-git`). Matrix `GOOS ∈ {linux,darwin,windows}`
× `GOARCH ∈ {amd64,arm64}` from a single Linux runner.

### GO-03 · SHOULD · Use goreleaser — or one generated list
goreleaser handles archives, checksums, SBOM (syft), cosign, Homebrew tap, Scoop, nfpm (deb/rpm)
from one config, avoiding the "asset list repeated 3× in YAML" problem. If you hand-roll, generate the
asset list from one matrix definition.

### GO-04 · MUST · Quality gates  [SEC-06, REL-03]
`gofmt`/`go vet` (also `GOOS=windows go vet`), `golangci-lint` (new issues vs `origin/main`),
`deadcode`, `govulncheck`, `go test -race`, fuzz targets for parsers.

### GO-05 · SHOULD · Deterministic archives  [REL-09]
`tar --sort=name --mtime=@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --owner=0 --numeric-owner --pax-option=delete=atime,delete=ctime | gzip -n`;
zip with fixed timestamps and `external_attr = 0o100755<<16`. (goreleaser `mod_timestamp`.)

### GO-06 · SHOULD · Paths  [CFG-01]
`os.UserConfigDir()` = `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS (not `~/.config`) — installers and
docs must use the same value (skillstation purge bug). Honour `XDG_STATE_HOME` only if absolute.
Expose `<bin> paths --json`.

### GO-07 · SHOULD · Self-update  [UPD-*]
Use `github.com/minio/selfupdate` or `creativeprojects/go-selfupdate`, or hand-roll: follow
`/releases/latest` redirect manually (≤5 hops, `CheckRedirect` returning `http.ErrUseLastResponse`),
`io.LimitReader` byte caps, `archive/tar` with header type checks, `os.Rename`; Windows rename running
exe to `.old` and delete on next start.

### GO-08 · SHOULD · Config round-trip
Preserve unknown keys by decoding into `map[string]json.RawMessage` and re-encoding [CFG-09];
`os.WriteFile` to temp + `os.Rename`, `0600` files in `0700` dir.

### GO-09 · SHOULD · Embedding  [REL-11]
`//go:embed` for web UI (`web/dist`) and skill templates; CI builds the UI before `go build`; a
placeholder `dist/.keep` lets `go build` succeed without Node in dev, CI asserts real bundle in release.

### GO-10 · SHOULD · CLI  [UX-07]
cobra (built-in `completion` command) or a hand-written dispatcher + explicit `completions` command.
Typed errors `{Summary, Why, Fix}` rendered for human and `--json`.

### GO-11 · MAY · `go install` channel
Works only if `main` package path is stable and version falls back to `ReadBuildInfo`.
