id_prefix: NODE
language: node / typescript
title: Node.js / TypeScript-specific packaging & distribution
detect: package.json
sources: [forgent (Node layer), mdview/herdr-go/skillstation (embedded web UIs)]
---

# Node.js / TypeScript

Two cases: (a) the product **is** a Node CLI; (b) Node is only a build tool for an embedded web UI
(then see REL-11 and the host language guide).

### NODE-01 · MUST · Version SoT = `package.json`  [VER-01]
Read at runtime via `createRequire(import.meta.url)('../package.json').version` or injected at bundle
time. `npm version` / release script updates `package.json` + `package-lock.json` together.

### NODE-02 · MUST · Choose the channel deliberately
- npm registry (`npm i -g <pkg>`, `npx <pkg>`) — best for Node CLIs; use `files` allow-list,
  `engines.node`, `bin` entries with `#!/usr/bin/env node`; `npm publish --provenance` from CI.
- npm-from-GitHub (`npm i -g github:o/r#vX`) — no registry, but runs `prepare` on user machines;
  treat as legacy/compat only.
- Single binary (`bun build --compile`, Node SEA, `pkg`) — then follow the common install/update rules
  like a compiled language.
Don't keep two primary channels; mark one as legacy in README (forgent gap).

### NODE-03 · MUST · No surprising install scripts
Avoid `postinstall` that downloads or writes outside the package; if needed (native binary), verify
checksums and support `--ignore-scripts` with a clear fallback. Prefer optionalDependencies per
platform (`@scope/pkg-linux-x64`) for native addons.

### NODE-04 · MUST · Engines & runtime check  [DOC-06]
`engines.node` in package.json + a doctor check (`node-version`) with fix hint.

### NODE-05 · SHOULD · Native addons (napi)
Prebuilt per target, loaded with a clear error naming the missing target; glibc ceiling [REL-01];
reproducibility check by independent rebuild (forgent).

### NODE-06 · SHOULD · Uninstall verifies ownership  [UNI-07]
Before `npm uninstall -g <pkg>`, check `npm root -g` actually contains it (npm exits 0 even if nothing
was removed).

### NODE-07 · SHOULD · Quality gates
`npm ci` (lockfile enforced), `npm audit --omit=dev`, typecheck, tests, `npm pack --dry-run` content
check in CI.

### NODE-08 · SHOULD · Front-end bundles for embedding
Vite/esbuild with deterministic output dir consumed by the host language embed; pin Node version
(`.nvmrc` / `engines`) in CI; either commit the bundle or have CI build it before the host build
(and fail if empty).

### NODE-09 · MAY · Shell completions
`omelette` / `tabtab`, or generate static scripts from the command definition.

title: Multi-language products
detect: more than one of Cargo.toml / go.mod / package.json / pyproject.toml at the product level

---

# Polyglot products

Load this **in addition to** each language guide involved.

### POLY-01 · MUST · Exactly one version SoT, others derived  [VER-01]
Pick one manifest; others use workspace inheritance or are rewritten by the release script; the
compiled language embeds the SoT file (`include_str!`, `//go:embed`) so it cannot disagree.

### POLY-02 · MUST · Drift test in the normal test suite
e.g. `findVersionDrift(root, version)` must be empty; covers every manifest, lockfile, plugin manifest.
Skip vendored third-party manifests explicitly.

### POLY-03 · MUST · One release-prep script for all ecosystems  [VER-05]
Rewrites all manifests + lockfiles in one pass, rolls CHANGELOG, prints git commands.

### POLY-04 · SHOULD · Shared contracts as data files
Things both runtimes must agree on (doctor rows, config schema, error codes) live in one JSON/YAML
contract consumed by both, with a test on each side.

### POLY-05 · SHOULD · Single owner per concern
E.g. config merge/validation implemented once (Rust), the other runtime goes through a facade/CLI —
never two implementations of the same rule.

### POLY-06 · SHOULD · Release tree with manifest
Ship one archive containing all runtimes' pieces + a `manifest.json` (file digests, modes, required
runtime versions, target) — enables verify/repair (SEC-07).

#!/bin/sh
# Reference installer skeleton — packaging-distribution-guide (INS-*, SEC-*).
# Replace APP / REPO / naming rule; keep the structure. Everything runs from main() on the LAST line.
# Usage: curl -fsSL https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
#        sh install.sh [--version vX.Y.Z] [--install-dir DIR] [--dry-run] [--no-modify-path] [--uninstall] [--yes]
set -eu

APP="myapp"
REPO="OWNER/REPO"
DEFAULT_VERSION='@APP_VERSION@'   # stamped by the release workflow (REL-08)
MARKER=".${APP}-managed"
MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES=134217728       # 128 MiB (SEC-04)

say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { say "error: $1"; [ -n "${2:-}" ] && say "  why: $2"; [ -n "${3:-}" ] && say "  fix: $3"; exit 1; }

parse_args() {
  VERSION="${MYAPP_VERSION:-$DEFAULT_VERSION}"
  INSTALL_DIR="${MYAPP_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
  BASE="${MYAPP_RELEASE_BASE:-https://github.com/$REPO/releases}"
  DRY_RUN="${MYAPP_DRY_RUN:-0}"; NO_PATH="${MYAPP_NO_MODIFY_PATH:-0}"
  UNINSTALL="${MYAPP_UNINSTALL:-0}"; YES="${MYAPP_YES:-0}"
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --version) VERSION="$2"; shift ;;
      --install-dir) INSTALL_DIR="$2"; shift ;;
      --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
      --no-modify-path) NO_PATH=1 ;;
      --uninstall) UNINSTALL=1 ;;
      --yes|-y) YES=1 ;;
      *) die "unknown option $1" "" "sh install.sh --help" ;;
    esac; shift
  done
  case "$VERSION" in @*@) die "unstamped installer" "this copy was not produced by a release" "pass --version vX.Y.Z or use the releases/latest/download URL" ;; esac
  case "$BASE" in https://*) ;; *) die "non-HTTPS release base: $BASE" ;; esac
  [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] && [ "${MYAPP_ALLOW_ROOT:-0}" != 1 ] && die "refusing to run as root" "installs are per-user" "re-run as your user, or MYAPP_ALLOW_ROOT=1"
  return 0
}

detect_target() {   # single naming rule (REL-02) — keep in sync with release workflow + updater
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux) os=linux ;; Darwin) os=darwin ;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) die "Windows shell detected" "" "irm https://github.com/$REPO/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex" ;;
    *) die "unsupported OS $(uname -s)" "" "build from source: see README" ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64|amd64) arch=amd64 ;; aarch64|arm64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) die "unsupported arch $(uname -m)" "" "build from source: see README" ;;
  esac
  ASSET="${APP}-${VERSION#v}-${os}-${arch}.tar.gz"
}

fetch() {  # url dest  — HTTPS only, wall-clock timeout, size cap (SEC-04)
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 --max-filesize "$MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES" -o "$2" "$1"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 130 wget -q --https-only -O "$2" "$1"
  else die "need curl or wget"; fi
}

sha256() { if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
           elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
           else openssl dgst -sha256 "$1" | awk '{print $NF}'; fi; }

verify() {  # exact filename match, exactly one entry (SEC-01)
  expected="$(awk -v f="$ASSET" '{n=$2; sub(/^\*/,"",n); if (n==f) {print $1; c++}} END{if (c!=1) exit 1}' "$TMP/checksums.txt")" \
    || die "checksum entry for $ASSET missing or duplicated"
  [ "$(sha256 "$TMP/$ASSET")" = "$expected" ] || die "checksum mismatch for $ASSET" "download corrupted or tampered" "retry; report if it persists"
  if command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    : # cosign verify-blob --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json --certificate-identity ".../release.yml@refs/tags/$VERSION" ...
  else
    say "note: checksum verified; signature NOT checked (install cosign or set MYAPP_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=1)"
    [ "${MYAPP_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE:-0}" = 1 ] && die "signature required but cosign not found"
  fi
}

install_bin() {
  members="$(tar -tzf "$TMP/$ASSET")"
  [ "$members" = "$APP" ] || die "unexpected archive layout" "expected exactly one file '$APP'"
  tar -xzf "$TMP/$ASSET" -C "$TMP"
  [ -f "$TMP/$APP" ] && [ ! -L "$TMP/$APP" ] || die "archive member is not a regular file"
  "$TMP/$APP" --version >/dev/null || die "downloaded binary does not run on this machine"
  target="$INSTALL_DIR/$APP"
  if [ -e "$target" ] && [ ! -f "$INSTALL_DIR/$MARKER" ]; then
    die "$target exists and is not managed by this installer" "" "remove it or install elsewhere with --install-dir"
  fi
  [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ] && { say "dry-run: would install $ASSET to $target"; return; }
  mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR"
  [ -f "$target" ] && cp -p "$target" "$target.rollback"
  cp "$TMP/$APP" "$INSTALL_DIR/.$APP.new.$$" && chmod 755 "$INSTALL_DIR/.$APP.new.$$"
  mv -f "$INSTALL_DIR/.$APP.new.$$" "$target"          # rename: no "Text file busy" (INS-06)
  if ! "$target" --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -f "$target.rollback" ] && mv -f "$target.rollback" "$target"; die "activation failed, rolled back"
  fi
  rm -f "$target.rollback"
  umask 077; printf '%s-managed-v1\nversion=%s\n' "$APP" "$VERSION" > "$INSTALL_DIR/$MARKER"
}

path_hint() {   # Policy A: print, don't edit (INS-10). Swap for fenced-block policy if chosen.
  case ":$PATH:" in *":$INSTALL_DIR:"*) ;; *) [ "$NO_PATH" = 1 ] || say "add to PATH:  export PATH=\"$INSTALL_DIR:\$PATH\"" ;; esac
}

uninstall() {
  [ -f "$INSTALL_DIR/$MARKER" ] || die "no managed install found in $INSTALL_DIR"
  say "will remove: $INSTALL_DIR/$APP $INSTALL_DIR/$MARKER"
  say "will keep: config and data (run '$APP uninstall --purge' to remove them)"
  [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ] && return
  [ "$YES" = 1 ] || [ -t 0 ] || die "non-interactive uninstall needs --yes"
  rm -f "$INSTALL_DIR/$APP" "$INSTALL_DIR/$MARKER"
}

main() {
  parse_args "$@"
  if [ "$UNINSTALL" = 1 ]; then uninstall; return; fi
  detect_target
  TMP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT INT TERM
  fetch "$BASE/download/$VERSION/$ASSET" "$TMP/$ASSET"
  fetch "$BASE/download/$VERSION/checksums.txt" "$TMP/checksums.txt"
  verify
  install_bin
  path_hint
  say "installed: $("$INSTALL_DIR/$APP" --version 2>/dev/null || echo "$APP $VERSION")"
  say "Next:  $APP doctor --fix"
}

main "$@"

---
id_prefix: CH-PLUGIN
channel: agent-host plugin / marketplace (Claude Code plugin, herdr plugin, …)
title: Agent-host plugin & marketplace distribution
applies_when: the tool also ships as a plugin inside a host (Claude Code marketplace, herdr, …)
sources: [forgent (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json), herdr-go (herdr-plugin.toml)]
---

# Agent-host plugin & marketplace

### CH-PLUGIN-01 · MUST · Plugin version synced with the product  [VER-03]
`plugin.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml` version is rewritten by the release script and checked by the drift
test / pre-commit hook. (forgent drifted: plugin 1.2.0 vs product 0.2.0.)

### CH-PLUGIN-02 · MUST · Thin launcher over the CLI
The plugin declares actions/skills/commands that call the installed binary; no second implementation.
Binaries come from releases (no build step inside the plugin).

### CH-PLUGIN-03 · SHOULD · Least-privilege actions
Expose read-only actions (`status`, `url`) by default; exclude control actions that would let the host
manage something that supervises the host.

### CH-PLUGIN-04 · SHOULD · Declare compatibility
`min_<host>_version`, supported platforms; doctor checks host version.

### CH-PLUGIN-05 · SHOULD · Skills mirrored from canonical source  [AGT-06]
Plugin `skills/` is generated from the canonical skill source; CI fails on drift.

### CH-PLUGIN-06 · SHOULD · Marketplace manifest lists only shippable plugins
Keep fixtures/dogfood plugins out of the public marketplace (or in a separate one).

name: packaging-distribution-guide
description: Best-practice guide for packaging and distributing a CLI/tool — build & release pipeline (cross-compile, asset naming, checksums, signing, SBOM), install.sh/install.ps1 one-liners, self-update, config/state/secrets locations, doctor diagnostics, uninstall, background service, AI-agent integration (skills, MCP, hooks, plugins) and distribution testing. Use when setting up or auditing release/install/update/config/doctor/uninstall for a new or existing project, or when asked "how should we ship/install/update this".

# Packaging & Distribution Guide

A rule catalogue distilled from real projects (see `case-studies/`). Each rule has a stable id
(`INS-06`), a level (**MUST** / **SHOULD** / **MAY**), the reason, and where it was seen.
Your job with this skill: turn the catalogue into a **concrete, project-specific checklist and plan**,
then (if asked) implement it.

## Layout (discover by listing — never assume a fixed file list)

```
SKILL.md                 this file (workflow only — no rules here)
common/NN-<topic>.md     language-agnostic rules, one topic per file, id prefix in frontmatter
languages/<lang>.md      language overlays; frontmatter `detect:` says when to load
channels/<channel>.md    distribution-channel overlays (package managers, plugin marketplaces…)
case-studies/<proj>.md   evidence: what each source project does well and its gaps
templates/               project-checklist.md (output format), install.sh (reference skeleton)
CONTRIBUTING.md          how to add/modify guides without breaking structure
scripts/lint-guides.sh   validates frontmatter + unique rule ids
```
Files starting with `_` are templates — ignore them when applying the guide.

## Workflow

1. **Profile the target project.** Read its manifests, CI workflows, existing installers, README.
   Record: language(s); product kind (CLI / daemon / library / agent tool); intended channels;
   platforms; whether it has config, secrets, a long-running process, agent integration.
2. **Select guides.**
   - `ls common/` → read `00-principles.md` always; read each other topic file and keep it if its
     frontmatter `applies_when` matches the profile (when in doubt, keep it).
   - `ls languages/` → load every file whose `detect` marker exists in the project
     (+ `polyglot.md` when more than one applies). No overlay for the language? Apply common rules
     only and say so; offer to create one from `languages/_template.md`.
   - `ls channels/` → load channels the project uses or plans to use.
   - Skim the relevant `case-studies/` for concrete examples when designing something non-trivial.
3. **Make the decisions explicit** (top table of `templates/project-checklist.md`): version SoT,
   target matrix, asset format + naming rule, channels, PATH policy, config locations, signing level,
   agent hosts. Ask the owner only for decisions you can't infer; otherwise state the default chosen.
4. **Audit / plan.** For every rule in the selected files assign `done` / `todo` / `gap` /
   `n/a (reason)`. All **MUST** rules must be `done`, `todo`, or justified `n/a`. Order the work:
   VER → REL/SEC → INS → UPD → CFG → DOC → UNI → SVC/AGT → TST → UX.
5. **Write the checklist** into the project (default `docs/packaging-checklist.md`) using the template.
6. **Implement on request**, citing rule ids in commit messages / code comments where it helps
   (`// UPD-07: stage next to binary so rename stays on one filesystem`). Use `templates/install.sh`
   as the starting point for a POSIX installer.
7. **Feed back.** If the project taught something new (a better practice, or a gap worth warning
   about), propose additions following `CONTRIBUTING.md` — new case study, new rule, or new overlay.

## Rule-reading tips
- Language overlay rules reference the common rule they implement (`[UPD-07]`); read both.
- "Seen:"/"sources" point to case studies; "gap" notes are anti-patterns to avoid.
- Precedence when rules seem to conflict: principles (`PRN-*`) > MUST > SHOULD > MAY; a language
  overlay may refine but not weaken a common MUST.

# Extending the guide

The structure is designed so additions never require restructuring: `SKILL.md` contains only the
workflow and discovers content by listing directories and reading frontmatter. **Adding a file never
requires editing SKILL.md.**

## Where does new knowledge go?

| You learned… | Add / edit |
|---|---|
| a practice that applies regardless of language | a new rule in the matching `common/NN-<topic>.md` |
| a whole new topic (e.g. telemetry, licensing, i18n) | new file `common/NN-<topic>.md` with a new `id_prefix` (pick an unused NN to place it in reading order) |
| how a language does something concretely | `languages/<lang>.md` (create from `_template.md` if new) |
| a distribution channel (brew, scoop, winget, npm, PyPI, Docker, deb/rpm, plugin marketplace) | `channels/<channel>.md` from `_template.md` |
| evidence from a project | `case-studies/<project>.md` (copy the frontmatter shape of an existing one) |
| reusable code | `templates/<file>` and reference it from the relevant rule |

## Rule format (mandatory)

```
### <PREFIX>-<NN> · <MUST|SHOULD|MAY> · <imperative title>  [<common ids implemented>]
<1–6 lines: what, why, how; concrete flags/paths/env names>
- Seen: <project> (good) / <project> (counter-example)
```

- **Ids are permanent.** Never renumber or reuse. Append new rules with the next number. To retire a
  rule, keep the heading and mark it `· DEPRECATED · see <new id>`.
- Levels: MUST = shipping without it causes broken installs, security holes or data loss; SHOULD =
  strong default, skip only with a reason; MAY = situational.
- Language/channel overlays must **not restate** common rules — only refine them, and cite the id.
- Keep each file focused on one topic; split when it grows past ~25 rules.

## Frontmatter (mandatory)

- `common/*.md`: `id_prefix`, `title`, `applies_when`
- `languages/*.md`: `id_prefix`, `language`, `title`, `detect`, `sources`
- `channels/*.md`: `id_prefix`, `channel`, `title`, `applies_when`, `sources`
- `case-studies/*.md`: `project`, `language`, `kind`, `channels`, `distilled` (date + version)

## Validate

```
sh scripts/lint-guides.sh
```
Checks frontmatter keys, rule-heading format, and that every rule id is unique across the skill.

## Re-distilling a source project

When a studied project evolves, update its case study (bump `distilled:`), then promote new good ideas
to rules and move fixed gaps out of the "Gaps observed" list.

# Agent-host plugin & marketplace

### CH-PLUGIN-01 · MUST · Plugin version synced with the product  [VER-03]
`plugin.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml` version is rewritten by the release script and checked by the drift
test / pre-commit hook. (forgent drifted: plugin 1.2.0 vs product 0.2.0.)

### CH-PLUGIN-02 · MUST · Thin launcher over the CLI
The plugin declares actions/skills/commands that call the installed binary; no second implementation.
Binaries come from releases (no build step inside the plugin).

### CH-PLUGIN-03 · SHOULD · Least-privilege actions
Expose read-only actions (`status`, `url`) by default; exclude control actions that would let the host
manage something that supervises the host.

### CH-PLUGIN-04 · SHOULD · Declare compatibility
`min_<host>_version`, supported platforms; doctor checks host version.

### CH-PLUGIN-05 · SHOULD · Skills mirrored from canonical source  [AGT-06]
Plugin `skills/` is generated from the canonical skill source; CI fails on drift.

### CH-PLUGIN-06 · SHOULD · Marketplace manifest lists only shippable plugins
Keep fixtures/dogfood plugins out of the public marketplace (or in a separate one).

D=/home/vantt/projects/devops/skills/packaging-distribution-guide; mkdir -p $D/scripts; cat > $D/scripts/lint-guides.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Validate guide structure: frontmatter keys, rule heading format, unique rule ids.
set -eu
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
fail=0
err() { printf 'ERROR %s\n' "$*" >&2; fail=1; }

need_keys() {  # file key...
  f="$1"; shift
  head -1 "$f" | grep -qx -- '---' || { err "$f: missing frontmatter"; return; }
  fm="$(awk 'NR==1{next} /^---$/{exit} {print}' "$f")"
  for k in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$fm" | grep -q "^$k:" || err "$f: frontmatter missing '$k'"; done
}

for f in "$ROOT"/common/*.md; do need_keys "$f" id_prefix title applies_when; done
for f in "$ROOT"/languages/*.md; do case "$(basename "$f")" in _*) continue;; esac; need_keys "$f" id_prefix language title detect sources; done
for f in "$ROOT"/channels/*.md; do case "$(basename "$f")" in _*) continue;; esac; need_keys "$f" id_prefix channel title applies_when sources; done
for f in "$ROOT"/case-studies/*.md; do case "$(basename "$f")" in _*) continue;; esac; need_keys "$f" project language kind channels distilled; done

ids="$(mktemp)"; trap 'rm -f "$ids"' EXIT
for f in "$ROOT"/common/*.md "$ROOT"/languages/*.md "$ROOT"/channels/*.md; do
  case "$(basename "$f")" in _*) continue;; esac
  prefix="$(awk 'NR==1{next} /^---$/{exit} /^id_prefix:/{print $2}' "$f")"
  grep '^### ' "$f" | while IFS= read -r h; do
    if ! printf '%s\n' "$h" | grep -Eq "^### ${prefix}-[0-9]{2} · (MUST|SHOULD|MAY|DEPRECATED) · "; then
      printf 'ERROR %s: bad rule heading: %s\n' "$f" "$h" >&2; echo BAD >> "$ids"
    else
      printf '%s\n' "$h" | sed -E 's/^### ([A-Z-]+-[0-9]{2}).*/\1/' >> "$ids"
    fi
  done
done
grep -q '^BAD$' "$ids" && fail=1
dups="$(grep -v '^BAD$' "$ids" | sort | uniq -d)"
[ -z "$dups" ] || err "duplicate rule ids: $dups"
prefixes="$(for f in "$ROOT"/common/*.md "$ROOT"/languages/*.md "$ROOT"/channels/*.md; do case "$(basename "$f")" in _*) continue;; esac; awk 'NR==1{next} /^---$/{exit} /^id_prefix:/{print $2}' "$f"; done | sort | uniq -d)"
[ -z "$prefixes" ] || err "duplicate id_prefix: $prefixes"

total="$(grep -vc '^BAD$' "$ids" || true)"
[ "$fail" = 0 ] && printf 'OK: %s rules, structure valid\n' "$total"
exit "$fail"
EOF
chmod +x $D/scripts/lint-guides.sh $D/templates/install.sh; sh $D/scripts/lint-guides.sh; sh -n $D/templates/install.sh && echo "install.sh syntax ok"; command -v shellcheck >/dev/null && shellcheck -s sh $D/templates/install.sh $D/scripts/lint-guides.sh | head -30

## Cấu trúc

```
SKILL.md                 chỉ chứa quy trình cho agent, không chứa rule
common/NN-<topic>.md     rule dùng chung cho mọi ngôn ngữ (13 chủ đề)

channels/                agent-host-plugin · _template   (brew/scoop/docker… thêm sau)
case-studies/            mdview · skillstation · herdr-go · forgent (cái hay + lỗi cần tránh)
templates/               project-checklist.md (mẫu kết quả) · install.sh (khung POSIX đã test)
CONTRIBUTING.md          quy tắc mở rộng
scripts/lint-guides.sh   kiểm tra frontmatter, định dạng rule, ID không trùng
```

**Mỗi rule có dạng:** `### INS-06 · MUST · <việc cần làm>  [rule chung liên quan]`, kèm lý do và dự án nào đã làm. Rule trong `languages/` chỉ bổ sung chi tiết cụ thể và trỏ lại ID của rule chung (ví dụ `RS-09 [UPD-*]`), không viết lại.

**Dễ mở rộng:** `SKILL.md` không giữ danh sách file cố định. Agent tự liệt kê thư mục rồi đọc frontmatter (`applies_when`, `detect: Cargo.toml`…) để chọn file phù hợp. Vì vậy:
- Thêm ngôn ngữ mới (Python…): copy `languages/_template.md`.
- Thêm kênh phân phối (Homebrew, Docker…): copy `channels/_template.md`.
- Thêm chủ đề mới: tạo `common/NN-x.md`.
- Thêm dự án đã học: thêm vào `case-studies/`.

Không cần sửa `SKILL.md`. ID rule không bao giờ đánh số lại; rule bỏ đi thì đánh dấu `DEPRECATED`.

**Khi dùng cho dự án mới,** agent sẽ:
1. Xem dự án dùng ngôn ngữ gì và có những thành phần nào.
2. Chọn các file rule phù hợp.
3. Chốt các quyết định chính.
4. Đánh trạng thái từng rule: done / todo / gap / n/a.
5. Ghi kết quả vào `docs/packaging-checklist.md` của dự án.
6. Triển khai nếu bạn yêu cầu.

## Mỗi dự án đóng góp điều hay nhất
- **skillstation:** chuỗi bảo mật bản phát hành tốt nhất. Có ký bằng cosign, SBOM, attestation và kiểm chứng ngay trong workflow. Phiên bản được ghi thẳng vào install.sh lúc release. Có file đánh dấu bản cài do installer quản lý, và bảng mã hash của mọi phiên bản skill từng phát hành.
- **forgent:** mỗi dự án ghim một bản runtime theo hash, nhờ một công cụ cài đặt nhỏ. Một version gốc dùng chung cho Rust và Node. Đóng gói được kiểm tra trên mọi PR, và CI cài thử từ chính các file release.
- **herdr-go:** self-update có kiểm tra sức khỏe và tự rollback. Binary tự sinh config mặc định, và việc gộp config do binary mới thực hiện. Có test cập nhật từ tag trước.
- **mdview:** chạy thử binary mới trước khi thay. Doctor có hai chiều đối xứng với uninstall. Có khối nội dung có đánh dấu trong AGENTS.md. Updater không chạy các bước của user khi đang ở sudo.

## Lỗi phát hiện trong các repo của bạn (tôi chưa sửa gì)
- **herdr-go:** `update` có vẻ ghi nguyên file `.tar.gz` đè lên binary mà không giải nén (`src/update/github.rs`, `rollout.rs`). Đây là kết luận từ đọc code, tôi chưa chạy thử. Lệnh gỡ cài đặt mà installer in ra trên macOS trỏ tới một URL không tồn tại.
- **skillstation:** `install.sh --purge-config` xóa đường dẫn kiểu Linux (`~/.config`), trong khi trên macOS binary lưu config ở `~/Library/Application Support`.
- **mdview:** khi đăng ký MCP, file JSON hỏng bị coi như `{}` rồi bị ghi đè. Doctor luôn trả exit code 0, nên không dùng được trong CI.
- **forgent:** version của plugin là `1.2.0`, lệch với version sản phẩm `0.2.0`.

# Principles (PRN) — every other rule applies one of these

- **PRN-01** MUST · One source of truth per fact (version, asset naming, paths, default config, targets); everything else is generated from it or tested against it. Every bug found in the source projects was drift between two copies.
- **PRN-02** MUST · Fail closed; every error prints Error / Why / Fix (exact next command).
- **PRN-03** MUST · Idempotent: install, setup, `doctor --fix`, update can be re-run; a no-op run says so.
- **PRN-04** MUST · Atomic changes: temp file in same dir → fsync → rename; keep the previous version until the new one is proven; roll back on failure.
- **PRN-05** MUST · Only modify what you provably own (marker file, fenced block, known digest); unknown content is the user's.
- **PRN-06** MUST · Destructive or out-of-own-dir changes: plan → preview (`--dry-run`) → confirm (non-TTY needs `--yes`) → apply.
- **PRN-07** SHOULD · Test what users actually run: the literal one-liner, from release assets, on every OS.
- **PRN-08** SHOULD · `--json` and meaningful exit codes on every user-facing command.
- **PRN-09** SHOULD · Never silently edit dotfiles, PATH, global agent config or services; print the command or write a fenced, removable block.
- **PRN-10** SHOULD · Respect privilege: no user-scoped steps as root/sudo; never widen permissions; secrets 0600.

title: Build & release pipeline
applies_when: compiled artifacts or GitHub Releases
---

# Build & release (REL)

- **REL-01** MUST · Explicit target matrix (typ. linux x64/arm64, darwin arm64, windows x64) + documented unsupported list and fallback. Linux: static (musl / CGO off); if glibc is unavoidable, build on the oldest image and check a glibc ceiling.
- **REL-02** MUST · One asset-naming rule shared by workflow, installer, updater, docs. Choose archive vs bare binary once — installer and updater must handle the same format. Avoid: herdr-go updater writing the .tar.gz over the exe.
- **REL-03** MUST · Release reruns full CI (reusable workflow / `needs:`).
- **REL-04** MUST · A reusable "build assets" workflow runs on every PR (build + package + consumer proof, no upload); the tag workflow calls it then publishes.
- **REL-05** MUST · One packaging script for local dry run, CI and release; no naming/layout logic in YAML.
- **REL-06** MUST · `checksums.txt` written by a final job that `needs:` all builds; includes installers; re-verified; expected asset count asserted.
- **REL-07** SHOULD · Draft → smoke test → publish, so a failing smoke test never leaves a broken public release.
- **REL-08** SHOULD · Stamp the version into release-attached installers (`@VERSION@` → sed); the unstamped repo copy refuses to run without `--version`.
- **REL-09** SHOULD · Reproducible: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, path trimming, deterministic tar/zip, sorted checksums.
- **REL-10** SHOULD · Workflow hardening: `permissions: {}` + per-job grants, actions pinned by SHA, pinned runner images, `fail-fast: false`.
- **REL-11** SHOULD · Embedded web/template assets: clean checkout builds without Node; CI fails if a release ships an empty bundle.
- **REL-12** SHOULD · Release profile tuned (strip, LTO) — see language overlay.

id_prefix: SEC
title: Supply-chain integrity & authenticity
applies_when: anything users download and execute
---

# Supply chain (SEC)

Checksums from the same origin give integrity only; signatures/provenance give authenticity.

- **SEC-01** MUST · Installer **and** updater verify SHA-256, matching the filename exactly (no grep substring), exactly one entry; fallback `sha256sum`→`shasum -a 256`→`openssl`.
- **SEC-02** SHOULD · Keyless cosign bundles + `attest-build-provenance` + SBOM, verified inside the release job (exact `…/release.yml@refs/tags/vX` identity) before upload.
- **SEC-03** SHOULD · Signature check runs when cosign exists, otherwise says "signature NOT checked" and prints the verify command; `<APP>_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=1` makes it mandatory.
- **SEC-04** MUST · Downloads: HTTPS only, connect + wall-clock timeout (wget `--timeout` is idle-only → wrap in `timeout`), per-asset byte cap.
- **SEC-05** MUST · Safe extraction: reject absolute, `..`, drive-letter, symlink, hardlink, device entries; expect an exact layout.
- **SEC-06** SHOULD · Dependency advisories gate the release (cargo deny / govulncheck / npm audit).

id_prefix: PRN
title: Cross-cutting principles
applies_when: always
---

# Principles (PRN) — every other rule applies one of these

- **PRN-01** MUST · One source of truth per fact (version, asset naming, paths, default config, targets); everything else is generated from it or tested against it. Every bug found in the source projects was drift between two copies.
- **PRN-02** MUST · Fail closed; every error prints Error / Why / Fix (exact next command).
- **PRN-03** MUST · Idempotent: install, setup, `doctor --fix`, update can be re-run; a no-op run says so.
- **PRN-04** MUST · Atomic changes: temp file in same dir → fsync → rename; keep the previous version until the new one is proven; roll back on failure.
- **PRN-05** MUST · Only modify what you provably own (marker file, fenced block, known digest); unknown content is the user's.
- **PRN-06** MUST · Destructive or out-of-own-dir changes: plan → preview (`--dry-run`) → confirm (non-TTY needs `--yes`) → apply.
- **PRN-07** SHOULD · Test what users actually run: the literal one-liner, from release assets, on every OS.
- **PRN-08** SHOULD · `--json` and meaningful exit codes on every user-facing command.
- **PRN-09** SHOULD · Never silently edit dotfiles, PATH, global agent config or services; print the command or write a fenced, removable block.
- **PRN-10** SHOULD · Respect privilege: no user-scoped steps as root/sudo; never widen permissions; secrets 0600.

---
id_prefix: VER
title: Versioning & version discipline
applies_when: always
---

# Versioning (VER)

- **VER-01** MUST · One version source (Cargo/package.json/tag), embedded at build time; `--version` reads only that.
- **VER-02** MUST · Release job fails if tag ≠ source version.
- **VER-03** MUST · Every other manifest (plugin.json, herdr-plugin.toml, lockfiles) is rewritten by the release script or checked by a drift test. Avoid: forgent plugin 1.2.0 vs product 0.2.0.
- **VER-04** SHOULD · Build fingerprint `X.Y.Z (sha[-dirty], commit-time)` in `version --json` and any health endpoint — lets upgrade tests prove the version changed. Use commit time, not wall clock.
- **VER-05** SHOULD · Release-prep script: clean tree, `main`==`origin/main`, tag absent, CI green, bump all manifests + CHANGELOG, confirm before tag/push; `--dry-run`.
- **VER-06** SHOULD · Pre-commit hook (via `core.hooksPath`, checked by CI/doctor) enforces monotonic versions and manifest sync; escape env var.
- **VER-07** SHOULD · Prerelease = `-` in tag; GitHub `latest` never points to it, so installers need `--version`; say so in README.
- **VER-08** SHOULD · CHANGELOG (Keep-a-Changelog) feeds release notes.

---
id_prefix: REL
title: Build & release pipeline
applies_when: compiled artifacts or GitHub Releases
---

# Build & release (REL)

- **REL-01** MUST · Explicit target matrix (typ. linux x64/arm64, darwin arm64, windows x64) + documented unsupported list and fallback. Linux: static (musl / CGO off); if glibc is unavoidable, build on the oldest image and check a glibc ceiling.
- **REL-02** MUST · One asset-naming rule shared by workflow, installer, updater, docs. Choose archive vs bare binary once — installer and updater must handle the same format. Avoid: herdr-go updater writing the .tar.gz over the exe.
- **REL-03** MUST · Release reruns full CI (reusable workflow / `needs:`).
- **REL-04** MUST · A reusable "build assets" workflow runs on every PR (build + package + consumer proof, no upload); the tag workflow calls it then publishes.
- **REL-05** MUST · One packaging script for local dry run, CI and release; no naming/layout logic in YAML.
- **REL-06** MUST · `checksums.txt` written by a final job that `needs:` all builds; includes installers; re-verified; expected asset count asserted.
- **REL-07** SHOULD · Draft → smoke test → publish, so a failing smoke test never leaves a broken public release.
- **REL-08** SHOULD · Stamp the version into release-attached installers (`@VERSION@` → sed); the unstamped repo copy refuses to run without `--version`.
- **REL-09** SHOULD · Reproducible: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, path trimming, deterministic tar/zip, sorted checksums.
- **REL-10** SHOULD · Workflow hardening: `permissions: {}` + per-job grants, actions pinned by SHA, pinned runner images, `fail-fast: false`.
- **REL-11** SHOULD · Embedded web/template assets: clean checkout builds without Node; CI fails if a release ships an empty bundle.
- **REL-12** SHOULD · Release profile tuned (strip, LTO) — see language overlay.

title: Supply-chain integrity & authenticity
applies_when: anything users download and execute

- **SEC-04** MUST · Downloads: HTTPS only, connect + wall-clock timeout (wget `--timeout` is idle-only → wrap in `timeout`), per-asset byte cap.
- **SEC-05** MUST · Safe extraction: reject absolute, `..`, drive-letter, symlink, hardlink, device entries; expect an exact layout.
- **SEC-06** SHOULD · Dependency advisories gate the release (cargo deny / govulncheck / npm audit).
- **SEC-07** MAY · Content-addressed release identity (digest of a canonical file manifest) → enables verify, quarantine, exact pins.
- **SEC-08** MAY · OS code signing (Authenticode, notarization); otherwise document the SmartScreen/Gatekeeper workaround.

---
id_prefix: INS
title: Install scripts (install.sh / install.ps1)
applies_when: binary distributed outside a package manager
---

# Install scripts (INS) — skeleton: `templates/install.sh`

- **INS-01** MUST · One-liners per OS from `releases/latest/download/install.{sh,ps1}` (version-stamped, REL-08), not raw `main`.
- **INS-02** MUST · POSIX sh, `set -eu`, all code in functions, `main "$@"` as the last line (a truncated `curl|sh` can't run half a script).
- **INS-03** MUST · Allow-list platform detection mapped through REL-02; Windows checks `PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` first; unsupported → name the source-build fallback.
- **INS-04** MUST · Every knob is a prefixed env var and a flag (`_VERSION`, `_INSTALL_DIR`, `_RELEASE_BASE`, `_DRY_RUN`, `_NO_MODIFY_PATH`, `_YES`, `_UNINSTALL`); each name has one meaning; document them in a table.
- **INS-05** MUST · Resolve latest via `releases/latest/download/` or the redirect, never the API (no rate limit).
- **INS-06** MUST · Temp dir + trap → verify (SEC-01/03/05) → run `candidate --version` → copy into the target dir → `mv -f`. Renaming avoids "Text file busy"; on Windows, rename the running exe to `.old` first.
- **INS-07** SHOULD · Ownership marker `.<app>-managed` (version inside) next to the binary; refuse to overwrite/uninstall unmarked binaries; same version → no-op.
- **INS-08** SHOULD · Keep `.rollback`; restore if the activated binary fails `--version`.
- **INS-09** MUST · Default `~/.local/bin` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\bin`; refuse root unless `<APP>_ALLOW_ROOT=1`.
- **INS-10** MUST · Pick one PATH policy and document it: (A) print the exact export/SetEnvironmentVariable line, or (B) fenced `# >>> app >>>` blocks (bash, zsh via `$ZDOTDIR`, fish conf.d, `.profile`; Windows `HKCU\Environment` keeping `REG_EXPAND_SZ` + `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`) removed on uninstall.
- **INS-11** SHOULD · Only HTTP 404 may fall back to a source build; other errors fail hard. Support curl and wget.
- **INS-12** MUST · Installer and binary agree on every path: take them from the binary (`<bin> paths --json`) or add a contract test. Avoid: skillstation purges `~/.config` but macOS uses Application Support.
- **INS-13** SHOULD · Keep the script small: place the binary, then delegate config/secrets/service/agent setup to `<bin> setup` / `doctor --fix`.
- **INS-14** MUST · Finish with `--version` and 1–3 "Next:" commands; print generated secrets only on first creation.
- **INS-15** SHOULD · `--local-fixture DIR` + a fake verifier make the full lifecycle testable offline.
- **INS-16** MAY · Preflight the service manager (`systemctl --user show-environment`, `launchctl`) before touching anything.

---
id_prefix: UPD
title: Self-update
applies_when: binary distributed via direct download (skip if package-manager only)
---

# Self-update (UPD)

- **UPD-01** MUST · `update [--check] [--version vX] [--force] [--json]`; `--check` exits non-zero when an update exists.
- **UPD-02** MUST · Only update what our installer installed (marker); for package-manager installs, print the `brew upgrade …`-style command instead.
- **UPD-03** MUST · Same checks as the installer (naming, checksum, signature, caps, extraction), using shared constants; report whether the signature was checked.
- **UPD-04** MUST · Update repo comes from build metadata (`CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`, ldflags), so forks update from themselves; a base-URL env var allows tests and mirrors.
- **UPD-05** MUST · Version policy is a pure, tested function: `latest` never downgrades; an explicit `--version` may. Resolve the release once and use it for both the compare and the download.
- **UPD-06** MUST · Handle the real release format (extract archives); CI tests the updater against real assets.
- **UPD-07** MUST · Stage next to the real binary (symlinks resolved), require `staged --version` == target, back up, rename (Windows `.old-<pid>`), roll back on failure; clean `.old`/`.bak` on next start.
- **UPD-08** SHOULD · Post-swap migrations/template refresh run in the **new** binary (`<new> doctor --after-update`, `--internal-merge-config`).
- **UPD-09** SHOULD · Daemon: stop → swap → migrate → start → health check (version == target) → roll back binary + config if unhealthy.
- **UPD-10** SHOULD · Under sudo, skip user-scoped steps and print what the user should run.
- **UPD-11** MAY · Cached, opt-out "update available" notice (off in CI/non-TTY); prerelease channel.
- **UPD-12** MAY · Teams needing identical bits: tiny global bootstrap + per-project committed digest pin with `upgrade`/`repair`/`verify` (forgent `fgctl`).

---
id_prefix: CFG
title: Config, state, secrets & migrations
applies_when: tool has persistent config, data, cache or secrets
---

# Config & state (CFG)

- **CFG-01** MUST · Separate config/state/cache using OS conventions: Linux XDG (honoured only if absolute), macOS `~/Library/Application Support` (Go `os.UserConfigDir`), Windows `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
- **CFG-02** MUST · One override env var per root (`<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`, `<APP>_STATE_DIR`), one meaning each; tests use them.
- **CFG-03** MUST · `<bin> paths [--json]` — installer, uninstaller and docs take paths from it.
- **CFG-04** MUST · Documented precedence flag > env > project > user > default; `config explain <key>` shows which layer won.
- **CFG-05** MUST · Zero-config start; defaults come from the binary (`config default`); no hand-kept example file that drifts.
- **CFG-06** MUST · Atomic writes that keep the existing file mode; 0700 dir when sensitive.
- **CFG-07** MUST · Secrets live outside the config (0600 / owner-only DACL); the binary refuses loose permissions; units and agent configs reference the path, never the value.
- **CFG-08** MUST · A corrupt config gives a clear error with file, problem and fix, never silent defaults; report all validation errors at once.
- **CFG-09** SHOULD · Choose deliberately: preserve unknown keys (user-edited, shared across versions) or deny them (security config); aliases for renamed keys.
- **CFG-10** SHOULD · Upgrades add missing keys only, with a backup and validation, run by the new binary.
- **CFG-11** SHOULD · Versioned data migrations, or the schema version in the filename (`registry-v4.db`) so old and new binaries coexist; legacy dir migration fails closed if both dirs exist.
- **CFG-12** SHOULD · `config show|get|set|unset|edit|check|path`; `edit` uses `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` and re-validates.
- **CFG-13** MAY · Config files store only diffs from a shipped standard, annotated with why; schema scopes stop a committed project file from setting machine or secret keys (forgent).
- **CFG-14** MUST · Insecure overrides (non-loopback bind, auth off) print a warning; never ship a fixed default token.

applies_when: binary distributed via direct download (skip if package-manager only)

# Self-update (UPD)

- **UPD-01** MUST · `update [--check] [--version vX] [--force] [--json]`; `--check` exits non-zero when an update exists.
- **UPD-02** MUST · Only update what our installer installed (marker); for package-manager installs, print the `brew upgrade …`-style command instead.
- **UPD-03** MUST · Same checks as the installer (naming, checksum, signature, caps, extraction), using shared constants; report whether the signature was checked.
- **UPD-04** MUST · Update repo comes from build metadata (`CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`, ldflags), so forks update from themselves; a base-URL env var allows tests and mirrors.
- **UPD-05** MUST · Version policy is a pure, tested function: `latest` never downgrades; an explicit `--version` may. Resolve the release once and use it for both the compare and the download.
- **UPD-06** MUST · Handle the real release format (extract archives); CI tests the updater against real assets.
- **UPD-07** MUST · Stage next to the real binary (symlinks resolved), require `staged --version` == target, back up, rename (Windows `.old-<pid>`), roll back on failure; clean `.old`/`.bak` on next start.
- **UPD-08** SHOULD · Post-swap migrations/template refresh run in the **new** binary (`<new> doctor --after-update`, `--internal-merge-config`).
- **UPD-09** SHOULD · Daemon: stop → swap → migrate → start → health check (version == target) → roll back binary + config if unhealthy.
- **UPD-10** SHOULD · Under sudo, skip user-scoped steps and print what the user should run.
- **UPD-11** MAY · Cached, opt-out "update available" notice (off in CI/non-TTY); prerelease channel.
- **UPD-12** MAY · Teams needing identical bits: tiny global bootstrap + per-project committed digest pin with `upgrade`/`repair`/`verify` (forgent `fgctl`).

title: Config, state, secrets & migrations
applies_when: tool has persistent config, data, cache or secrets
---

# Config & state (CFG)

- **CFG-01** MUST · Separate config/state/cache using OS conventions: Linux XDG (honoured only if absolute), macOS `~/Library/Application Support` (Go `os.UserConfigDir`), Windows `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
- **CFG-02** MUST · One override env var per root (`<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`, `<APP>_STATE_DIR`), one meaning each; tests use them.
- **CFG-03** MUST · `<bin> paths [--json]` — installer, uninstaller and docs take paths from it.
- **CFG-04** MUST · Documented precedence flag > env > project > user > default; `config explain <key>` shows which layer won.
- **CFG-05** MUST · Zero-config start; defaults come from the binary (`config default`); no hand-kept example file that drifts.
- **CFG-06** MUST · Atomic writes that keep the existing file mode; 0700 dir when sensitive.
- **CFG-07** MUST · Secrets live outside the config (0600 / owner-only DACL); the binary refuses loose permissions; units and agent configs reference the path, never the value.
- **CFG-08** MUST · A corrupt config gives a clear error with file, problem and fix, never silent defaults; report all validation errors at once.
- **CFG-09** SHOULD · Choose deliberately: preserve unknown keys (user-edited, shared across versions) or deny them (security config); aliases for renamed keys.
- **CFG-10** SHOULD · Upgrades add missing keys only, with a backup and validation, run by the new binary.
- **CFG-11** SHOULD · Versioned data migrations, or the schema version in the filename (`registry-v4.db`) so old and new binaries coexist; legacy dir migration fails closed if both dirs exist.
- **CFG-12** SHOULD · `config show|get|set|unset|edit|check|path`; `edit` uses `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` and re-validates.
- **CFG-13** MAY · Config files store only diffs from a shipped standard, annotated with why; schema scopes stop a committed project file from setting machine or secret keys (forgent).
- **CFG-14** MUST · Insecure overrides (non-loopback bind, auth off) print a warning; never ship a fixed default token.

-# Doctor (`<bin> doctor`)
+# Doctor (DOC)
-### DOC-01 · MUST · Read-only by default

+- **DOC-01** MUST · Read-only by default (open DBs read-only); changes only with `--fix`; never prompt without a TTY.
+- **DOC-02** MUST · `doctor [--fix [--dry-run]] [--json] [--strict]`; exit 0 healthy / 1 problems / 2 bad usage. Avoid: mdview doctor always exits 0.
+- **DOC-03** MUST · Each check has a stable code, status (ok/warn/fail/skip), critical flag, detail, fix command and an optional auto-fix.
+- **DOC-04** MUST · `--fix` re-runs every check (bounded loop); the exit code reflects the post-fix state; each change is reported.
+- **DOC-05** SHOULD · Check registry (modules register checks and fixes); each check isolated with a timeout.
+- **DOC-06** SHOULD · Catalogue:
+  - binary on PATH and the version;
+  - config valid and secret permissions;
+  - schema version;
+  - service running with live version == binary;
+  - external dependency min versions;
+  - endpoints reachable without sending secrets;
+  - agent skill/block/MCP/hooks in sync **and** actually executable;
+  - leftover `.old`/legacy files.
-### DOC-02 · MUST · CLI surface and exit codes
-`doctor [--fix [--dry-run]] [--json] [--strict|--check] [--verbose]`.
-Exit `0` healthy (or only warnings), `1` problems remain, `2` invalid invocation. Doctor that always
-exits 0 is useless in CI.
-### DOC-03 · MUST · Check model
-Each check: stable `code` (e.g. `config_missing`, `client_entry_outdated`), `status`
-(`ok|warn|fail|skip|info`), `critical` bool, human `detail`, `fix` hint (exact command) and optional
-automatic fix action. JSON output is a stable, documented schema.
-### DOC-04 · MUST · `--fix` then re-check
-Apply fixes, re-run all checks (loop ≤ N rounds), exit code reflects **post-fix** state. Report each
-change (`FIXED +`).
-### DOC-05 · SHOULD · Pluggable check registry
-`registerCheck` / `registerFix` / `RegisterProvider` so each module owns its checks. Run each check
-panic/exception-safe with a timeout.
-### DOC-06 · SHOULD · Standard check catalogue
-- binary on PATH and is the one being run; version (+ newer available?)
-- config present & valid; paths writable; secret file permissions
-- data schema version (read-only)
-- running daemon/service: registered, running, **live version == binary version**
-- external dependencies present with min versions (git, node, runtime CLIs)
-- network endpoints reachable (without sending secrets unasked)
-- agent integration: skill/instruction block/MCP entry/hooks present and **in sync** (byte-exact with
-  embedded template) — and **actually executes** (run hook with harmless input + timeout)
-- only check/configure third-party tools that are installed (else `skip`)
-- leftovers: legacy files, `.old`/`.bak` binaries, legacy dirs
-### DOC-07 · SHOULD · Guided fixes in TTY

id_prefix: DOC
title: Doctor / diagnostics / setup
applies_when: always (any tool with config, integrations, services or external deps)
---

# Doctor (`<bin> doctor`)

### DOC-01 · MUST · Read-only by default
`doctor` diagnoses only — never creates or modifies files (open DBs read-only). Changes only with
`--fix`. Non-TTY never prompts.

### DOC-02 · MUST · CLI surface and exit codes
`doctor [--fix [--dry-run]] [--json] [--strict|--check] [--verbose]`.
Exit `0` healthy (or only warnings), `1` problems remain, `2` invalid invocation. Doctor that always
exits 0 is useless in CI.

### DOC-03 · MUST · Check model
Each check: stable `code` (e.g. `config_missing`, `client_entry_outdated`), `status`
(`ok|warn|fail|skip|info`), `critical` bool, human `detail`, `fix` hint (exact command) and optional
automatic fix action. JSON output is a stable, documented schema.

### DOC-04 · MUST · `--fix` then re-check
Apply fixes, re-run all checks (loop ≤ N rounds), exit code reflects **post-fix** state. Report each
change (`FIXED +`).

### DOC-05 · SHOULD · Pluggable check registry
`registerCheck` / `registerFix` / `RegisterProvider` so each module owns its checks. Run each check
panic/exception-safe with a timeout.

### DOC-06 · SHOULD · Standard check catalogue
- binary on PATH and is the one being run; version (+ newer available?)
- config present & valid; paths writable; secret file permissions
- data schema version (read-only)
- running daemon/service: registered, running, **live version == binary version**
- external dependencies present with min versions (git, node, runtime CLIs)
- network endpoints reachable (without sending secrets unasked)
- agent integration: skill/instruction block/MCP entry/hooks present and **in sync** (byte-exact with
  embedded template) — and **actually executes** (run hook with harmless input + timeout)
- only check/configure third-party tools that are installed (else `skip`)
- leftovers: legacy files, `.old`/`.bak` binaries, legacy dirs

### DOC-07 · SHOULD · Guided fixes in TTY
Interactive mode offers fixes one by one; `--yes` applies all; never auto-sends credentials to remote
services — print the command instead.

### DOC-08 · SHOULD · `status` = fast subset ending with exactly one next command

### DOC-09 · SHOULD · `setup` / `init` is fill-only and idempotent
Creates only what's missing, never overwrites customisation, reports exactly what changed or "nothing
to do". Works from worktrees (resolve main checkout when relevant).

### DOC-10 · MAY · `--after-update` hidden mode
Invoked by the updater via the new binary to refresh templates/skills that already exist.

title: AI-agent integration (skills, MCP, hooks, instruction blocks)
applies_when: tool is meant to be used by coding agents
---

# Agent integration (AGT)

- **AGT-01** MUST · The binary installs the integration, opt-in and reversible (`connect [-g] [--dry-run]` / `connect --remove`); hosts that aren't installed are skipped.
- **AGT-02** MUST · Per-host adapter table kept in code and docs:

  | Host | Project config | User config | Permissions |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `~/.claude.json` | `.claude/settings*.json` |
  | Codex | `.codex/config.toml` | `~/.codex/config.toml` | — |
  | Gemini | `.gemini/settings.json` | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | — |
- **AGT-03** MUST · Edit third-party config surgically: preserve its format (toml_edit), compare-and-swap on a preimage digest, back up, keep the file mode. A malformed file is refused, never overwritten as `{}` (mdview gap).
- **AGT-04** MUST · Register the absolute binary path (or a stable shim); pass a token **file path**, never the token.
- **AGT-05** SHOULD · `<!-- app:START/END -->` block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md: idempotent upsert, written through symlinks, byte-exact with an embedded template (LF via `.gitattributes`).
- **AGT-06** SHOULD · One canonical skill source generates per-host wrappers; CI/doctor fail on drift.
- **AGT-07** SHOULD · Ownership of installed skills by digests of every shipped version: known → upgrade, unknown → user-edited, leave alone; CI checks the table.
- **AGT-08** SHOULD · Project-local hooks through a stable entry point; fill-only merge; doctor runs the hook with harmless input.
- **AGT-09** SHOULD · MCP server is a thin per-call proxy to the CLI, so upgrades need no reconnect.
- **AGT-10** MAY · WSL → Windows desktop client via `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e <bin> mcp`.
- **AGT-11** MAY · Narrow permission rule (`Bash(app open:*)`), removed on uninstall.

Hooks call a stable path (`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.<app>/bin/<app> hook <kind>` or the absolute
binary) that survives upgrades; fill-only merge preserving user hooks; exact migration of our old hook
commands; doctor executes the hook with harmless input + timeout.

### AGT-09 · SHOULD · MCP server survives upgrades
Make the MCP server a thin proxy that shells out to the CLI per call (or re-execs), so a binary update
applies without client reconnect.

### AGT-10 · SHOULD · Cross-environment reach
WSL → Windows desktop clients via `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e <abs-binary> mcp`, detected with
`WSL_DISTRO_NAME` / `/proc/version`.

### AGT-11 · SHOULD · Plugin / marketplace manifests are thin and versioned
`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`, host plugin manifests: thin launchers over the CLI,
expose read-only actions unless control is intended, `min_<host>_version`, version synced by VER-03.

### AGT-12 · MAY · Permissions entry for the CLI
Add a narrow allow rule (`Bash(<app> open:*)`) rather than broad ones; remove on uninstall.

# Service / daemon (SVC)

- **SVC-01** MUST · User-level service installed by the binary: systemd `--user` (+ `enable-linger`), LaunchAgent (`bootstrap gui/<uid>`), per-user Scheduled Task. No root.
- **SVC-02** MUST · `service install|uninstall|start|stop|restart|status|logs` as a thin pass-through that prints the native command.
- **SVC-03** MUST · Idempotent: `bootout` before `bootstrap`; disable conflicting legacy/dev units.
- **SVC-04** MUST · No secrets in unit files.
- **SVC-05** SHOULD · systemd `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths`, `Restart=always`; launchd `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`; Windows restart count (1 min minimum interval).
- **SVC-06** MUST · Bind `127.0.0.1` with a generated token by default.
- **SVC-07** SHOULD · The health endpoint reports the fingerprint; the CLI restarts an older daemon (asks the live process, never trusts a lock file, never downgrades).
- **SVC-08** SHOULD · Linux `current_exe()` gains ` (deleted)` after a swap — strip it before re-spawning.
- **SVC-09** MAY · Separate dev unit from a template (`dev-deploy.sh`).

- **TST-07** SHOULD · Tests redirect HOME and the config/state dirs to temp dirs.

# Uninstall (UNI)

- **UNI-01** MUST · `<bin> uninstall` and/or `install.sh --uninstall` exist, and the documented command resolves. Avoid: herdr-go prints a 404 URL.
- **UNI-02** MUST · Exact inverse of install + setup + `doctor --fix`: binary, marker, PATH blocks, service, skills/MCP/hooks/blocks, permissions, PATH symlinks.
- **UNI-03** MUST · Plan → `--dry-run` / confirm (`--yes` without a TTY) → apply; re-read third-party configs at apply time; timestamped backups.
- **UNI-04** MUST · Remove only what is still exactly ours; report anything else (unfenced rc lines, other projects' blocks) without touching it.
- **UNI-05** MUST · Keep user data and say where it is; `--purge --yes` removes it, never `/`, `$HOME` or `..`; paths come from CFG-03.
- **UNI-06** SHOULD · Irreversible steps last, skipped if any earlier step failed.
- **UNI-07** SHOULD · Windows deferred self-delete; refuse to run under sudo; for package-manager installs, print the right command (verify the package manager owns it — npm exits 0 even if nothing was removed).

---
id_prefix: AGT
title: AI-agent integration (skills, MCP, hooks, instruction blocks)
applies_when: tool is meant to be used by coding agents
---

# Agent integration (AGT)

- **AGT-01** MUST · The binary installs the integration, opt-in and reversible (`connect [-g] [--dry-run]` / `connect --remove`); hosts that aren't installed are skipped.
- **AGT-02** MUST · Per-host adapter table kept in code and docs:

  | Host | Project config | User config | Permissions |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `~/.claude.json` | `.claude/settings*.json` |
  | Codex | `.codex/config.toml` | `~/.codex/config.toml` | — |
  | Gemini | `.gemini/settings.json` | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | — |
- **AGT-03** MUST · Edit third-party config surgically: preserve its format (toml_edit), compare-and-swap on a preimage digest, back up, keep the file mode. A malformed file is refused, never overwritten as `{}` (mdview gap).
- **AGT-04** MUST · Register the absolute binary path (or a stable shim); pass a token **file path**, never the token.
- **AGT-05** SHOULD · `<!-- app:START/END -->` block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md: idempotent upsert, written through symlinks, byte-exact with an embedded template (LF via `.gitattributes`).
- **AGT-06** SHOULD · One canonical skill source generates per-host wrappers; CI/doctor fail on drift.
- **AGT-07** SHOULD · Ownership of installed skills by digests of every shipped version: known → upgrade, unknown → user-edited, leave alone; CI checks the table.
- **AGT-08** SHOULD · Project-local hooks through a stable entry point; fill-only merge; doctor runs the hook with harmless input.
- **AGT-09** SHOULD · MCP server is a thin per-call proxy to the CLI, so upgrades need no reconnect.
- **AGT-10** MAY · WSL → Windows desktop client via `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e <bin> mcp`.
- **AGT-11** MAY · Narrow permission rule (`Bash(app open:*)`), removed on uninstall.

---
id_prefix: SVC
title: Background service / daemon
applies_when: tool runs a long-lived process
---

# Service / daemon (SVC)

- **SVC-01** MUST · User-level service installed by the binary: systemd `--user` (+ `enable-linger`), LaunchAgent (`bootstrap gui/<uid>`), per-user Scheduled Task. No root.
- **SVC-02** MUST · `service install|uninstall|start|stop|restart|status|logs` as a thin pass-through that prints the native command.
- **SVC-03** MUST · Idempotent: `bootout` before `bootstrap`; disable conflicting legacy/dev units.
- **SVC-04** MUST · No secrets in unit files.
- **SVC-05** SHOULD · systemd `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths`, `Restart=always`; launchd `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`; Windows restart count (1 min minimum interval).
- **SVC-06** MUST · Bind `127.0.0.1` with a generated token by default.
- **SVC-07** SHOULD · The health endpoint reports the fingerprint; the CLI restarts an older daemon (asks the live process, never trusts a lock file, never downgrades).
- **SVC-08** SHOULD · Linux `current_exe()` gains ` (deleted)` after a swap — strip it before re-spawning.
- **SVC-09** MAY · Separate dev unit from a template (`dev-deploy.sh`).

---
id_prefix: TST
title: Testing the distribution
applies_when: always
---

# Testing (TST)

- **TST-01** MUST · Consumer proof: install from the built assets outside the checkout (sh, PowerShell 5.1 and 7) before upload.
- **TST-02** MUST · Smoke test on every OS: one-liner → `bash -l -c '<bin> --version'` (proves PATH) → `doctor --strict` → service health → uninstall → command gone.
- **TST-03** MUST · Upgrade from the previous tag (resolved dynamically); assert the version changed and config survived.
- **TST-04** SHOULD · Offline installer lifecycle via fixture: re-run, upgrade, rollback, unmanaged refusal, checksum mismatch, caps, purge guards.
- **TST-05** SHOULD · Static contract test wired into CI: asset names, paths, doc links and retired names agree across workflow, installers, binary and docs.
- **TST-06** SHOULD · Unit tests for the pure policies: version compare, platform→asset, precedence, merge, paths for each OS.
- **TST-07** SHOULD · Tests redirect HOME and the config/state dirs to temp dirs.

---
id_prefix: UX
title: Docs & CLI UX
applies_when: always
---

# Docs & UX (UX)

- **UX-01** MUST · README Install section: per-OS one-liner, platforms, how to pin a version, a prerelease note, the source fallback, then Upgrade / Uninstall / Doctor / Config links.
- **UX-02** MUST · `docs/installation.md`: env-var table, per-OS "where things live" table, signature verification, troubleshooting (SmartScreen, PATH, glibc).
- **UX-03** SHOULD · `docs/release-runbook.md`: cut, verify, roll back or yank a release.
- **UX-04** MUST · Errors are Error / Why / Fix, in both human and JSON output.
- **UX-05** SHOULD · Installer, init and status end with "Next:" commands; `--help` is task-ordered.
- **UX-06** SHOULD · `--json` with published schemas for version, status, doctor, `update --check`, paths, config.
- **UX-07** SHOULD · `completions <shell>` + a man page, shipped in archives. None of the source projects had this.
- **UX-08** SHOULD · A rename is a migration: alias or shim for a window, auto-move dirs/env/agent entries.
- **UX-09** SHOULD · No internal ticket jargon in user-facing docs.

- **RS-04** MUST · musl targets via `cross`/`cargo-zigbuild`; `rustls` rather than OpenSSL; `rusqlite` with `bundled`; `aarch64-apple-darwin` on `macos-14`. [REL-01]
- **RS-05** SHOULD · `rust-toolchain.toml` pins channel, components and targets.
- **RS-06** MUST · CI: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, tests on Linux + Windows, `cargo deny check advisories bans sources`. [SEC-06]
- **RS-07** SHOULD · Heavy crates (Tauri/GUI) left out of `default-members`.
- **RS-08** SHOULD · `include_str!` for templates, `rust-embed` for the UI, `build.rs` creates the embed dir. [REL-11]
- **RS-09** SHOULD · Updates with `self-replace`/`self_update`, `flate2`+`tar`/`zip`, `sha2`, `semver`; canonicalize `current_exe()`. [UPD-06, UPD-07]
- **RS-10** SHOULD · Config with `directories`/`etcetera`; `serde(default|alias|deny_unknown_fields)`; `toml_edit` for third-party TOML; `tempfile::persist`. [CFG-*, AGT-03]
- **RS-11** SHOULD · `clap` + `clap_complete` + `clap_mangen`. [UX-07]
- **RS-12** MAY · Fallback `cargo install --git … --locked` or `cargo binstall` metadata; `--root` installs into `<root>/bin`. [INS-11]

language: go
title: Go overlay
detect: go.mod
sources: [skillstation]
---

# Go (GO) — refines common rules in [brackets]

- **GO-01** MUST · `-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w -X …Version -X …Commit -X …Date(commit time) -X …Dirty"`; defaults `dev`; fallback `debug.ReadBuildInfo()`. [VER-01, VER-04]
- **GO-02** MUST · `CGO_ENABLED=0` with pure-Go deps (`modernc.org/sqlite`); cross-compile GOOS×GOARCH from one runner. [REL-01]
- **GO-03** SHOULD · goreleaser (archives, checksums, SBOM, cosign, brew/scoop/nfpm) rather than hand-listing assets in YAML. [REL-05]
- **GO-04** MUST · `go vet` (also with `GOOS=windows`), golangci-lint, `govulncheck`, `go test -race`. [SEC-06]
- **GO-05** SHOULD · Remember that `os.UserConfigDir()` is Application Support on macOS; installers use `<bin> paths`. [CFG-01, INS-12]
- **GO-06** SHOULD · Updates: `minio/selfupdate` or hand-rolled code with `CheckRedirect` + `http.ErrUseLastResponse`, `io.LimitReader`, tar header type checks. [UPD-*]
- **GO-07** SHOULD · Keep unknown config keys with a `map[string]json.RawMessage` round-trip. [CFG-09]
- **GO-08** SHOULD · `//go:embed` for the UI and templates; `dist/.keep` placeholder; CI checks the real bundle. [REL-11]
- **GO-09** SHOULD · cobra `completion`, or an explicit `completions` command. [UX-07]

id_prefix: NODE
language: node / typescript
title: Node.js / TypeScript overlay
detect: package.json
sources: [forgent; embedded UIs in mdview/herdr-go/skillstation]
---

# Node / TS (NODE) — if Node only builds an embedded UI, just REL-11 + NODE-06 apply

- **NODE-01** MUST · `package.json` version is the source of truth; `npm version` / the release script updates the lockfile with it. [VER-01]
- **NODE-02** MUST · Pick one primary channel: npm registry (`files` allow-list, `engines`, `bin`, `npm publish --provenance`), a compiled single binary (bun / SEA, then follow the common rules), or npm-from-GitHub as legacy only.
- **NODE-03** MUST · No `postinstall` that downloads or writes outside the package; ship native binaries as per-platform `optionalDependencies`.
- **NODE-04** MUST · `engines.node` plus a doctor check for it. [DOC-06]
- **NODE-05** SHOULD · Prebuilt napi addons per target, with a glibc ceiling. [REL-01]
- **NODE-06** SHOULD · `npm ci`, `npm audit --omit=dev`, and a `npm pack --dry-run` content check; pin Node via `.nvmrc` in CI. [SEC-06]
- **NODE-07** SHOULD · Before `npm uninstall -g`, confirm the package is installed (`npm root -g`). [UNI-07]

id_prefix: POLY
language: polyglot
title: Multi-language products overlay
detect: more than one of Cargo.toml / go.mod / package.json / pyproject.toml at product level
sources: [forgent]
---

# Polyglot (POLY) — load together with each language overlay

- **POLY-01** MUST · One version source of truth; compiled code embeds that file (`include_str!`, `//go:embed`). [VER-01]
- **POLY-02** MUST · A drift test in the normal suite covers every manifest, lockfile and plugin manifest (skip vendored ones). [VER-03]
- **POLY-03** MUST · One release-prep script for all ecosystems. [VER-05]
- **POLY-04** SHOULD · Shared contracts (doctor rows, config schema, error codes) live as data files read by both runtimes.
- **POLY-05** SHOULD · Each rule has one implementation; the other runtime calls it through a facade.
- **POLY-06** SHOULD · One release tree with `manifest.json` (digests, modes, required runtimes). [SEC-07]

language: <name>
title: <Name> overlay
detect: <marker file, e.g. pyproject.toml>
sources: [<project or external link>]

# <Name> (XX) — refines common rules in [brackets]; never restate a common rule

- **XX-01** MUST · Version source → binary. [VER-01]
- **XX-02** MUST · Targets / artifact type / cross-build. [REL-01]
- **XX-03** MUST · CI quality + advisory gates. [SEC-06]
- **XX-04** SHOULD · Native channel (pipx, gem…) and how update/uninstall defer to it. [UPD-02, UNI-07]
- **XX-05** SHOULD · Libraries for paths, atomic writes, self-update, completions. [CFG-*, UPD-*, UX-07]

channel: agent-host plugin / marketplace
title: Agent-host plugin & marketplace
applies_when: tool also ships as a plugin inside a host (Claude Code marketplace, herdr, …)
sources: [forgent, herdr-go]

# Agent-host plugin (CH-PLUGIN)

- **CH-PLUGIN-01** MUST · The plugin version is synced by the release script and drift test. [VER-03]
- **CH-PLUGIN-02** MUST · The plugin is a thin launcher over the installed CLI: no second implementation, no build step.
- **CH-PLUGIN-03** SHOULD · Read-only actions by default; leave out controls that would let the host manage its own supervisor.
- **CH-PLUGIN-04** SHOULD · Declare `min_<host>_version` and platforms; doctor checks the host version.
- **CH-PLUGIN-05** SHOULD · Plugin skills are generated from the canonical source. [AGT-06]
- **CH-PLUGIN-06** SHOULD · Keep fixture/dogfood plugins out of the public marketplace.

channel: <name, e.g. homebrew, scoop, docker, pypi>
title: <Channel>
applies_when: <when to use this channel>
sources: [<project or external link>]

- **CH-XX-01** MUST · How the channel's version stays in sync. [VER-03]
- **CH-XX-02** MUST · How it's published from CI (token, provenance). [REL-*]
- **CH-XX-03** MUST · How update/uninstall defer to it. [UPD-02, UNI-07]
- **CH-XX-04** SHOULD · Smoke test for this channel. [TST-02]

# Rust

Rules here **implement** common rules (referenced in brackets) with Rust specifics.

### RS-01 · MUST · Version from Cargo, workspace-wide  [VER-01]
`[workspace.package] version = "X.Y.Z"` + `version.workspace = true` in members. Binary uses
`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`; repo for updates from `env!("CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY")` [UPD-04].
Polyglot: `include_str!("…/package.json")` + parse at build time, or `build.rs` reading the SoT.

### RS-02 · SHOULD · Build fingerprint via `build.rs`  [VER-04]
Emit `cargo:rustc-env=<APP>_FINGERPRINT=X.Y.Z (sha[-dirty], commit-time)`; fall back to `nogit`.
Note: emitting no `rerun-if-*` lines reruns on every package change (fresh dirty flag) at the cost of
rebuilding the build script output; choose deliberately.

### RS-03 · MUST · Release profile  [REL-12]
```toml
[profile.release]
strip = true
lto = "thin"          # or true + codegen-units = 1 for smallest/fastest
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"       # only if you don't rely on unwinding
opt-level = 3         # or "s" for size-sensitive CLIs
```

### RS-04 · MUST · Targets  [REL-01]
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` (via `cross` or `cargo-zigbuild`; static, any
distro), `aarch64-apple-darwin` (`macos-14`), `x86_64-apple-darwin` if needed (cross-compile from
arm runner rather than waiting for scarce Intel runners), `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.
If glibc is unavoidable (napi, some C deps): build on oldest image + glibc ceiling check.
Use `rustls` instead of OpenSSL to keep musl builds simple; `rusqlite` with `bundled`.

### RS-05 · SHOULD · Pin toolchain
`rust-toolchain.toml` with channel + components + targets.

### RS-06 · MUST · Supply-chain gates  [SEC-06]
`cargo deny check advisories bans sources` (or `cargo audit`) in CI; `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` on Linux + Windows.

### RS-07 · SHOULD · Exclude heavy crates from default build
Desktop/GUI crates (Tauri) out of `default-members` so the CLI never needs webview libs.

### RS-08 · SHOULD · Embedded assets  [REL-11]
`include_str!` / `include_bytes!` for templates (skills, instruction blocks) with LF enforced in
`.gitattributes`; `rust-embed` for web UIs with `build.rs` creating the folder; CI asserts
`index.html` is present in release builds.

### RS-09 · SHOULD · Self-update implementation  [UPD-*]
Crates: `self_update` or `self-replace` (handles Windows running-exe), `reqwest` (rustls),
`flate2` + `tar` / `zip` if archives, `sha2`, `semver`. Resolve `current_exe()` → `canonicalize`;
stage in the same directory; `std::fs::rename`. Strip Linux ` (deleted)` suffix before re-spawn
[SVC-08]. Clean `.old-*` at start of `main`.

### RS-10 · SHOULD · Config  [CFG-*]
`directories` / `etcetera` / `dirs` for OS paths; `serde` with `#[serde(default)]`, `#[serde(alias)]`,
or `deny_unknown_fields` (choose per CFG-09); `toml_edit` for comment-preserving edits of TOML (own and
third-party, e.g. Codex `~/.codex/config.toml`); `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist` for atomic writes;
keep permissions via `std::fs::set_permissions` from old metadata.

### RS-11 · SHOULD · CLI  [UX-07]
`clap` derive; `clap_complete` for `completions <shell>`; `clap_mangen` for man page; generate both in
release and ship in archives.

### RS-12 · MAY · Fallback install channel
`cargo install --git <repo> --locked` (or crates.io `cargo install <crate>`; `cargo binstall` metadata
`[package.metadata.binstall]` pointing at release assets). Installer falls back to it only on 404
[INS-11]; mind `--root` puts binaries in `<root>/bin`.

# Node.js / TypeScript

Two cases: (a) the product **is** a Node CLI; (b) Node is only a build tool for an embedded web UI
(then see REL-11 and the host language guide).

### NODE-01 · MUST · Version SoT = `package.json`  [VER-01]
Read at runtime via `createRequire(import.meta.url)('../package.json').version` or injected at bundle
time. `npm version` / release script updates `package.json` + `package-lock.json` together.

### NODE-02 · MUST · Choose the channel deliberately
- npm registry (`npm i -g <pkg>`, `npx <pkg>`) — best for Node CLIs; use `files` allow-list,
  `engines.node`, `bin` entries with `#!/usr/bin/env node`; `npm publish --provenance` from CI.
- npm-from-GitHub (`npm i -g github:o/r#vX`) — no registry, but runs `prepare` on user machines;
  treat as legacy/compat only.
- Single binary (`bun build --compile`, Node SEA, `pkg`) — then follow the common install/update rules
  like a compiled language.
Don't keep two primary channels; mark one as legacy in README (forgent gap).

### NODE-03 · MUST · No surprising install scripts
Avoid `postinstall` that downloads or writes outside the package; if needed (native binary), verify
checksums and support `--ignore-scripts` with a clear fallback. Prefer optionalDependencies per
platform (`@scope/pkg-linux-x64`) for native addons.

### NODE-04 · MUST · Engines & runtime check  [DOC-06]
`engines.node` in package.json + a doctor check (`node-version`) with fix hint.

### NODE-05 · SHOULD · Native addons (napi)
Prebuilt per target, loaded with a clear error naming the missing target; glibc ceiling [REL-01];
reproducibility check by independent rebuild (forgent).

### NODE-06 · SHOULD · Uninstall verifies ownership  [UNI-07]
Before `npm uninstall -g <pkg>`, check `npm root -g` actually contains it (npm exits 0 even if nothing
was removed).

### NODE-07 · SHOULD · Quality gates
`npm ci` (lockfile enforced), `npm audit --omit=dev`, typecheck, tests, `npm pack --dry-run` content
check in CI.

### NODE-08 · SHOULD · Front-end bundles for embedding
Vite/esbuild with deterministic output dir consumed by the host language embed; pin Node version
(`.nvmrc` / `engines`) in CI; either commit the bundle or have CI build it before the host build
(and fail if empty).

### NODE-09 · MAY · Shell completions
`omelette` / `tabtab`, or generate static scripts from the command definition.

E.g. config merge/validation implemented once (Rust), the other runtime goes through a facade/CLI —
never two implementations of the same rule.

### POLY-06 · SHOULD · Release tree with manifest
Ship one archive containing all runtimes' pieces + a `manifest.json` (file digests, modes, required
runtime versions, target) — enables verify/repair (SEC-07).

---
name: packaging-distribution-guide
description: Best-practice rules for packaging and distributing a CLI/tool — release pipeline (cross-compile, asset naming, checksums, signing), install.sh/install.ps1, self-update, config/state/secrets, doctor, uninstall, background service, AI-agent integration (skills, MCP, hooks, plugins) and distribution testing. Generic rules plus language overlays (Rust, Go, Node, polyglot) and channel guides. Use when setting up or auditing release/install/update/config/doctor/uninstall for a project, or when asked how to ship, install or update a tool.
---

# Packaging & Distribution Guide

One-line rules with stable ids (`INS-06`) and levels **MUST / SHOULD / MAY**. You turn them into a
project-specific checklist and plan, then implement it if asked.

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-<topic>.md` — language-agnostic rules; frontmatter `applies_when`
- `languages/<lang>.md` — overlays; frontmatter `detect` (marker file)
- `channels/<channel>.md` — package managers, plugin marketplaces…
- `references.md` — rule → real code in the source repos (open it when implementing)
- `templates/` — `project-checklist.md` (output), `install.sh` (tested POSIX skeleton)

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project: languages, kind (CLI/daemon/agent tool), platforms, channels; whether it has config, secrets, a long-running process, agent integration.
2. **Select**:
   - always read `common/00-principles.md`;
   - read every other `common/` file whose `applies_when` matches;
   - read every language overlay whose `detect` file exists (+ `polyglot.md` if more than one matches);
   - read channels in use.
   If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
3. **Decide** (table in the checklist template): version source of truth, targets, asset format and naming, channels, PATH policy, config paths, signing level, agent hosts. Ask only about what you can't infer.
4. **Audit**: mark every selected rule `done` / `todo` / `gap` / `n/a (reason)`. A MUST can't be skipped without a reason. Order the work VER → REL/SEC → INS → UPD → CFG → DOC → UNI → SVC/AGT → TST → UX.
5. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
6. **Implement** on request; cite rule ids in comments/commits where useful. Open `references.md` for proven code.
7. **Feed back** new lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Precedence: PRN > MUST > SHOULD > MAY. An overlay may refine a common MUST but not weaken it.

---
name: packaging-distribution-guide
description: Best-practice guide for packaging and distributing a CLI/tool — build & release pipeline (cross-compile, asset naming, checksums, signing, SBOM), install.sh/install.ps1 one-liners, self-update, config/state/secrets locations, doctor diagnostics, uninstall, background service, AI-agent integration (skills, MCP, hooks, plugins) and distribution testing.
