id_prefix: CMD
title: Command surface — verbs, the init/doctor model, flags, output, agent-native (the CLI contract)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: always (every shipped binary)
---

# Command surface (CMD) — the only place that defines command names and syntax

Every project uses the same surface, so users and agents learn it once:
**`init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.**

## 1. Pick the archetype
| | **A. Single binary** (mdview, skillstation, herdr-go) | **B. Manager + runtime** (forgent: `fgctl` + `fgos`) |
|---|---|---|
| When | the product is one self-contained binary | big system: runtime tree pinned per project, several binaries, the team needs identical bits |
| `install.sh` installs | `<app>` | `<ctl>` only |
| First run | `<app> init` | `<ctl> init` (fetch + verify + activate runtime), which then runs `<app> init` |
| New version | `<app> update` (alias `upgrade`) | `<ctl> upgrade`; `<app> update` never self-updates — it forwards to or prints `<ctl> upgrade` |
| Rollback / integrity | automatic inside `update` | `<ctl> repair` (previous version), `<ctl> verify` (re-hash) |
| Manager itself | — | `<ctl> --version`, `<ctl> self-update` (one command; no re-running the installer) |

Default to A. Choose B only when A truly can't work, and write down why.

## 2. Standard verbs
```
<app> --version | version [--json]
<app> init     [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]                 first run: create + converge
<app> doctor   [--fix] [--dry-run] [--strict] [--json]      diagnose; --fix repairs
<app> status   [--json]                                     fast summary + one next command
<app> update   [--check] [--version vX.Y.Z] [--force] [--yes] [--json]     alias: upgrade   (A only)
<app> config   path|show|get|set|unset|edit|explain|check|default
<app> paths    [--json]
<app> uninstall [--purge] [--dry-run] [--yes]               alias: remove
<app> completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>
<app> connect  [<host>] [-g] [--dry-run] [--remove]         agent tools only
<app> mcp      [--http ADDR]                                MCP servers only; stdio by default
<app> service  install|uninstall|start|stop|restart|status|logs            daemons only
<ctl> init|upgrade|repair|verify|status|self-update|--version              archetype B only
```

## 3. The init / doctor model — one engine
- **CMD-01** MUST · `doctor` is the only engine that reaches the desired state. Every desired state — config file, data store, hooks, skills, MCP entries, PATH, service, permissions — is a **doctor check with a fix**. No verb writes setup state outside this engine. Avoid: forgent `setup` writing rc lines, config, hooks and skills that `doctor --fix` doesn't know about.
- **CMD-02** MUST · `doctor` is read-only. `doctor --fix` repairs what exists but has drifted or broken. It never **creates** a new workspace or project: checks that create one are marked `creates` and only run under `init`, just as `git status` never runs `git init`.
- **CMD-03** MUST · `init` = `doctor --fix` with `creates` checks enabled, then "✓ Ready" and the next step (ONB-10). It is idempotent, so re-running it is always safe. For agent tools, it detects installed hosts and connects them; with `--yes` it uses project scope. So `init --yes` alone yields a working setup.
- **CMD-04** MUST · There is no `setup` verb. Keep an old one only as a hidden alias of `init` for a deprecation window.
- **CMD-05** SHOULD · `status` runs the fast subset of the same checks and ends with exactly one next command.

## 4. Conventions
- **CMD-06** MUST · Both `--version` and `version` work; `version --json` returns the full fingerprint (VER-04).
- **CMD-07** MUST · Global flags mean the same thing on every verb: `--json`, `-y/--yes`, `--dry-run`, `-q/--quiet`, `-v/--verbose`, `--no-color` (and honour `NO_COLOR`), `-c/--config <file>`.
- **CMD-08** MUST · Exit codes, the same for every verb:
  - `0` ok;
  - `1` problems found or failed;
  - `2` usage error;
  - `10` `update --check` found an update.
- **CMD-09** MUST · **stdout carries only the requested output** (data, `--json`, protocol). Hints, progress, update notices and logs go to stderr. They are suppressed for `mcp`, for `--json`, and when stdout isn't a TTY, because a stray line breaks MCP stdio and JSON parsers.
- **CMD-10** MUST · Errors use the form Error / Why / Fix, where Fix is a copy-pasteable command. Report every validation error at once.
- **CMD-11** MUST · `--json` uses one envelope everywhere, printed on stdout even on failure:

  ```
  {"schema":1,"ok":bool,"data":…,"error":{"code","why","fix"}|null,"next":["cmd",…]}
  ```

  The `fix` and `next` commands are non-interactive (they include `--yes`) and idempotent. Keys and codes stay stable across versions; a removal needs a deprecation window.
- **CMD-12** SHOULD · Unknown verb or flag → "did you mean …?". Aliases only for names users really type (`upgrade`, `remove`); help and docs show the canonical name.
- **CMD-13** SHOULD · Internal verbs that the installer or updater calls (`--internal-print-default-config`, `--internal-merge-config`, `doctor --after-update`) are hidden from help, but stay stable, because an old binary may call a new one.
- **CMD-14** SHOULD · Keep the verb set small; a new feature becomes a flag or subcommand, not a new top-level verb. `install.sh` uses the same flag names (`--version`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--uninstall`, `--help`).

## 5. Agent-native — `--help` and `--json` are enough
Test: a user says "install <app> for me". An agent that reads only `<app> --help`, `<app> init --help`
and `<app> doctor --help` must reach a working setup without the README and without asking anyone.
- **CMD-15** MUST · Running with no arguments prints short, task-ordered help ("Get started: 1. `<app> init` 2. … 3. …").
- **CMD-16** MUST · The `--help` of `init`, `doctor`, `update`, `config` and `uninstall` is self-sufficient. Each one gives:
  - what the command does and what it changes on disk;
  - prerequisites;
  - every flag with its default;
  - 2–4 copy-paste examples, one of them non-interactive;
  - the exit codes;
  - what to run next.
- **CMD-17** MUST · Everything can run non-interactively. With no TTY, a command never waits on a prompt; it fails and names the flag to pass.
- **CMD-18** MUST · Agents follow one loop: `init --yes --json`, then while `doctor --json` is not ok, run every `fix`. The loop must finish in a bounded number of rounds.
- **CMD-19** SHOULD · The top-level `--help` has an "Agents / automation" section listing that loop and the schema location. `help --json` lists the verbs and flags.
- **CMD-20** SHOULD · `completions <shell>` and a man page are generated from the command definition and shipped in archives. None of the source projects had them.
- **CMD-21** MAY · `llms.txt` / `docs/agents.md` generated from `--help`.

---
id_prefix: UX
title: Ease — fast install, fast update, few dependencies, config easy to understand and edit
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: always
---

# Ease (UX)

## Fast install
- **UX-01** MUST · Prebuilt binaries for every common platform: linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, Windows x64. Building from source is a documented last resort.
- **UX-02** MUST · The installer finishes in seconds: one download, no compile, no bootstrapping a package manager, no questions by default.
- **UX-03** MUST · It works right after install. The command runs in a new shell, or the installer prints the one line that fixes PATH. `--version` and the first real command work with zero config.

## Fast update
- **UX-04** MUST · Updating is one command (CMD archetype table). The user never re-runs the installer, downloads by hand or edits config; the config is migrated silently.
- **UX-05** SHOULD · Quiet and quick: one small download; daemons restart themselves; MCP clients and hooks keep working without a reconnect.
- **UX-06** SHOULD · The user learns an update exists without asking: a once-a-day cached hint on stderr (CMD-09), off in CI and non-TTY, with an opt-out env var; `status` shows it too.

## Few dependencies
- **UX-07** MUST · The product needs no runtime, interpreter or system library the user has to install: a static binary with embedded assets. If something is truly unavoidable (Node for a Node CLI), doctor checks it and explains how to get it.
- **UX-08** MUST · The installer needs only `sh`, `curl` or `wget` (including busybox), `tar`, and a SHA-256 tool with fallbacks. Windows needs only PowerShell 5.1+. Optional extras such as cosign never become required.
- **UX-09** SHOULD · No root, Docker or Homebrew required; package-manager channels are extras.

## Config: easy to understand
- **UX-10** MUST · Zero-config by default; most users never open the file.
- **UX-11** MUST · When a config file exists, it explains itself:
  - The binary generates it (`config default`).
  - It shows only the commonly changed keys, each with a one-line comment: what it does, allowed values, default.
  - Advanced keys are listed commented out.
  - The format allows comments (TOML or YAML).
- **UX-12** SHOULD · Store only what differs from the defaults; `config explain <key>` shows the effective value and which layer set it.
- **UX-13** SHOULD · Human names and values: `port = 8080`, `timeout = "30s"`. No magic numbers or internal abbreviations.

## Config: easy to change (when a config file exists)
- **UX-14** MUST · `config edit` opens `$VISUAL`, else `$EDITOR`, else `vi` or `notepad`. On save it validates, shows each error with file:line and a fix, and offers to re-open. `config set` and `config unset` cover one-liners and agents.
- **UX-15** MUST · Friendly validation: the bad key, what is allowed, and "did you mean …" for typos.
- **UX-16** SHOULD · Changes apply without ceremony: a daemon reloads or restarts itself, and the CLI says what changed.
- **UX-17** MAY · A settings page in the UI that writes the same file with the same validation.

## Renames
- **UX-18** SHOULD · A rename is a migration: keep an alias or shim for a while and move dirs, env vars and agent entries automatically. Avoid: skillstation's 8-step manual migration from Skill Hub.

id_prefix: INS
title: Install scripts (install.sh / install.ps1)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: binary (or archetype-B manager) distributed outside a package manager
---

# Install scripts (INS)

Skeletons: `templates/install.sh` (tested). For PowerShell, adapt skillstation `scripts/install.ps1` (see `references.md`).

- **INS-01** MUST · Serve the installers from `releases/latest/download/install.{sh,ps1}`, version-stamped by the release (REL-08), never from raw `main`. Document the flag pass-through: `curl … | sh -s -- --version vX`.
- **INS-02** MUST · POSIX `sh`, `set -eu`, all code in functions, `main "$@"` as the last line, so a truncated `curl | sh` can't run half a script.
- **INS-03** MUST · Allow-list platform detection that follows the single naming rule (REL-02). On Windows, check `PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` first. Unsupported platforms get a pointer to the source build. MSYS/Cygwin shells are sent to `install.ps1`.
- **INS-04** MUST · Every option is both a prefixed env var and a flag: `<APP>_VERSION`, `_INSTALL_DIR`, `_RELEASE_BASE`, `_DRY_RUN`, `_NO_MODIFY_PATH`, `_YES`. Each has exactly one meaning. `--help` exists. `--version` accepts both `1.2.3` and `v1.2.3`.
- **INS-05** MUST · Resolve "latest" through `releases/latest/download/` or the redirect, never the API, to avoid rate limits.
- **INS-06** MUST · Activation order:
  1. Download into a temp dir with a trap.
  2. Verify (SEC-01, 03, 05).
  3. Run `candidate --version`.
  4. Copy into the target dir and `mv -f` over the old binary. Renaming avoids "Text file busy".
  5. On Windows, rename the running exe to `<exe>.old-<pid>` first; the binary deletes `*.old-*` on its next start.
- **INS-07** SHOULD · Put an ownership marker `.<app>-managed` (holding the version) next to the binary. Refuse to overwrite or uninstall a binary without it. Same version → no-op.
- **INS-08** SHOULD · Keep a `.rollback` copy; restore it if the activated binary fails `--version`.
- **INS-09** MUST · Default to `~/.local/bin` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\bin`. Refuse root unless `<APP>_ALLOW_ROOT=1`.
- **INS-10** MUST · Pick one PATH policy and document it:
  - **(A)** Print the exact `export` / `SetEnvironmentVariable` line.
  - **(B)** Write fenced `# >>> app >>>` blocks into bash, zsh (`$ZDOTDIR`), fish `conf.d` and `.profile`; on Windows, update `HKCU\Environment` keeping `REG_EXPAND_SZ` and broadcast `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`. Uninstall removes the blocks.
- **INS-11** SHOULD · Only an HTTP 404 may fall back to a source build; any other error fails hard. Support curl and busybox wget; busybox wget has no `--https-only`, so enforce HTTPS on the URL.
- **INS-12** MUST · The installer takes paths from the binary (`<bin> paths --json`) or is covered by a contract test. Avoid: skillstation purges `~/.config` while macOS stores config in Application Support.
- **INS-13** MUST · Keep the script small. It places the binary (or `<ctl>`), then prints the next step `<abs-path> init`. All config, secrets, service and agent setup happen in `init` (CMD-03).
- **INS-14** SHOULD · Support `--local-fixture DIR` plus a fake signature verifier, so CI can test install, re-run, upgrade, rollback, unmanaged refusal, checksum mismatch and uninstall offline.
- **INS-15** MUST · Uninstall (`--uninstall`) asks through `/dev/tty` when one exists. With no TTY, it requires `--yes`. Print the purge hint **before** removing the binary.
- **INS-16** SHOULD · Archive layout allow-list: exactly one executable `<app>` plus optional `LICENSE*`, `README*`, `completions/`, `man/`; reject anything else, including links.
- **INS-17** MUST · PowerShell 5.1: set `[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol` to TLS 1.2, verify with `Get-FileHash`, and extract with System32 `tar.exe` (Git-for-Windows tar misreads `C:`).

title: Self-update (behaviour; syntax is in 07-command-surface)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: archetype A binary, or the archetype-B manager, distributed by direct download
---

# Self-update (UPD)

- **UPD-01** MUST · Update only what our installer installed (marker file). For package-manager installs, print `brew upgrade …` or the equivalent. In archetype B, the product forwards to `<ctl> upgrade`.
- **UPD-02** MUST · Run the same checks as the installer (naming, checksum, signature, size caps, extraction) from shared constants, and report whether the signature was actually checked.
- **UPD-03** MUST · The update source comes from build metadata (`CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`, ldflags), so forks update from themselves. A base-URL env var allows tests and mirrors.
- **UPD-04** MUST · Version policy is a pure, tested function:
  - `latest` never downgrades;
  - an explicit `--version` may downgrade;
  - resolve the release once, and use it for both the comparison and the download.
- **UPD-05** MUST · Handle the real release format (extract archives). CI updates from the previous tag using the real assets (TST-03). Avoid: herdr-go writing the `.tar.gz` over the executable.
- **UPD-06** MUST · Swap procedure:
  1. Stage next to the real binary, with symlinks resolved.
  2. Require `staged --version` to equal the target.
  3. Back up the current binary.
  4. Rename the staged binary into place. On Windows, rename the running exe to `<exe>.old-<pid>` first.
  5. Roll back on any failure.
  6. On the next start, delete `*.old-*` and backups beyond the last one.
- **UPD-07** SHOULD · Post-swap work (config merge, template and skill refresh) runs inside the **new** binary: `<new> doctor --after-update`, `--internal-merge-config`.
- **UPD-08** SHOULD · Daemon update: stop → swap → migrate → start → health check (version == target). If the check fails, roll back both binary and config.
- **UPD-09** SHOULD · Under sudo, skip user-scoped steps and print what the user should run.
- **UPD-10** MAY · Archetype B: the project commits a digest pin. `<ctl> upgrade` moves the pin, `repair` rolls back, and `verify` re-hashes and quarantines bad installs (forgent `fgctl`).

title: Config, state, secrets & migrations (mechanics; UX is in 05-user-experience)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: tool has persistent config, data, cache or secrets
---

# Config & state (CFG)

- **CFG-01** MUST · Keep config, state and cache separate, using OS conventions:
  - Linux: XDG, honoured only if the value is absolute.
  - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support` (what Go's `os.UserConfigDir` returns).
  - Windows: `%APPDATA%` for config, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` for state and cache.
- **CFG-02** MUST · One override env var per root (`<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`, `<APP>_STATE_DIR`), each with one meaning; tests use them.
- **CFG-03** MUST · `paths --json` is the single source; installers, uninstall and docs use it.
- **CFG-04** MUST · Documented precedence: flag > env > project > user > default.
- **CFG-05** MUST · The binary owns the defaults (`config default`). No hand-kept example file that can drift.
- **CFG-06** MUST · Atomic writes that keep the existing file mode; the dir is 0700 when it holds anything sensitive.
- **CFG-07** MUST · Secrets live outside the config (0600 / owner-only DACL), and the binary refuses loose permissions. Service units and agent configs reference the secret's path, never its value. Generated secrets are printed once.
- **CFG-08** MUST · A corrupt config is an error (CMD-10), never silent defaults.
- **CFG-09** SHOULD · Decide on unknown keys deliberately: preserve them for user-edited files shared across versions, deny them for security config. Renamed keys are accepted through aliases.
- **CFG-10** SHOULD · An upgrade only adds missing keys: back up first, validate, and run it in the new binary.
- **CFG-11** SHOULD · Version data migrations, or put the schema version in the filename (`registry-v4.db`) so old and new binaries can coexist. Migrating a legacy dir fails closed if both the old and new dirs exist.
- **CFG-12** MAY · A committed project config can't set machine or secret keys: the schema marks keys `global-only` or `secret` (forgent).
- **CFG-13** MUST · Insecure overrides (non-loopback bind, auth off) print a warning. Never ship a fixed default token.

title: Doctor engine — check model and catalogue (verbs and init/doctor model are in 07-command-surface)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: always (doctor is the setup engine — CMD-01)
---

# Doctor engine (DOC)

- **DOC-01** MUST · Each check has:
  - a stable `code`;
  - a `status` (`ok`, `warn`, `fail` or `skip`);
  - a `critical` flag and a one-line `detail`;
  - a `fix` command;
  - an optional auto-fix function;
  - a `creates` flag (only runs under `init`, CMD-02).
- **DOC-02** MUST · `--fix` applies fixes and re-runs every check, up to N rounds. The exit code reflects the post-fix state, and each change is reported. Avoid: mdview's doctor always exits 0.
- **DOC-03** MUST · Diagnosis never writes: databases are opened read-only and nothing is created. Without a TTY, doctor never prompts.
- **DOC-04** SHOULD · Checks live in a registry, so each module registers its own checks and fixes. Each runs isolated, with a timeout. The whole of `init` is just this registry.
- **DOC-05** SHOULD · Catalogue (installed tools only; everything else is `skip`):
  - **Binary:** on PATH, is the one running, version, update available.
  - **Config:** valid; secret permissions; schema version.
  - **Service:** registered, running, live version == binary.
  - **Dependencies:** external tools at minimum versions.
  - **Endpoints:** reachable, checked without sending secrets unasked.
  - **Agent setup** (skills, instruction block, MCP entry, hooks): in sync byte-exact **and** they actually run (call the hook or MCP with harmless input and a timeout).
  - **Leftovers:** `*.old-*`, legacy files and dirs.
- **DOC-06** SHOULD · Fixes never send credentials to remote services; they print the command instead.
- **DOC-07** MAY · A hidden `--after-update` mode, called by the updater through the new binary, refreshes templates that are already installed.

id_prefix: INS
title: Install scripts (install.sh / install.ps1)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: binary (or archetype-B manager) distributed outside a package manager

# Install scripts (INS)

Skeletons: `templates/install.sh` (tested). For PowerShell, adapt skillstation `scripts/install.ps1` (see `references.md`).

- **INS-01** MUST · Serve the installers from `releases/latest/download/install.{sh,ps1}`, version-stamped by the release (REL-08), never from raw `main`. Document the flag pass-through: `curl … | sh -s -- --version vX`.
- **INS-02** MUST · POSIX `sh`, `set -eu`, all code in functions, `main "$@"` as the last line, so a truncated `curl | sh` can't run half a script.
- **INS-03** MUST · Allow-list platform detection that follows the single naming rule (REL-02). On Windows, check `PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` first. Unsupported platforms get a pointer to the source build. MSYS/Cygwin shells are sent to `install.ps1`.
- **INS-04** MUST · Every option is both a prefixed env var and a flag: `<APP>_VERSION`, `_INSTALL_DIR`, `_RELEASE_BASE`, `_DRY_RUN`, `_NO_MODIFY_PATH`, `_YES`. Each has exactly one meaning. `--help` exists. `--version` accepts both `1.2.3` and `v1.2.3`.
- **INS-05** MUST · Resolve "latest" through `releases/latest/download/` or the redirect, never the API, to avoid rate limits.
- **INS-06** MUST · Activation order:
  1. Download into a temp dir with a trap.
  2. Verify (SEC-01, 03, 05).
  3. Run `candidate --version`.
  4. Copy into the target dir and `mv -f` over the old binary. Renaming avoids "Text file busy".
  5. On Windows, rename the running exe to `<exe>.old-<pid>` first; the binary deletes `*.old-*` on its next start.
- **INS-07** SHOULD · Put an ownership marker `.<app>-managed` (holding the version) next to the binary. Refuse to overwrite or uninstall a binary without it. Same version → no-op.
- **INS-08** SHOULD · Keep a `.rollback` copy; restore it if the activated binary fails `--version`.
- **INS-09** MUST · Default to `~/.local/bin` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>\bin`. Refuse root unless `<APP>_ALLOW_ROOT=1`.
- **INS-10** MUST · Pick one PATH policy and document it:
  - **(A)** Print the exact `export` / `SetEnvironmentVariable` line.
  - **(B)** Write fenced `# >>> app >>>` blocks into bash, zsh (`$ZDOTDIR`), fish `conf.d` and `.profile`; on Windows, update `HKCU\Environment` keeping `REG_EXPAND_SZ` and broadcast `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`. Uninstall removes the blocks.
- **INS-11** SHOULD · Only an HTTP 404 may fall back to a source build; any other error fails hard. Support curl and busybox wget; busybox wget has no `--https-only`, so enforce HTTPS on the URL.
- **INS-12** MUST · The installer takes paths from the binary (`<bin> paths --json`) or is covered by a contract test. Avoid: skillstation purges `~/.config` while macOS stores config in Application Support.
- **INS-13** MUST · Keep the script small. It places the binary (or `<ctl>`), then prints the next step `<abs-path> init`. All config, secrets, service and agent setup happen in `init` (CMD-03).
- **INS-14** SHOULD · Support `--local-fixture DIR` plus a fake signature verifier, so CI can test install, re-run, upgrade, rollback, unmanaged refusal, checksum mismatch and uninstall offline.
- **INS-15** MUST · Uninstall (`--uninstall`) asks through `/dev/tty` when one exists. With no TTY, it requires `--yes`. Print the purge hint **before** removing the binary.
- **INS-16** SHOULD · Archive layout allow-list: exactly one executable `<app>` plus optional `LICENSE*`, `README*`, `completions/`, `man/`; reject anything else, including links.
- **INS-17** MUST · PowerShell 5.1: set `[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol` to TLS 1.2, verify with `Get-FileHash`, and extract with System32 `tar.exe` (Git-for-Windows tar misreads `C:`).

title: Self-update (behaviour; syntax is in 07-command-surface)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: archetype A binary, or the archetype-B manager, distributed by direct download
---

# Self-update (UPD)

- **UPD-01** MUST · Update only what our installer installed (marker file). For package-manager installs, print `brew upgrade …` or the equivalent. In archetype B, the product forwards to `<ctl> upgrade`.
- **UPD-02** MUST · Run the same checks as the installer (naming, checksum, signature, size caps, extraction) from shared constants, and report whether the signature was actually checked.
- **UPD-03** MUST · The update source comes from build metadata (`CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`, ldflags), so forks update from themselves. A base-URL env var allows tests and mirrors.
- **UPD-04** MUST · Version policy is a pure, tested function:
  - `latest` never downgrades;
  - an explicit `--version` may downgrade;
  - resolve the release once, and use it for both the comparison and the download.
- **UPD-05** MUST · Handle the real release format (extract archives). CI updates from the previous tag using the real assets (TST-03). Avoid: herdr-go writing the `.tar.gz` over the executable.
- **UPD-06** MUST · Swap procedure:
  1. Stage next to the real binary, with symlinks resolved.
  2. Require `staged --version` to equal the target.
  3. Back up the current binary.
  4. Rename the staged binary into place. On Windows, rename the running exe to `<exe>.old-<pid>` first.
  5. Roll back on any failure.
  6. On the next start, delete `*.old-*` and backups beyond the last one.
- **UPD-07** SHOULD · Post-swap work (config merge, template and skill refresh) runs inside the **new** binary: `<new> doctor --after-update`, `--internal-merge-config`.
- **UPD-08** SHOULD · Daemon update: stop → swap → migrate → start → health check (version == target). If the check fails, roll back both binary and config.
- **UPD-09** SHOULD · Under sudo, skip user-scoped steps and print what the user should run.
- **UPD-10** MAY · Archetype B: the project commits a digest pin. `<ctl> upgrade` moves the pin, `repair` rolls back, and `verify` re-hashes and quarantines bad installs (forgent `fgctl`).

id_prefix: SVC
title: Background service / daemon
tier: 2-safety
applies_when: tool runs a long-lived process (a stdio MCP server started by the client is not a daemon)
---

# Service / daemon (SVC)

- **SVC-01** MUST · `init` installs a user-level service as a doctor check:
  - Linux: `systemd --user`. `loginctl enable-linger` keeps it running after logout; it may need polkit or root on some distros, so if it is refused, tell the user.
  - macOS: a LaunchAgent (`bootstrap gui/<uid>`).
  - Windows: a per-user Scheduled Task.
- **SVC-02** MUST · `service …` (CMD) is a thin pass-through that prints the native command it runs.
- **SVC-03** MUST · Registration is idempotent: `bootout` before `bootstrap`, and conflicting legacy or dev units are disabled.
- **SVC-04** MUST · Unit files contain no secrets.
- **SVC-05** SHOULD · Restart policy:
  - systemd: `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=3`;
  - launchd: `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`;
  - Windows: a restart count, with a minimum interval of 1 min.

  Sandboxing (`ProtectSystem=strict`, `NoNewPrivileges`) in **user** units needs unprivileged user namespaces, which Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor can block. Verify the unit starts; if it doesn't, drop the sandboxing.
- **SVC-06** MUST · Bind `127.0.0.1` by default with a generated token.
- **SVC-07** SHOULD · The health endpoint reports the fingerprint. The CLI asks the live process for its version, restarts an older daemon, and never downgrades it.
- **SVC-08** SHOULD · After a swap, Linux `current_exe()` ends with ` (deleted)`; strip it before re-spawning.

id_prefix: TST
title: Testing the distribution
tier: 3-correctness
applies_when: always
---

# Testing (TST)

- **TST-01** MUST · Consumer proof: before upload, install from the built assets outside the checkout, under sh and under PowerShell 5.1 and 7.
- **TST-02** MUST · Smoke test on every OS, in this order:
  1. the one-liner;
  2. `bash -l -c '<app> --version'`;
  3. `<app> init --yes`;
  4. `doctor --strict`;
  5. service health check;
  6. uninstall;
  7. confirm the command is gone.

  Draft releases aren't served from `releases/latest/download`, so point `<APP>_RELEASE_BASE` at the draft.
- **TST-03** MUST · Upgrade from the previous tag (resolved dynamically); assert that the version changed and the config survived.
- **TST-04** MUST · Agent-native test: run CMD-18's loop non-interactively on a clean runner; it must end with `doctor` ok.
- **TST-05** SHOULD · Offline installer lifecycle using a fixture (INS-14).
- **TST-06** SHOULD · Contract test in CI checks that asset names, paths, doc links and command names agree across the workflow, installers, binary, README and `--help`.
- **TST-07** SHOULD · Unit tests cover the pure policies: version compare, platform→asset mapping, precedence, merge, and paths for each OS.
- **TST-08** SHOULD · Tests redirect HOME and the config/state dirs to temp dirs.

---
id_prefix: AGT
title: AI-agent integration (MCP, skills, hooks, instruction blocks)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: tool is meant to be used by coding agents
---

# Agent integration (AGT) — verbs `connect` / `mcp` are in 07-command-surface

- **AGT-01** MUST · Integration is a set of doctor checks with fixes. `init` connects detected hosts (CMD-03), `connect` / `connect --remove` adjust them, and uninstall reverses them. Hosts that aren't installed are skipped.
- **AGT-02** MUST · Keep the per-host adapter table in code and docs, re-checked whenever a host changes (last checked 2026-11):

  | Host | Project | User | Permissions |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `~/.claude.json` | `.claude/settings*.json` |
  | Codex | `.codex/config.toml` | `~/.codex/config.toml` | — |
  | Gemini | `.gemini/settings.json` | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | — |
- **AGT-03** MUST · Edit third-party config surgically:
  - preserve the format (`toml_edit`, key order);
  - compare-and-swap on a preimage digest;
  - back up first and keep the file mode;
  - refuse a malformed file; never overwrite it as `{}`.

  Avoid: mdview `register_json_mcp`.
- **AGT-04** MUST · Register the absolute binary path (or a stable shim) with `mcp` as the argument. Pass a token **file path**, never the token itself.
- **AGT-05** MUST · The MCP server speaks the protocol only on stdout (CMD-09). It is a thin per-call proxy to the CLI, so upgrades apply without the client reconnecting.
- **AGT-06** SHOULD · The `<!-- app:START/END -->` block in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md:
  - upserted idempotently, written through symlinks;
  - byte-exact with a template embedded in the binary (LF line endings via `.gitattributes`);
  - removed on uninstall.
- **AGT-07** SHOULD · One canonical skill source generates the per-host wrappers; doctor and CI fail on drift. Installed skill files are owned by digest: a digest from a shipped version gets upgraded, unknown content is the user's and is left alone. CI checks that the digest table covers every release.
- **AGT-08** SHOULD · Hooks are project-local and go through a stable entry point, merged fill-only. Doctor runs each hook with harmless input.
- **AGT-09** MAY · From WSL, reach the Windows desktop client with `wsl.exe -d <distro> -e <abs-bin> mcp`.
- **AGT-10** MAY · Add a narrow permission rule (`Bash(app open:*)`), removed on uninstall.

---
id_prefix: SVC
title: Background service / daemon
tier: 2-safety
applies_when: tool runs a long-lived process (a stdio MCP server started by the client is not a daemon)
---

# Service / daemon (SVC)

- **SVC-01** MUST · `init` installs a user-level service as a doctor check:
  - Linux: `systemd --user`. `loginctl enable-linger` keeps it running after logout; it may need polkit or root on some distros, so if it is refused, tell the user.
  - macOS: a LaunchAgent (`bootstrap gui/<uid>`).
  - Windows: a per-user Scheduled Task.
- **SVC-02** MUST · `service …` (CMD) is a thin pass-through that prints the native command it runs.
- **SVC-03** MUST · Registration is idempotent: `bootout` before `bootstrap`, and conflicting legacy or dev units are disabled.
- **SVC-04** MUST · Unit files contain no secrets.
- **SVC-05** SHOULD · Restart policy:
  - systemd: `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=3`;
  - launchd: `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false`;
  - Windows: a restart count, with a minimum interval of 1 min.

  Sandboxing (`ProtectSystem=strict`, `NoNewPrivileges`) in **user** units needs unprivileged user namespaces, which Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor can block. Verify the unit starts; if it doesn't, drop the sandboxing.
- **SVC-06** MUST · Bind `127.0.0.1` by default with a generated token.
- **SVC-07** SHOULD · The health endpoint reports the fingerprint. The CLI asks the live process for its version, restarts an older daemon, and never downgrades it.
- **SVC-08** SHOULD · After a swap, Linux `current_exe()` ends with ` (deleted)`; strip it before re-spawning.

---
id_prefix: TST
title: Testing the distribution
tier: 3-correctness
applies_when: always
---

# Testing (TST)

- **TST-01** MUST · Consumer proof: before upload, install from the built assets outside the checkout, under sh and under PowerShell 5.1 and 7.
- **TST-02** MUST · Smoke test on every OS, in this order:
  1. the one-liner;
  2. `bash -l -c '<app> --version'`;
  3. `<app> init --yes`;
  4. `doctor --strict`;
  5. service health check;
  6. uninstall;
  7. confirm the command is gone.

  Draft releases aren't served from `releases/latest/download`, so point `<APP>_RELEASE_BASE` at the draft.
- **TST-03** MUST · Upgrade from the previous tag (resolved dynamically); assert that the version changed and the config survived.
- **TST-04** MUST · Agent-native test: run CMD-18's loop non-interactively on a clean runner; it must end with `doctor` ok.
- **TST-05** SHOULD · Offline installer lifecycle using a fixture (INS-14).
- **TST-06** SHOULD · Contract test in CI checks that asset names, paths, doc links and command names agree across the workflow, installers, binary, README and `--help`.
- **TST-07** SHOULD · Unit tests cover the pure policies: version compare, platform→asset mapping, precedence, merge, and paths for each OS.
- **TST-08** SHOULD · Tests redirect HOME and the config/state dirs to temp dirs.

name: cs-packaging-distribution
description: Code standard (cs-*) for packaging and distributing a CLI/tool, user-experience first — README intro and quick start, one consistent command surface (init / doctor / update / config / uninstall), agent-native --help and --json, one-command install and update, minimal dependencies, easy config — then safety, correctness, speed. Covers release pipeline, checksums/signing, install.sh/install.ps1, self-update, config/state/secrets, doctor engine, uninstall, daemons, MCP/skills/hooks integration and distribution testing, with Rust/Go/Node/polyglot overlays and proven reference code from the owner's projects. Use when setting up or auditing how a project is released, installed, initialised, diagnosed, updated or removed.
---

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.
2. **Choose the archetype** (`07-command-surface.md` §1). A is a single binary with `update`; B is a manager plus a runtime. Then open the **"Start from"** row of `references.md` for the closest proven project.
3. **Select files.**
   - In `common/`, follow the read order in `00-principles.md` and keep files whose `applies_when` matches.
   - Add every language overlay whose `detect` file exists, plus `polyglot.md` if there is more than one language.
   - Add the channels in use.
   - If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
4. **Decide** using the checklist template's table, UX first:
   - tagline;
   - quick-start promise;
   - archetype and verbs;
   - install one-liner;
   - dependency budget;
   - config format.

   Then the rest. Ask only about what you can't infer.
5. **Audit.** List every MUST plus each SHOULD you adopt, with the status `done`, `todo` or `gap`. Collapse rules that don't apply to one line per file ("n/a: no daemon").
6. **Plan** tier-1 gaps first. Build order may follow dependencies (a release must exist before an installer can fetch it), but never postpone a tier-1 item for a lower tier.
7. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
8. **Implement** on request. For each rule, open its `references.md` entry and adapt that code (and `templates/`). Cite rule ids where useful.
9. **Verify** with the agent-native test (TST-04), then **feed back** lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

# Extending the skill

This skill is a long-lived playbook. Follow the priority order at the top of `SKILL.md` when adding to
it. Every lesson is classified into a tier, and no edit may make first contact, command syntax,
agent-native use, install, update or config harder for users. The only exception is a lower-tier MUST
that truly requires it, and the rule must then say why.

## Record what works
When a project proves a better way (shipped and working for users):
1. Add or update the `references.md` row that points at its code.
2. Rewrite the rule so it describes that way.

Agents follow recorded proven ways by default, so recording one is how it becomes the standard.
A pitfall seen in a real project becomes `Avoid: <project> …` at the end of the relevant rule; delete
the note once the project fixes it.

## Where things go
`SKILL.md` discovers files by listing directories, so **adding a file never requires editing `SKILL.md`**.

Repos: `github.com/vantt/<repo>`; local clones are in `~/projects/<repo>` when present. Read files with
`gh api repos/vantt/<repo>/contents/<path> --jq .content | base64 -d`, or clone with `--depth 1`.
Paths were last checked on 2026-11-02 (`sh scripts/check-references.sh`).

## Start from — the closest proven project for the new one

|---|---|---|
| Go CLI (+ MCP server, + web UI) | **skillstation** | Go, MCP proxy, most hardened release/installer/update |
| Rust CLI (+ local web viewer, MCP) | **mdview** | Rust single binary, update with smoke test, doctor/uninstall symmetry |
| Rust long-running service | **herdr-go** | user services on 3 OSes, update with health check and rollback, config merge |
| Big system, per-project pinned runtime, Node/polyglot (archetype B) | **forgent** | `fgctl` manager, digest pins, one version across Rust and Node |

| Rules | Lang | Project | Path |

| REL-06, TST-03 (upgrade from previous tag) | Rust | herdr-go | `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `scripts/generate-checksums.sh` |

| VER-05/06 | sh | herdr-go | `scripts/release.sh`, `scripts/check-version.sh`, `.githooks/pre-commit` |
| VER-05, POLY-01..03 | Node/Rust | forgent | `scripts/prepare-release.mjs`, `packages/distribution/rust/src/lib.rs` |

| INS-13, CFG-05/07, SVC-* | Rust | herdr-go | `install.sh`, `install.ps1`, `src/config/mod.rs`, `packaging/` |

| CFG-02/09 | Go | skillstation | `internal/userconfig/userconfig.go` |

| DOC-02 (re-run after fix, exit code) | Rust | herdr-go | `src/doctor/mod.rs` |
| DOC-04 (check registry) | Node | forgent | `src/setup/registrations.mjs` |
| UNI-* | Rust | mdview | `crates/mdview/src/uninstall.rs` |
| AGT-02/03/07 | Go | skillstation | `internal/hostintegration/`, `internal/systemskills/known-digests.go` |
| AGT-06/09 | Rust | mdview | `crates/mdview/src/doctor.rs` |
| AGT-07/08 | Node | forgent | `src/setup/agent-hooks.mjs`, `src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs` |

---
name: cs-packaging-distribution
description: Code standard (cs-*) for packaging and distributing a CLI/tool, user-experience first — README intro and quick start, one consistent command surface (init / doctor / update / config / uninstall), agent-native --help and --json, one-command install and update, minimal dependencies, easy config — then safety, correctness, speed. Covers release pipeline, checksums/signing, install.sh/install.ps1, self-update, config/state/secrets, doctor engine, uninstall, daemons, MCP/skills/hooks integration and distribution testing, with Rust/Go/Node/polyglot overlays and proven reference code from the owner's projects. Use when setting up or auditing how a project is released, installed, initialised, diagnosed, updated or removed.
---

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.
2. **Choose the archetype** (`07-command-surface.md` §1). A is a single binary with `update`; B is a manager plus a runtime. Then open the **"Start from"** row of `references.md` for the closest proven project.
3. **Select files.**
   - In `common/`, follow the read order in `00-principles.md` and keep files whose `applies_when` matches.
   - Add every language overlay whose `detect` file exists, plus `polyglot.md` if there is more than one language.
   - Add the channels in use.
   - If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
4. **Decide** using the checklist template's table, UX first:
   - tagline;
   - quick-start promise;
   - archetype and verbs;
   - install one-liner;
   - dependency budget;
   - config format.

   Then the rest. Ask only about what you can't infer.
5. **Audit.** List every MUST plus each SHOULD you adopt, with the status `done`, `todo` or `gap`. Collapse rules that don't apply to one line per file ("n/a: no daemon").
6. **Plan** tier-1 gaps first. Build order may follow dependencies (a release must exist before an installer can fetch it), but never postpone a tier-1 item for a lower tier.
7. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
8. **Implement** on request. For each rule, open its `references.md` entry and adapt that code (and `templates/`). Cite rule ids where useful.
9. **Verify** with the agent-native test (TST-04), then **feed back** lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

# Extending the skill

This skill is a long-lived playbook. Follow the priority order at the top of `SKILL.md` when adding to
it. Every lesson is classified into a tier, and no edit may make first contact, command syntax,
agent-native use, install, update or config harder for users. The only exception is a lower-tier MUST
that truly requires it, and the rule must then say why.

## Record what works
When a project proves a better way (shipped and working for users):
1. Add or update the `references.md` row that points at its code.
2. Rewrite the rule so it describes that way.

Agents follow recorded proven ways by default, so recording one is how it becomes the standard.
A pitfall seen in a real project becomes `Avoid: <project> …` at the end of the relevant rule; delete
the note once the project fixes it.

## Where things go
`SKILL.md` discovers files by listing directories, so **adding a file never requires editing `SKILL.md`**.

| New knowledge | Goes to |
|---|---|
| README, intro, quick start, first run | `common/03-first-contact.md` |
| command names, flags, exit codes, JSON, init/doctor model, agent-native help | `common/07-command-surface.md` (the **only** place syntax is defined) |
| install/update speed, dependencies, config ease | `common/05-user-experience.md` |
| anything else language-agnostic | the matching `common/NN-<topic>.md`, or a new file with an unused prefix, a `tier`, and an entry in the read order in `00-principles.md` |
| language specifics | `languages/<lang>.md` (copy `_template.md`) |
| a channel (brew, scoop, docker, pypi…) | `channels/<channel>.md` (copy `_template.md`) |
| proven code | a row in `references.md` |

## Rule format
```
- **<PREFIX>-<NN>** <MUST|SHOULD|MAY|DEPRECATED> · <what + key detail>. [<ids refined>]
```
- **One idea, one owner.** Before adding a rule, grep for it. Reference the existing id rather than restating it.
- **Only what agents don't already know.** Skip generic advice such as "write tests" or "use a linter".
- **Ids are permanent.** Append the next number; retire a rule with `DEPRECATED · see <id>`.
- **Levels:**
  - MUST: without it users can't install, update or configure easily, or installs break, security weakens or data is lost.
  - SHOULD: the strong default.
  - MAY: situational.

## Frontmatter
- `common/*.md`: `id_prefix`, `title`, `tier`, `applies_when`.
- `languages/*.md`: `id_prefix`, `language`, `title`, `detect`, `sources`.
- `channels/*.md`: `id_prefix`, `channel`, `title`, `applies_when`, `sources`.

## Checks

#!/bin/sh
# Validate: frontmatter keys, rule line format, unique ids, every referenced id (incl. ranges) exists.
set -eu
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
fail=0
err() { printf 'ERROR %s\n' "$*" >&2; fail=1; }
fm() { awk 'NR==1{next} /^---$/{exit} {print}' "$1"; }
need_keys() { f="$1"; shift
  head -1 "$f" | grep -qx -- '---' || { err "$f: missing frontmatter"; return 0; }
  for k in "$@"; do fm "$f" | grep -q "^$k:" || err "$f: frontmatter missing '$k'"; done; }
LIST="$(mktemp)"; IDS="$(mktemp)"; trap 'rm -f "$LIST" "$IDS"' EXIT
for f in "$ROOT"/common/*.md "$ROOT"/languages/*.md "$ROOT"/channels/*.md; do
  case "$(basename "$f")" in _*) ;; *) printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$LIST";; esac; done

while IFS= read -r f; do
  case "$f" in
    */common/*)    need_keys "$f" id_prefix title tier applies_when ;;
    */languages/*) need_keys "$f" id_prefix language title detect sources ;;
    */channels/*)  need_keys "$f" id_prefix channel title applies_when sources ;;
  esac
  prefix="$(fm "$f" | awk '/^id_prefix:/{print $2}')"
  grep -E '^- \*\*[A-Z]' "$f" | while IFS= read -r line; do
    if printf '%s\n' "$line" | grep -Eq "^- \*\*${prefix}-[0-9]{2,}\*\* (MUST|SHOULD|MAY|DEPRECATED) · "; then
      printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -E 's/^- \*\*([A-Z-]+-[0-9]+)\*\*.*/\1/' >> "$IDS"
    else printf 'ERROR %s: bad rule line: %.80s\n' "$f" "$line" >&2; echo BAD >> "$IDS"; fi
  done
done < "$LIST"
grep -q '^BAD$' "$IDS" && fail=1
dups="$(grep -v '^BAD$' "$IDS" | sort | uniq -d)"; [ -z "$dups" ] || err "duplicate rule ids: $dups"
prefixes="$(while IFS= read -r f; do fm "$f" | awk '/^id_prefix:/{print $2}'; done < "$LIST")"
dp="$(printf '%s\n' "$prefixes" | sort | uniq -d)"; [ -z "$dp" ] || err "duplicate id_prefix: $dp"

# references: single ids and ranges like CMD-13..19 / CMD-13…19 (every id in the range must exist)
alt="$(printf '%s\n' "$prefixes" | paste -sd'|' -)"
refs="$(grep -rhoE "\b($alt)-[0-9]{2,}((\.\.|…)[0-9]{2,})?" "$ROOT" --include='*.md' | sort -u)"
for r in $refs; do
  p="${r%-*}"; nums="${r##*-}"
  case "$nums" in
    *..*|*…*) a="$(printf '%s' "$nums" | sed -E 's/^([0-9]+).*/\1/')"; b="$(printf '%s' "$nums" | sed -E 's/.*[^0-9]([0-9]+)$/\1/')" ;;
    *) a="$nums"; b="$nums" ;;
  esac
  w=${#a}; i=$(expr "$a" + 0); end=$(expr "$b" + 0)
  while [ "$i" -le "$end" ]; do
    id="$(printf "%s-%0${w}d" "$p" "$i")"; grep -qx "$id" "$IDS" || err "reference $r → unknown rule $id"
    i=$((i + 1)); done
done
[ "$fail" = 0 ] && printf 'OK: %s rules, structure valid\n' "$(grep -vc '^BAD$' "$IDS")"
exit "$fail"
EOF

  done
  [ "$fail" = 0 ] || exit 1
done && echo "OK: all reference paths exist"
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# Reference installer skeleton — cs-packaging-distribution (INS-*, SEC-*, CMD-14).
# Replace APP / REPO and the naming rule in detect_target(); keep the structure.
# main "$@" is the LAST line so a truncated `curl | sh` never runs a partial script (INS-02).
set -eu

APP="myapp"
REPO="OWNER/REPO"
DEFAULT_VERSION='@APP_VERSION@'   # stamped by the release workflow (REL-08)
MARKER=".${APP}-managed"
MAX_BYTES=134217728               # 128 MiB per download (SEC-04)

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Install, upgrade or remove ${APP}.

Usage:
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh -s -- [options]

Options (each also as an env var):
  --version <vX.Y.Z>     install this version          MYAPP_VERSION      (default: this release)
  --install-dir <dir>    where the binary goes         MYAPP_INSTALL_DIR  (default: ~/.local/bin)
  --dry-run              show what would happen        MYAPP_DRY_RUN=1
  --no-modify-path       don't print PATH advice       MYAPP_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1
  --uninstall            remove the binary (keeps config and data)   MYAPP_UNINSTALL=1
  -y, --yes              don't ask for confirmation    MYAPP_YES=1
  -h, --help             show this help
Other env: MYAPP_RELEASE_BASE (mirror / draft / test fixture), MYAPP_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=1, MYAPP_ALLOW_ROOT=1

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage error.
After installing, run:  ${APP} init
EOF
}

say() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die() { say "error: $1"; [ -z "${2:-}" ] || say "  why: $2"; [ -z "${3:-}" ] || say "  fix: $3"; exit 1; }
usage_err() { say "error: $1"; say "  fix: sh install.sh --help"; exit 2; }

parse_args() {
  VERSION="${MYAPP_VERSION:-$DEFAULT_VERSION}"
  INSTALL_DIR="${MYAPP_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
  BASE="${MYAPP_RELEASE_BASE:-https://github.com/$REPO/releases}"
  DRY_RUN="${MYAPP_DRY_RUN:-0}"; NO_PATH="${MYAPP_NO_MODIFY_PATH:-0}"
  UNINSTALL="${MYAPP_UNINSTALL:-0}"; YES="${MYAPP_YES:-0}"
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --version|--install-dir)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] && [ -n "$2" ] || usage_err "$1 needs a value"
        if [ "$1" = --version ]; then VERSION="$2"; else INSTALL_DIR="$2"; fi; shift ;;
      --version=*) VERSION="${1#*=}" ;;
      --install-dir=*) INSTALL_DIR="${1#*=}" ;;
      --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
      --no-modify-path) NO_PATH=1 ;;
      --uninstall) UNINSTALL=1 ;;
      -y|--yes) YES=1 ;;
      -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
      *) usage_err "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac; shift
  done
  case "$VERSION" in @*@|v*) ;; [0-9]*) VERSION="v$VERSION" ;; esac   # accept 1.2.3 and v1.2.3
  case "$BASE" in https://*) ;; *) die "release base must be https: $BASE" ;; esac
  if [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] && [ "${MYAPP_ALLOW_ROOT:-0}" != 1 ]; then
    die "refusing to run as root" "installs are per-user" "re-run as your user, or set MYAPP_ALLOW_ROOT=1"
  fi
}

detect_target() {   # single naming rule (REL-02) — keep in sync with the release workflow and the updater
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux) os=linux ;; Darwin) os=darwin ;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) die "Windows shell detected" "" "irm https://github.com/$REPO/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex" ;;
    *) die "unsupported OS: $(uname -s)" "no prebuilt binary" "build from source — see README" ;;

Xong cả ba phần: đổi tên, chuẩn hóa init/doctor, và sửa theo review. Script kiểm tra cấu trúc chạy qua với 212 rule. Script mới `check-references.sh` xác nhận mọi đường dẫn code mẫu đều có thật trên GitHub. `install.sh` mẫu đã được test lại bằng `dash`.

**1. Đổi tên thành `cs-packaging-distribution`**
- Thư mục và symlink `~/.claude/skills/cs-packaging-distribution` đều đã đổi.
- Description mở đầu bằng "Code standard (cs-*)", sẵn cho cả họ `cs-` sau này.

**2. Chuẩn hóa init / doctor / setup** (`common/07-command-surface.md`)
- **Doctor là bộ máy duy nhất.** Mọi trạng thái mong muốn đều là một check có fix. Không lệnh nào được ghi file thiết lập ngoài doctor.
- **`doctor`** chỉ đọc. **`doctor --fix`** chỉ sửa những gì đã có, không bao giờ biến một thư mục bất kỳ thành dự án.
- **`init` = `doctor --fix` + được phép tạo mới,** rồi in "✓ Ready". Với công cụ cho agent, `init` tự kết nối các agent đã cài, nên chỉ `init --yes` là xong.
- **Không có `setup`.** Lệnh cũ chỉ được giữ làm alias ẩn của `init`.
- **Bảng hai kiểu phân phối:**
  - **A, một binary:** `<app> update`, gõ `upgrade` cũng được.
  - **B, bộ cài + runtime:** `<ctl> init`, `upgrade`, `repair`, `verify`, `self-update`. Còn `<app> update` chỉ chuyển sang `<ctl> upgrade`.

- **Khuôn `--json` chung** cho mọi dự án: `{schema, ok, data, error:{code,why,fix}, next}`.
- **`references.md`** có bảng "Start from" theo loại dự án, cột ngôn ngữ, và trỏ tới MCP proxy của skillstation. GO-03 giờ bảo bắt đầu từ pipeline của skillstation.
- **Bỏ trùng lặp:**
  - Principles chỉ còn định nghĩa các tầng và 8 rule dùng chung.
  - Cú pháp lệnh chỉ nằm trong file CMD.
  - Thứ tự ưu tiên chỉ viết một lần, ở đầu SKILL.md.
- **Checklist ngắn lại:** chỉ liệt kê MUST và những SHOULD được chọn; phần không áp dụng gộp thành một dòng mỗi file. Agent integration được chuyển lên tầng UX.
- **`install.sh`** giờ có:
  - `--help`;
  - hỏi xác nhận qua `/dev/tty`, và khi không có terminal thì yêu cầu `--yes`;

1. Chuyển những gì `fgos setup` đang làm riêng (dòng source trong rc, file config, git hooks, Claude hook, copy skills) thành các check có fix của doctor. Sau đó `setup` chỉ còn là alias của `init`.

**Lớp 1: script tự động cho những gì kiểm được bằng máy**

Thêm `scripts/audit-project.sh <repo-dir> [<binary>]`. Mỗi kết quả gắn với ID rule và có trạng thái `PASS` / `FAIL` / `MANUAL`. Agent điền thẳng kết quả vào checklist. Ví dụ những thứ kiểm được:

| Nhóm | Kiểm tra |
|---|---|
| First contact | README có one-liner `releases/latest/download/install.sh`, có mục Quick start nằm trước phần kiến trúc (ONB-04/07) |
| install.sh | có `set -eu`, dòng cuối là `main "$@"`, có `--help`, `--version`, `--uninstall`, chạy được `sh -n` (INS-02/04) |
| Bộ lệnh | `--version` và `version` đều chạy; `init`, `doctor`, `update`, `uninstall` đều có `--help` (CMD-06/16) |
| Agent-native | `--help` có ví dụ và exit code; cờ sai trả exit 2; `doctor --json` đúng khuôn `{schema,ok,data,error,next}`; stdout với `--json` không lẫn dòng thừa (CMD-08/09/11) |
| Không hỏi khi không có terminal | `init` chạy với stdin `/dev/null` thì không treo (CMD-17) |
| Release | workflow có tạo checksums, action pin theo SHA, có job kiểm tra tag khớp version (REL-06/10, VER-02) |

Nên giới hạn khoảng 25–30 check, chỉ cho các MUST thật sự đo được. Script này cũng có thể chép sang CI của từng dự án để giữ chuẩn về sau.

**Lớp 2: agent kiểm tra những gì cần phán đoán**

Script không đánh giá được tagline có hay không, quick start có thật sự xong trong 2 phút không, hay `--help` có đủ để tự làm không. Phần này cần agent:

- **Review first contact:** agent đọc màn hình đầu README như một người dùng mới, chấm theo ONB-01..08.

---
name: cs-packaging-distribution
description: Code standard (cs-*) for packaging and distributing a CLI/tool, user-experience first — README intro and quick start, one consistent command surface (init / doctor / update / config / uninstall), agent-native --help and --json, one-command install and update, minimal dependencies, easy config — then safety, correctness, speed. Covers release pipeline, checksums/signing, install.sh/install.ps1, self-update, config/state/secrets, doctor engine, uninstall, daemons, MCP/skills/hooks integration and distribution testing, with Rust/Go/Node/polyglot overlays and proven reference code from the owner's projects. Use when setting up or auditing how a project is released, installed, initialised, diagnosed, updated or removed.
---

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.
2. **Choose the archetype** (`07-command-surface.md` §1). A is a single binary with `update`; B is a manager plus a runtime. Then open the **"Start from"** row of `references.md` for the closest proven project.
3. **Select files.**
   - In `common/`, follow the read order in `00-principles.md` and keep files whose `applies_when` matches.
   - Add every language overlay whose `detect` file exists, plus `polyglot.md` if there is more than one language.
   - Add the channels in use.
   - If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
4. **Decide** using the checklist template's table, UX first:
   - tagline;
   - quick-start promise;
   - archetype and verbs;
   - install one-liner;
   - dependency budget;
   - config format.

   Then the rest. Ask only about what you can't infer.
5. **Audit.** List every MUST plus each SHOULD you adopt, with the status `done`, `todo` or `gap`. Collapse rules that don't apply to one line per file ("n/a: no daemon").
6. **Plan** tier-1 gaps first. Build order may follow dependencies (a release must exist before an installer can fetch it), but never postpone a tier-1 item for a lower tier.
7. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
8. **Implement** on request. For each rule, open its `references.md` entry and adapt that code (and `templates/`). Cite rule ids where useful.
9. **Verify** with the agent-native test (TST-04), then **feed back** lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
