## How to run commands

schema_version: 1
labels: [code-standard]
topics: [packaging, distribution, installation, self-update, release-engineering, cli-ux, agent-native, supply-chain]
technologies: [rust, go, node, posix-sh, powershell, github-actions, cosign, mcp]
routing:
  operations: [design, implement, review]
  min_scope: multi_step
  triggers:
    - install.sh one-line installer for a CLI
    - self-update or upgrade command for a binary
    - init and doctor commands for a tool
    - GitHub release pipeline with checksums and signing
    - agent-native --help and --json for setup
    - README intro and quick start for installing a tool
    - register MCP server in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini on install
    - uninstall command that keeps user config
    - config file location and paths for a CLI
    - packaging and distribution audit of a CLI
  examples:
    - Set up install.sh, self-update and a release workflow for this Go CLI so users can install it with one curl command
    - Audit how this Rust tool is installed, updated and diagnosed, and list the gaps
    - Design init and doctor commands an agent can run by itself just from --help
    - Rewrite the README intro and quick start so a new user gets the tool working in two minutes
    - Add an uninstall command that removes the MCP registration and PATH entry but keeps the user's config
  not_for:
    - Docker image or Kubernetes deployment for a web service
    - deploying a web app to a server or cloud
    - publishing a library package other code imports
    - reviewing code architecture or test quality
    - implementing the product's own features
    - installing or using an existing tool as an end user
  counter_examples:
    - install skillstation on my laptop
    - write a Dockerfile for the API service
    - review this pull request for bugs

Đúng như anh thấy, skill hiện **không có `skill.yaml`**. Vì vậy trên hub nó không có topic, operation hay routing nào. Bản gửi lên hub từ xa cũng không nhận cờ routing, nên muốn những thông tin này đi kèm thì phải viết sẵn vào `skill.yaml` trong thư mục skill.

Bản nháp ở `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-vantt-projects-devops/6a207191-5a2b-4956-9f48-9efae5fe3b0f/scratchpad/skill.yaml`:

**Trước:** không có gì.
**Sau:**

| Trường | Giá trị |
|---|---|
| `labels` | `code-standard` (để gom họ cs-* sau này) |
| `topics` | packaging, distribution, installation, self-update, release-engineering, cli-ux, agent-native, supply-chain |
| `technologies` | rust, go, node, posix-sh, powershell, github-actions, cosign, mcp |
| `operations` | design, implement, review |
| `min_scope` | `multi_step`: chỉ gợi ý skill cho việc lớn, không gợi ý cho một chỉnh sửa lẻ |
| `triggers` (10) | install.sh one-line installer for a CLI · self-update or upgrade command for a binary · init and doctor commands for a tool · GitHub release pipeline with checksums and signing · agent-native --help and --json for setup · README intro and quick start for installing a tool · register MCP server in Claude Code, Codex or Gemini on install · uninstall command that keeps user config · config file location and paths for a CLI · packaging and distribution audit of a CLI |
| `examples` (5) | giống bản nháp trước: Go CLI install/update/release · audit Rust tool · init/doctor cho agent · README quick start · uninstall giữ config |
| `not_for` (6) | Docker/K8s cho web service · deploy web app · publish thư viện · review kiến trúc/test (để dành cho cs-* khác) · làm tính năng sản phẩm · **cài hoặc dùng một tool có sẵn với tư cách người dùng** |
| `counter_examples` (3) | "install skillstation on my laptop" · "write a Dockerfile for the API service" · "review this pull request for bugs" |

Tôi thêm `not_for` "cài hoặc dùng một tool có sẵn" và câu đối chứng "install skillstation on my laptop" vì skill có rất nhiều chữ "install". Thiếu hai mục này thì một yêu cầu cài tool bình thường cũng có thể bị gợi ý skill này.

Anh đồng ý thì tôi sẽ:
1. Chép file vào `skills/cs-packaging-distribution/skill.yaml`.
2. Gửi lại lên hub (xem trước rồi chạy `--yes`). Lần gửi này tạo một bản gửi mới thay cho `SUB-01M6NAX34J7THX6HNF2M584W8V`, trên hub chỉ cần duyệt bản mới nhất.

Hub đang chạy bản skillstation cũ, chưa có `skill lint`, nên tôi chưa kiểm tra được trigger có trùng với skill khác không. Sau khi duyệt, tôi sẽ thử bằng `skill_resolve`.

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.
2. **Choose the archetype** (`07-command-surface.md` §1). A is a single binary with `update`; B is a manager plus a runtime. Then open the **"Start from"** row of `references.md` for the closest proven project.
3. **Select files.**
   - In `common/`, follow the read order in `00-principles.md` and keep files whose `applies_when` matches.
   - Add every language overlay whose `detect` file exists, plus `polyglot.md` if there is more than one language.
   - Add the channels in use.
   - If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
4. **Decide** using the checklist template's table, UX first:
   - tagline;
   - quick-start promise;
   - archetype and verbs;
   - install one-liner;
   - dependency budget;
   - config format.

   Then the rest. Ask only about what you can't infer.
5. **Audit.** List every MUST plus each SHOULD you adopt, with the status `done`, `todo` or `gap`. Collapse rules that don't apply to one line per file ("n/a: no daemon").
6. **Plan** tier-1 gaps first. Build order may follow dependencies (a release must exist before an installer can fetch it), but never postpone a tier-1 item for a lower tier.
7. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
8. **Implement** on request. For each rule, open its `references.md` entry and adapt that code (and `templates/`). Cite rule ids where useful.
9. **Verify** (below), update the checklist statuses, then **feed back** lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
   When auditing an existing project, run Verify first to learn where it stands.

## Verify — run these yourself; each failure is a `gap` on that rule
Work in a temp HOME (`HOME=$(mktemp -d)`) so the user's real setup is never touched. `x` is the binary.

| # | Run / inspect | Pass when | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | README first screen | tagline about user pain/gain; quick start before internals; promise "from nothing to … in N min, you need …" | ONB-01/04/06 |
| 2 | `tail -1 install.sh`; `grep -n 'set -eu' install.sh`; `sh -n install.sh`; `sh install.sh --help` | `main "$@"` is last; strict mode; parses; help exits 0 | INS-02/04 |
| 3 | `x --version`; `x version --json` | both work; JSON has the fingerprint | CMD-06 |
| 4 | `x`; `x --help` | task-ordered "Get started" steps; an "Agents / automation" section | CMD-15/19 |
| 5 | `x init --help`; `x doctor --help`; `x update --help`; `x uninstall --help` | each covers: what it changes, flags + defaults, examples incl. non-interactive, exit codes, next step | CMD-16 |
| 6 | `x --bogus; echo $?` | exit 2 + "did you mean" / help hint | CMD-08/12 |
| 7 | `x init --yes --json </dev/null` | finishes without waiting; JSON envelope `{schema,ok,data,error,next}`; nothing but JSON on stdout | CMD-03/09/11/17 |
| 8 | `x doctor --json; echo $?` then `x doctor --fix --yes` | read-only first; exit 0 only when healthy; `fix` / `next` are runnable commands | CMD-02, DOC-02 |
| 9 | `x init --yes` again | idempotent: "nothing to do", no changes | CMD-03, PRN-05 |
| 10 | `x update --check; echo $?` (A) or `<ctl> --version` + `<ctl> upgrade --help` (B) | update path exists, exit codes per CMD-08 | CMD §1 |
| 11 | release workflow | checksums job needs all builds; tag == version gate; actions pinned by SHA | REL-06/10, VER-02 |
| 12 | **Agent-native test:** start a fresh subagent with no README access and only the instruction "install x from <release url> and get it working, using only its --help and --json output" | it reaches `doctor` ok without asking anyone | TST-04 |

Steps 1 and 12 need judgment; the rest are mechanical. Report results as a table (rule, pass/gap, evidence).

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.
2. **Choose the archetype** (`07-command-surface.md` §1). A is a single binary with `update`; B is a manager plus a runtime. Then open the **"Start from"** row of `references.md` for the closest proven project.
3. **Select files.**
   - In `common/`, follow the read order in `00-principles.md` and keep files whose `applies_when` matches.
   - Add every language overlay whose `detect` file exists, plus `polyglot.md` if there is more than one language.
   - Add the channels in use.
   - If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
4. **Decide** using the checklist template's table, UX first:
   - tagline;
   - quick-start promise;
   - archetype and verbs;
   - install one-liner;
   - dependency budget;
   - config format.

   Then the rest. Ask only about what you can't infer.
5. **Audit.** List every MUST plus each SHOULD you adopt, with the status `done`, `todo` or `gap`. Collapse rules that don't apply to one line per file ("n/a: no daemon").
6. **Plan** tier-1 gaps first. Build order may follow dependencies (a release must exist before an installer can fetch it), but never postpone a tier-1 item for a lower tier.
7. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
8. **Implement** on request. For each rule, open its `references.md` entry and adapt that code (and `templates/`). Cite rule ids where useful.
9. **Verify** (below), update the checklist statuses, then **feed back** lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
   When auditing an existing project, run Verify first to learn where it stands.

## Verify — run these yourself; each failure is a `gap` on that rule
Work in a temp HOME (`HOME=$(mktemp -d)`) so the user's real setup is never touched. `x` is the binary.

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.

3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.

- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.

- `agent-native --help and --json output for a CLI`

Khi duyệt, máy hub vẫn sẽ hiện 11 cảnh báo bảo mật như lần trước, đều là chữ trong tài liệu và mẫu installer, không phải lệnh skill tự chạy.

**Về câu hỏi skill hỗ trợ:**
- **`skillstation-send`**: tôi làm theo phần "Improve routing" của skill này. Example là 3–5 câu như người thật gõ; trigger nêu rõ đối tượng; not_for là việc gần giống nhưng thuộc skill khác. Tôi cũng làm theo quy trình gửi của nó: xem trước, quét bảo mật, chờ anh đồng ý rồi mới `--yes`.
- **Quy tắc của `skill-curator`**: skill này không chạy được trên máy này, nên tôi đọc thẳng file hướng dẫn của nó trong bản clone repo skillstation để lấy quy tắc. Quy tắc giống như trong `skillstation-send`.
- **Mã nguồn skillstation, không phải skill**: `skillstation-send` không nói `skill.yaml` có những trường nào, nên tôi đọc mã nguồn để biết. Đó là các trường `operations`, `topics`, `technologies`, `labels`, `min_scope`, `counter_examples`, và giá trị `multi_step`.
- **`skill_get`**: tôi dùng để xem routing đang có trên hub, nhờ đó giữ nguyên các mục cũ.

Có một bước tôi đã bỏ qua. Theo hướng dẫn của skillstation, tôi phải gọi `skill_resolve` khi bắt đầu việc này để hub chọn skill, nhưng tôi đã dùng thẳng `skillstation-send`. Kết quả không đổi vì nó đúng là skill dành cho việc này, nhưng lần sau tôi sẽ gọi `skill_resolve` trước.

Duyệt xong anh báo tôi. Tôi sẽ gọi `skill_resolve` với 5 câu example và 3 câu counter_example để kiểm tra mỗi câu ra đúng skill.

content.text:
Bản đang **active** trên hub không phải bản vừa gửi. Đó là bản của một lần duyệt trước đó.

Tôi so bản hub đang phục vụ (bản mà `skill_get` tải về máy này) với thư mục skill ở đây:
- **Nội dung giống hệt.** Chỉ khác một dòng trống mà hub tự chèn sau phần frontmatter của `SKILL.md`.
- **Routing trên hub đúng là bản tôi soạn**, gồm 9 trigger, 5 example và 5 not_for. Lúc trước tôi đưa routing này kèm lệnh `skillstation skill review SUB-01M6DMW0CATJGWRG5C15R2J1D4 --trigger …`.
- **Không có `skill.yaml`**, vì tôi mới tạo file này cho lần gửi gần nhất.

Vậy là đã có người duyệt một bản gửi trước trên máy hub, kèm routing đó. Rất có thể là `SUB-01M6DMW0…`, duyệt bằng chính lệnh tôi đưa, có thể qua curator hoặc qua trang web. Hub tạo skill mới bằng một lần chạy duyệt + approve + activate, nên skill lên active ngay. Từ máy này tôi không xem được lịch sử duyệt, nên không biết chắc ai duyệt và duyệt bản nào. Anh xem trên máy hub bằng `skillstation skill show cs-packaging-distribution --verbose`, hoặc ở mục lịch sử trên trang web.

Bản mới `SUB-01M6NB8WMEJCZHFQ8RGPR0PZ2F` vẫn **đang chờ duyệt**. Trước khi bản này được duyệt, hub tiếp tục dùng bản active hiện tại, chưa có operations hay topics.

Thêm một điều: thư mục skill ở đây vẫn giữ thời gian sửa đổi là ngày 2/11. Vì vậy nếu lúc trước anh "vừa chỉnh xong" ở một chỗ khác thì các chỉnh sửa đó chưa nằm trong bản gửi. Ba bản gửi đều có cùng nội dung hướng dẫn; bản cuối chỉ khác là có thêm `skill.yaml`.

content.text:
Đúng vậy. Trên hub, bản gửi chờ duyệt (`SUB-…`) và skill đang active là hai thứ tách riêng. Bản gửi chỉ gắn vào skill khi được áp dụng lúc duyệt. Vì thế trang của skill vẫn hiện bản cũ là active và không cho biết đang có bản thay thế chờ duyệt. Người xem phải tự vào **Waiting for review** mới thấy.

Đây là một thiếu sót về UX. Người mở trang skill sẽ tưởng bản đang chạy là mới nhất, và dễ quên duyệt bản mới. Ở đây có ba bản gửi cho cùng một skill, nên càng dễ duyệt nhầm bản cũ.

Tôi đề xuất sửa phía skillstation như sau:
- **Trên trang skill:** hiện một dải thông báo, ví dụ "1 update waiting for review (SUB-…, sent 14:53 from <máy>)", kèm nút đi thẳng tới trang duyệt.
- **Trong danh sách skill:** thêm nhãn "update pending" cạnh skill có bản chờ duyệt.
- **Khi có nhiều bản cùng chờ:** gom chúng lại, chỉ đề xuất bản mới nhất và cho bỏ các bản cũ chỉ bằng một thao tác.
- **Trong CLI:** `skillstation status` và `skill show <id>` cũng nên hiện dòng "update waiting for review".

Tôi chưa đọc mã web UI của skillstation, nên chưa biết chắc hiện tại có chỗ nào khác đã hiện thông tin này hay không. Anh muốn tôi soạn issue cho `vantt/skillstation` gồm ý này và lỗi gợi ý cờ `--user` lúc trước không? Tôi sẽ đưa nội dung cho anh xem trước rồi mới tạo.

content.text:
Tôi chưa bắt tay làm phần UI được. Có ba điều anh cần biết.

**1. Không có skill `ak:frontend-development` trên máy này.**
- Không có trong danh sách skill của phiên, trong `~/.claude` hay `~/.agents`, và hub cũng báo `not_found`.
- Tôi thử nhờ hub tìm skill phù hợp cho việc này bằng `skill_resolve`. Lần đầu nó trả về **`cs-packaging-distribution`** với độ tin cậy medium, tức là chọn nhầm. Tôi từ chối và hỏi lại thì hub báo không có skill nào khớp.
- Máy này cũng không có repo skillstation trong `~/projects`. Chỉ có một bản clone tạm trong thư mục scratchpad, không dùng để làm việc thật được.

Anh chọn giúp: (a) cài AgentKit hoặc chỉ cho tôi chỗ để skill đó, hoặc (b) tôi làm luôn không cần skill: clone `vantt/skillstation` vào `~/projects/skillstation`, sửa trên một nhánh mới rồi mở PR.

**2. Việc chọn nhầm ở trên là bằng chứng routing đang quá rộng.** Một việc frontend thuần túy vẫn bị chuyển sang skill đóng gói và phát hành. Hub đã trừ điểm vì `not_for` nhưng skill vẫn thắng. Bản `skill.yaml` mới đã thêm `operations` và `min_scope`. Tôi đề nghị thêm một mục `not_for: build or change a web UI or frontend page` rồi gửi lại lên hub. Anh đồng ý thì tôi làm.

**3. Về `skillstation-send`: anh nhận xét đúng.** Lần này tôi gặp các thiếu sót sau:
- **Không xem được metadata hiện tại từ máy khách.** `skill show` bị từ chối khi hub nằm ở máy khác. `skill_get` chỉ trả về triggers, examples và not_for, không có operations, topics, technologies hay min_scope. Vì vậy tôi đã khẳng định nhầm là "skill chưa có routing".
- **Skill không nói `skill.yaml` có những trường nào.** Nó chỉ nhắc triggers, examples và not_for. Tôi phải đọc mã nguồn skillstation mới biết các trường `operations`, `topics`, `technologies`, `labels`, `min_scope` và `counter_examples`.
- **Không có lệnh kéo routing đang có trên hub về `skill.yaml`.** Chỉ `checkout` hay `pull` mới kéo về, mà các lệnh đó dùng cho skill đã checkout từ trước.
- **Lệnh kiểm tra routing `lint` phụ thuộc phiên bản skillstation trên máy hub.** Hub đang chạy bản cũ nên lệnh này không chạy được.
- **Không có bước xem trước kết quả chọn skill.** Đã có `skill_resolve` nhưng skill không hướng dẫn dùng nó để thử các câu ví dụ.

Hai việc này có thể gộp vào một issue cho `vantt/skillstation`: dải thông báo "update waiting for review" trên web, và quy trình quản lý metadata trong `skillstation-send` gồm hiện metadata hiện tại, liệt kê đủ các trường, kéo routing về và thử bằng `skill_resolve`. Nếu anh chọn (b), tôi soạn issue cho anh xem trước rồi làm luôn phần UI trong cùng nhánh.

content.content:
# Agent Instructions

When sections conflict, Project Specifics wins over Skillstation, and both win
over the generic Engineering Rules.

## Project Specifics

### Layout and authority
- Go module: binary in `cmd/skillstation`, application services in `internal/app`,
  delivery surfaces in `internal/delivery/{cli,mcpserver,web}`; the React UI
  lives in `web/` and is embedded from `internal/delivery/web/dist`.
- Architecture decisions: `docs/design/01..07` (Vietnamese), entry point
  `docs/design/01-system-architecture.md`. `archive/final.md` is the
  historical pre-V1 decision record, not authority.
  Public contracts: `docs/contracts/` and JSON schemas in `schemas/`.
- Bundled system skills, installed in `.agents/skills/<id>/` with a generated
  Claude Code wrapper in `.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`:
  - curator (hub folder only, for the hub's owner): edit `system-skills/curator/SKILL.md`;
  - skillstation-send (every project and user scope, never the hub folder; how an agent sends,
    checks and fixes a skill): edit `system-skills/send/SKILL.md`;
  - distill-lab (hub folder only): edit `.agents/skills/distill-lab/` (SKILL.md
    and the Node script `scripts/distill.mjs` with js-yaml 4.3.2 vendored in
    `scripts/lib/`). `.claude/skills/distill-lab/SKILL.md` is the generated
    wrapper, not a source;
  - skill-audit (hub folder only): edit `.agents/skills/skill-audit/` (SKILL.md,
    the rule list `rules/rules.txt` and the Node script `scripts/audit.mjs`).
    A new rule needs a `match:` and a `clean:` example;
    `node .agents/skills/skill-audit/scripts/audit.mjs --self-test` runs them.
  All four are mirrored into `internal/systemskills/` and kept in sync by tests;
  after editing curator or skillstation-send copy the file to
  `internal/systemskills/curator/SKILL.md` or `internal/systemskills/send/SKILL.md`;
  after editing distill-lab run
  `rm -r internal/systemskills/distill-lab && cp -R .agents/skills/distill-lab internal/systemskills/distill-lab`,
  and likewise for skill-audit.
  To update js-yaml, follow the steps in the header comment of
  `scripts/distill.mjs` (pinned tarball, registry sha512 check, digests in
  `internal/systemskills/distill_script_test.go`, `npm run notices` in `web/`).
  Release rule: once a release shipped a bundled file or a wrapper render, a
  later change to it needs the shipped digest in
  `internal/systemskills/known-digests.go` or
  `internal/hostintegration/known-wrappers.go`; the tag-derived tests
  (`SKILLSTATION_REQUIRE_TAGS=1`) fail until it is there.
- Active plans go in `plans/`; completed plans move to `archive/plans/`.

### Single authority

Each concept has one owner. Before adding storage, a helper, a digest or a
parser, look the concept up here and search its owner first; a second
implementation needs a row here saying why.

| Concept | The one place |
|---|---|
| Skill metadata files (`skill.yaml`, `.meta/hub.yaml`, older layouts) | `internal/skillmeta` (`Read`, `Merge`, `Split`, `HubKeys`, and `SetKey` to set or remove one top-level key while keeping the order and comments of the others); per-skill hub state such as status, approval or audit is a key in `.meta/hub.yaml`, never a new file |
| Writing canonical hub files | `mutation.PlanMutation` and `mutation.ConfirmMutationWithOptions`, called from an `internal/app` service |
| Skill content digest (approval and audit) | `skillruntime.ContentDigest`, computed for a hub skill by `app.SkillService.ContentTrustFor` |
| Distributed bundle digest | `skillruntime.ManifestDigest` |
| Digest of bytes in the `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` form, and checking that form | `internal/digest` (`Bytes`, `Valid`), a leaf package any layer may import |
| Skill audit record | `app.SkillAuditService`; scripts use `skillstation skill audit-status` and `skill audit-record` |
| Static security scan of a skill folder (rule format, matching, rules digest) | `internal/skillscan`, run by `app.SkillScanService` (`skillstation skill scan`) with the rules of `.agents/skills/skill-audit/rules/rules.txt`; `audit.mjs` still carries its own scan until it calls the binary, and `TestFolderScanFindsWhatTheScriptFinds` and `TestRulesDigestMatchesTheScript` hold the two equal |
| A skill's sources | `app.SourceService`; agents and scripts use `skillstation source ...` |
| Which sources a skill learns from (the `sources` block of `.meta/distill.yaml`) | `distill.ReadSources` and `distill.WithSources` for the file, `app.readSkillSourceLinks` for the hub; the hub writes the block through `PlanMutation`, the distill-lab script keeps it as it is. The source record in `sources/catalog/<id>.yaml` stays the authority on the address |
| Atomic file write | `internal/fsutil` (`WriteFileAtomic`, `WriteNewFileAtomic` for a file that must not exist yet, `Replace`, `SyncDir`) |
| Skill and collection id form | `skillmeta.ValidSkillID` |
| Skill ids reserved for system skills | `systemskills.IsSystemSkillID`; `mutation` refuses a new hub skill under such an id (`refuseReservedSkillIDs`) and leaves one the hub already holds, since newer system ids were free when it was added. `canonical` validation also refuses the two curator ids in any hub: they were reserved from the start |
| Finding a skill in the hub by id, and listing the ids | `skill.Load` and `skill.IDs`; they refuse a symbolic link in place of a collection, a skill folder or its metadata, and an id filed in two collections, and give `skill.ErrNotFound` for a missing id or `skills/` folder. `skill.ReadEntrypoint` reads `SKILL.md` and the app walkers read the other files with the same rules (`skill.ErrInvalidSkillTree`). `app.takenSkillIDs` is wider on purpose: the ids a new skill must not take, folders without metadata and catalog ids included |
| Approving a third-party skill's content | the `internal/app` service compares the digest the person was shown with the content it applies: `SkillCommitService.Apply` (`ApproveContentDigest`) and `SkillService.PreviewSubmissionApproval`; a delivery surface only passes the digest on |
| Withholding unreviewed third-party content from agents | `skillruntime.Evaluate` decides; the snapshots apply it to active skills and `app.SkillService.InactiveSkillReviewGate` to the others |
| Hub folder discovery | `workspace.Discover`; the CLI resolves `--workspace` in `internal/delivery/cli/workspace_resolve.go` |
| ERROR/WHY/FIX errors | `internal/app/errors.go`, mapped by `app.ClassifyError`; every code is in `docs/contracts/error-codes.md` and the enum of `schemas/error-envelope.schema.json` (`TestErrorCodeRegistryMatchesContract`) |
| The hub's user service (unit name, unit path, restart command) | `app.HubServiceUnitPath` and `app.InstalledHubService`; `serve --install-service` writes it, `update` and `doctor --fix` restart it |
| Import rules between layers | `internal/archtest`; a delivery surface matches the errors of the lower packages through the names in `internal/app/sentinels.go` |

Bundled scripts (`.agents/skills/*/scripts`) ask the binary (`--json`) for hub
facts instead of reading hub metadata or hashing skill files themselves.

### Commands
- `make check` before committing: gofmt check, vet, lint (new issues only),
  deadcode (no new unreachable function), full test suite. While working, run
  `make lint` and `make deadcode` after each change; they are quick and
  `internal/archtest` holds the import rules between layers. `make vulncheck`

# Agent Instructions

When sections conflict, Project Specifics wins over Skillstation, and both win
over the generic Engineering Rules.

## Project Specifics

### Layout and authority
- Go module: binary in `cmd/skillstation`, application services in `internal/app`,
  delivery surfaces in `internal/delivery/{cli,mcpserver,web}`; the React UI
  lives in `web/` and is embedded from `internal/delivery/web/dist`.
- Architecture decisions: `docs/design/01..07` (Vietnamese), entry point
  `docs/design/01-system-architecture.md`. `archive/final.md` is the
  historical pre-V1 decision record, not authority.
  Public contracts: `docs/contracts/` and JSON schemas in `schemas/`.
- Bundled system skills, installed in `.agents/skills/<id>/` with a generated
  Claude Code wrapper in `.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`:
  - curator (hub folder only, for the hub's owner): edit `system-skills/curator/SKILL.md`;
  - skillstation-send (every project and user scope, never the hub folder; how an agent sends,
    checks and fixes a skill): edit `system-skills/send/SKILL.md`;
  - distill-lab (hub folder only): edit `.agents/skills/distill-lab/` (SKILL.md
    and the Node script `scripts/distill.mjs` with js-yaml 4.3.2 vendored in
    `scripts/lib/`). `.claude/skills/distill-lab/SKILL.md` is the generated
    wrapper, not a source;
  - skill-audit (hub folder only): edit `.agents/skills/skill-audit/` (SKILL.md,
    the rule list `rules/rules.txt` and the Node script `scripts/audit.mjs`).
    A new rule needs a `match:` and a `clean:` example;
    `node .agents/skills/skill-audit/scripts/audit.mjs --self-test` runs them.
  All four are mirrored into `internal/systemskills/` and kept in sync by tests;
  after editing curator or skillstation-send copy the file to
  `internal/systemskills/curator/SKILL.md` or `internal/systemskills/send/SKILL.md`;
  after editing distill-lab run
  `rm -r internal/systemskills/distill-lab && cp -R .agents/skills/distill-lab internal/systemskills/distill-lab`,
  and likewise for skill-audit.
  To update js-yaml, follow the steps in the header comment of
  `scripts/distill.mjs` (pinned tarball, registry sha512 check, digests in
  `internal/systemskills/distill_script_test.go`, `npm run notices` in `web/`).
  Release rule: once a release shipped a bundled file or a wrapper render, a
  later change to it needs the shipped digest in
  `internal/systemskills/known-digests.go` or
  `internal/hostintegration/known-wrappers.go`; the tag-derived tests
  (`SKILLSTATION_REQUIRE_TAGS=1`) fail until it is there.
- Active plans go in `plans/`; completed plans move to `archive/plans/`.

### Single authority

Each concept has one owner. Before adding storage, a helper, a digest or a
parser, look the concept up here and search its owner first; a second
implementation needs a row here saying why.

| Concept | The one place |
|---|---|
| Skill metadata files (`skill.yaml`, `.meta/hub.yaml`, older layouts) | `internal/skillmeta` (`Read`, `Merge`, `Split`, `HubKeys`, and `SetKey` to set or remove one top-level key while keeping the order and comments of the others); per-skill hub state such as status, approval or audit is a key in `.meta/hub.yaml`, never a new file |
| Writing canonical hub files | `mutation.PlanMutation` and `mutation.ConfirmMutationWithOptions`, called from an `internal/app` service |
| Skill content digest (approval and audit) | `skillruntime.ContentDigest`, computed for a hub skill by `app.SkillService.ContentTrustFor` |
| Distributed bundle digest | `skillruntime.ManifestDigest` |
| Digest of bytes in the `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` form, and checking that form | `internal/digest` (`Bytes`, `Valid`), a leaf package any layer may import |
| Skill audit record | `app.SkillAuditService`; scripts use `skillstation skill audit-status` and `skill audit-record` |
| Static security scan of a skill folder (rule format, matching, rules digest) | `internal/skillscan`, run by `app.SkillScanService` (`skillstation skill scan`) with the rules of `.agents/skills/skill-audit/rules/rules.txt`; `audit.mjs` still carries its own scan until it calls the binary, and `TestFolderScanFindsWhatTheScriptFinds` and `TestRulesDigestMatchesTheScript` hold the two equal |
| A skill's sources | `app.SourceService`; agents and scripts use `skillstation source ...` |
| Which sources a skill learns from (the `sources` block of `.meta/distill.yaml`) | `distill.ReadSources` and `distill.WithSources` for the file, `app.readSkillSourceLinks` for the hub; the hub writes the block through `PlanMutation`, the distill-lab script keeps it as it is. The source record in `sources/catalog/<id>.yaml` stays the authority on the address |
| Atomic file write | `internal/fsutil` (`WriteFileAtomic`, `WriteNewFileAtomic` for a file that must not exist yet, `Replace`, `SyncDir`) |
| Skill and collection id form | `skillmeta.ValidSkillID` |
| Skill ids reserved for system skills | `systemskills.IsSystemSkillID`; `mutation` refuses a new hub skill under such an id (`refuseReservedSkillIDs`) and leaves one the hub already holds, since newer system ids were free when it was added. `canonical` validation also refuses the two curator ids in any hub: they were reserved from the start |
| Finding a skill in the hub by id, and listing the ids | `skill.Load` and `skill.IDs`; they refuse a symbolic link in place of a collection, a skill folder or its metadata, and an id filed in two collections, and give `skill.ErrNotFound` for a missing id or `skills/` folder. `skill.ReadEntrypoint` reads `SKILL.md` and the app walkers read the other files with the same rules (`skill.ErrInvalidSkillTree`). `app.takenSkillIDs` is wider on purpose: the ids a new skill must not take, folders without metadata and catalog ids included |
| Approving a third-party skill's content | the `internal/app` service compares the digest the person was shown with the content it applies: `SkillCommitService.Apply` (`ApproveContentDigest`) and `SkillService.PreviewSubmissionApproval`; a delivery surface only passes the digest on |
| Withholding unreviewed third-party content from agents | `skillruntime.Evaluate` decides; the snapshots apply it to active skills and `app.SkillService.InactiveSkillReviewGate` to the others |
| Hub folder discovery | `workspace.Discover`; the CLI resolves `--workspace` in `internal/delivery/cli/workspace_resolve.go` |
| ERROR/WHY/FIX errors | `internal/app/errors.go`, mapped by `app.ClassifyError`; every code is in `docs/contracts/error-codes.md` and the enum of `schemas/error-envelope.schema.json` (`TestErrorCodeRegistryMatchesContract`) |
| The hub's user service (unit name, unit path, restart command) | `app.HubServiceUnitPath` and `app.InstalledHubService`; `serve --install-service` writes it, `update` and `doctor --fix` restart it |
| Import rules between layers | `internal/archtest`; a delivery surface matches the errors of the lower packages through the names in `internal/app/sentinels.go` |

Bundled scripts (`.agents/skills/*/scripts`) ask the binary (`--json`) for hub
facts instead of reading hub metadata or hashing skill files themselves.

### Commands
- `make check` before committing: gofmt check, vet, lint (new issues only),
  deadcode (no new unreachable function), full test suite. While working, run
  `make lint` and `make deadcode` after each change; they are quick and
  `internal/archtest` holds the import rules between layers. `make vulncheck`

Đã làm xong phần giao diện trên nhánh `feat/web-pending-submission-notice` trong `~/projects/skillstation`. Toàn bộ 229 test của web đều qua, kiểm tra kiểu, lint và build cũng sạch. Tôi chưa commit hay đẩy lên GitHub, chờ anh xem trước.

**Những gì đã đổi:**
- **Trang chi tiết skill:** khi có bản gửi đang chờ duyệt, trang hiện dòng thông báo màu cảnh báo, ví dụ *"An update to this skill is waiting for review: SUB-…, sent 2026-11-05 from <máy>."*, kèm nút **Review it →** dẫn tới bản mới nhất. Nếu còn bản cũ hơn thì có thêm câu "2 older submissions are also waiting…" và nút **Discard older**. Nút này hỏi xác nhận rồi mới bỏ các bản cũ, bản mới nhất vẫn nằm chờ duyệt.
- **Danh sách skill:** skill nào có bản chờ duyệt thì có nhãn **Update waiting for review** cạnh trạng thái.
- **Mục Waiting for review:** bản nào đã có bản mới hơn cho cùng skill thì gắn nhãn **Older · a newer submission is waiting**.

Bản mới nhất được xác định theo mã `SUB-…`, vì mã này có thứ tự theo thời gian gửi. Tôi không sửa backend, chỉ đọc danh sách chờ duyệt mà hub đã có sẵn.

Code chính nằm ở:
- `web/src/domain/pending-submissions.ts`
- `web/src/screens/skill-detail/PendingSubmissionsNote.tsx`

Mỗi phần đều có test riêng.

Vài chỗ cần lưu ý:
- Skill `ak-frontend-development` có trong `.claude/skills/` của dự án nhưng chưa nạp vào phiên này, nên tôi đọc thẳng file `SKILL.md` của nó và làm theo.
- Phía CLI (`skillstation status` và `skill show` báo có bản chờ duyệt) là code Go, tôi chưa làm.
- Tôi chưa kiểm tra bằng cách mở web thật trên trình duyệt, chỉ mới chạy test.

**Về metadata, câu hỏi "folder này phải có sẵn skill cs-* kèm meta rồi chứ":** hiện chưa, vì cách skillstation đang chạy:
- `skills/cs-packaging-distribution` trong devops là thư mục gốc anh tự viết. Đây không phải bản checkout từ hub, bản xem trước có ghi `checked_out: false`.
- Routing do người duyệt đặt chỉ được lưu trên hub và không bao giờ chép ngược về thư mục đã gửi. Vì thế trước hôm nay thư mục này không có `skill.yaml`.
- Giờ thư mục đã có `skill.yaml` do tôi viết, giữ nguyên routing của hub và thêm metadata. Nhưng hai bên vẫn không tự đồng bộ: sửa trên hub thì thư mục không biết.

Theo tôi đây là lỗ hổng thiết kế của skillstation và nên đưa vào issue: sau khi bản gửi được duyệt, thư mục gửi đi phải được liên kết với hub, như một bản checkout, để `skill pull` kéo được metadata về. Từ giờ tới lúc đó, cách tạm là chờ anh duyệt `SUB-01M6NB8WMEJCZHFQ8RGPR0PZ2F` xong rồi chạy `skillstation skill checkout cs-packaging-distribution`. Lệnh này ghi một bản kèm `skill.yaml` của hub vào `.agents/skills/cs-packaging-distribution/`.

**Còn cần anh quyết định:**
1. Có commit và mở PR cho nhánh `feat/web-pending-submission-notice` không?
2. Sau khi duyệt và checkout sẽ có hai bản của skill. Anh muốn lấy bản checkout trong `.agents/skills/` làm bản làm việc chính thay cho `skills/cs-packaging-distribution` không?
3. Có soạn issue cho `vantt/skillstation` gồm ba ý không: phần CLI báo có bản chờ duyệt, quy trình quản lý metadata trong `skillstation-send`, và liên kết thư mục gửi với hub sau khi duyệt?

- advisor: Use this agent to run the interview-driven `ak-advise` advisory workflow in an isolated context on the strongest available model. It scouts, interviews the user one question at a time until the requirements and expected outcome are locked, relays a visual preview of that outcome for the user to confirm, then delivers honest advice (what to do, what to avoid, better alternatives, benefits, trade-offs, a work checklist, success metrics, and a handoff brief). Because a Claude Code subagent cannot call `AskUserQuestion` itself, this agent relays each interview question back to the orchestrator and is re-spawned with the user's answer. Examples: - - (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Write, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore), Edit)
- brainstormer: Use this agent when you need to brainstorm software solutions, evaluate architectural approaches, or debate technical decisions before implementation. Examples: - - - (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage)
- code-reviewer: Comprehensive code review with scout-based edge case detection. Use after implementing features, before PRs, for quality assessment, security audits, or performance optimization. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Write, Edit)
- code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore))
- debugger: Use this agent when you need to investigate issues, analyze system behavior, diagnose performance problems, examine database structures, collect and analyze logs from servers or CI/CD pipelines, run tests for debugging purposes, or optimize system performance. This includes troubleshooting errors, identifying bottlenecks, analyzing failed deployments, investigating test failures, and creating diagnostic reports. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore), Task(kongming))
- docs-manager: Use this agent to create, reconcile, or audit evidence-backed project documentation for both people and AI collaborators without imposing a fixed docs layout, while honouring an explicit route the repository or the user supplies. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore))
- fullstack-developer: Execute implementation phases from parallel plans. Handles backend (Node.js, APIs, databases), frontend (React, TypeScript), and infrastructure tasks. Designed for parallel execution with strict file ownership boundaries. Use when implementing a specific phase from `the engineer plan skill --parallel` output. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore), Task(kongming))
- git-manager: Stage, commit, and push code changes with conventional commits. Use when user says "commit", "push", or finishes a feature/fix. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, PowerShell, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage)
- journal-writer: Use this agent when:
- A test suite fails repeatedly despite multiple fix attempts
- A critical bug is discovered in production or staging
- An implementation approach proves fundamentally flawed and requires complete redesign
- External dependencies (APIs, services, libraries) cause blocking issues
- Performance bottlenecks are discovered that significantly impact user experience
- Security vulnerabilities are identified
- Database migrations fail or cause data integrity issues
- CI/CD pipelines break unexpectedly
- Integration conflicts arise between major system components
- Technical debt reaches a critical threshold requiring immediate attention
- A feature implementation takes significantly longer than estimated
- Architectural decisions prove problematic in practice (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage)
- kongming: Autonomous counsel from the strongest model (`fable`) in one run — no session model switch, no user interview. Mention `@kongming` from a lower tier (opus/sonnet) or spawn it from a stuck subagent for hard design, debugging, or trade-off calls. Advisory-only; returns advice, not code. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, Write, Task(Explore), Edit)
- planner: Use this agent when you need to research, analyze, and create comprehensive implementation plans for new features, system architectures, or complex technical solutions. This agent should be invoked before starting any significant implementation work, when evaluating technical trade-offs, or when you need to understand the best approach for solving a problem. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore), Task(researcher), Task(kongming))
- project-manager: Use this agent when you need comprehensive project oversight and coordination. (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, WebSearch, BashOutput, KillBash, ListMcpResourcesTool, ReadMcpResourceTool, SendMessage)

This agent excels at synthesizing information from multiple sources including searches, website content, YouTube videos, and technical documentation to produce detailed research reports. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Write, Edit)
- tester: Use this agent when you need to validate code quality through testing, including running unit and integration tests, analyzing test coverage, validating error handling, checking performance requirements, or verifying build processes. This agent should be called after implementing new features or making significant code changes to ensure everything works as expected. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore), Task(kongming))
- ui-ux-designer: Use this agent when the user needs UI/UX design work including interface designs, wireframes, design systems, user research, responsive layouts, animations, or design documentation. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch, WebSearch, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList, SendMessage, Task(Explore), Task(researcher))

The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- ak-advise: Interview until user and agent share the outcome picture, preview it, then give evidence-backed advice. - Invoke for second opinions or plan pressure-tests before planning; implementation goes to a delivery workflow.
- ak-agent-browser: Automate tool-managed browsers with agent-browser for snapshots, clicks, forms and browser testing. - Invoke for browser automation; real Chrome account state needs chrome-profile.
- ak-agentize: Expose existing code or APIs as an agent-friendly CLI, MCP server, or both. - Invoke to ship code as a tool for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or skills.sh.
- ak-agentkit: Route AgentKit work by classifying the task, chaining installed skills and spawning subagents at trigger points; also operate the ak CLI. - Invoke at the start of multi-step work, when the right skill is unclear, or when the next action is an ak subcommand.
- ak-ai-artist: Generate mockups, brand visuals and concept art via Nano Banana in search, creative or wild mode, with styles like Ukiyo-e and Bento grid. - Invoke for visual assets or prompt search.
- ak-ai-multimodal: Analyze and generate image, audio, video and document content, falling back from native vision to the Multix CLI and live provider catalogs. - Invoke for media generation, transcription or OCR the model cannot do.
- ak-ask: Answer technical and architecture questions on design decisions, best practices or solution comparisons. - Invoke for analysis-only answers before changing code.
- ak-atoz: Take a request A to Z: lock scope via ak-advise, collect all prerequisites first, then run parallel sub-sessions on a GitHub issue until each Done-means item is verified. - Invoke for one upfront confirmation, no check-ins; advice or preflight only goes to ak-advise or ak-goal-warmup.
- ak-autoresearch: Route bounded, goal-directed iteration to the AgentKit skill that owns the desired outcome. - Invoke when repeated, verified iterations should improve a measurable result.
- ak-backend-development: Implement server code in Node.js, Python or Go (Express, NestJS, FastAPI, Django): endpoints, services, data access, auth, tests. - Invoke for handlers, slow endpoints or N+1 queries; schema-only design is ak-databases.
- ak-better-auth: Add Better Auth (TypeScript): email/password, OAuth (Google, GitHub), 2FA/MFA, passkeys/WebAuthn, sessions, RBAC, rate limiting. - Invoke when setting up or extending an app's authentication.
- ak-bootstrap: Bootstrap web, mobile, CLI, API, MCP, WebMCP or library projects via ak-cook, ak-code-review, ak-enhance-ux-ax --auto and optional verified release; no planning. - Invoke to start from scratch in auto, full, fast or parallel mode; --ask locks scope via ak-advise.
- ak-brainstorm: Turn unclear intent into an accepted outcome and compare viable approaches before delivery. - Use when opening multi-step delivery or picking between viable fixes.
- ak-bro: Restate the assistant's last message in simpler, shorter, jargon-free language. - Use when the user says ak-bro, simplify that, or say it plainly.
- ak-chrome-profile: Drive a real Google Chrome profile via Chrome DevTools MCP with the chrome-profile CLI, deterministic profile discovery and URL-anchor tab selection. - Invoke when automation needs the user's own cookies or account.
- ak-code-review: Review code for bugs, regressions, maintainability, reliability and verification gaps with evidence. - Invoke for pending changes, a PR number, a commit hash or a codebase scan.
- ak-codex-goal: Guide long-running Codex /goal work to a verifiable stop condition, not generic iteration loops or multi-CLI orchestration. - Use for goal mode, durable objectives or autonomous multi-turn runs.
- ak-coding-level: Set the user's coding experience level to tune explanation depth, code complexity and response format; only on an explicit user request. - Invoke only when the user explicitly asks to set or change their coding level; never infer one.
- ak-context-engineering: Manage context, task budgets, compaction and model choice from outcome evidence, plus memory and agent systems. - Invoke for token waste, context left, usage limits, long tasks, forgetful sessions or benchmark cost.
- ak-cook: Implement features, plans and fixes through a structured workflow. - Invoke to implement known scope after requirements are clear.
- ak-copywriting: Write conversion copy with headline templates, email patterns, landing page structures, CTA optimization and style extraction. - Invoke for high-converting copy or a style from assets/writing-styles/.
- ak-cti-expert: Analyze threat intel and OSINT: domain and tenant recon, breach checks, username/email/phone lookups, image forensics, blockchain tracing, darknet checks. - Invoke for exposure reviews, CVE lookup, threat models or reports.
- ak-databases: Design schemas and SQL/NoSQL queries for MongoDB and PostgreSQL: aggregation, indexes, migrations, replication, performance, psql CLI. - Invoke when database design, not app code, is the main work.

- ak-xia: Extract, compare, port or adapt a feature from a GitHub or local repository into the current project. - Invoke to port another repo's feature; triggers: 'port from', 'clone feature from', 'like how X does it', 'xia'.

Cả 5 lỗi có **chung một nguyên nhân**: các test chưa cách ly hết khỏi máy thật. Chúng đọc phải cấu hình Codex và Gemini thật của anh, mà cấu hình này mới được ghi lúc 14:46 hôm nay khi anh chạy `skillstation connect --global`. Code của skillstation không sai, và commit web của tôi cũng không liên quan.

**Cơ chế gây lỗi**
1. `TestMain` đổi `HOME` và các biến `XDG_*` sang thư mục tạm, nhưng không đổi thư mục làm việc. Test vẫn chạy trong `~/projects/skillstation/internal/delivery/cli`.
2. Lệnh `status` và `doctor` đi ngược từ thư mục làm việc lên các thư mục cha để tìm cấu hình của dự án. Khi tới `/home/vantt`, chúng gặp `~/.codex/config.toml` và `~/.gemini/settings.json`, đều đang trỏ tới hub `http://100.93.158.78:7420`.
3. Vì HOME lúc này là thư mục tạm, code không nhận ra `/home/vantt` là thư mục nhà. Nó coi hai file trên là cấu hình của một dự án tên "/home/vantt", nên kết quả có thêm phần *"This project (/home/vantt) uses the hub at …"*.
4. Phần đó so đường dẫn lệnh đã đăng ký (`skillstation` thật) với binary đang chạy (binary test), thấy khác nhau, báo **Connection files FAILED** rồi gợi ý *"Next: reconnect this project to the hub"*.

**Từng test lỗi ra sao**

| Test | Kỳ vọng | Bị lỗi vì |
|---|---|---|
| `TestDoctorReportsAMissingGitIdentity` | `doctor` trên hub đã có danh tính git thì thoát mã 0 | thoát mã 1 do dòng Connection files FAILED |
| `TestStatusSaysTheIndexIsBehindAfterAHandEditAndDoesNotFail` | `status` báo chỉ mục tìm kiếm cũ, nhưng không có chữ `FAILED` | kết quả có chữ `FAILED` |
| `TestStatusNeverCallsACommittedHubNew` | hub có bản nháp thì `status` không nhắc tới `connect` | kết quả có lời gợi ý `skillstation connect …` |
| `TestStatusSuggestsRunnableCreateCommandBUG17` | hub rỗng thì bước tiếp theo gợi ý `skillstation skill create` | bước tiếp theo bị thay bằng "reconnect this project" |
| `TestSkillMutationHintsPrintTheCommitCommandStatusPrints` | `status` in ra lệnh commit giống gợi ý sau `skill activate` | `status` gợi ý reconnect nên không có lệnh commit |

**Bằng chứng**
- Kết quả của cả 5 test đều có phần "This project (/home/vantt) …".
- `~/.codex/config.toml` và `~/.gemini/settings.json` được sửa lúc 14:46 hôm nay và đều có địa chỉ hub.
- Lỗi xảy ra y hệt trên `main` trước commit của tôi.
- Trên máy CI không có hai file này nên không bị lỗi.
- Đổi HOME khi chạy test cũng không hết lỗi, vì nguyên nhân là thư mục làm việc chứ không phải HOME.

**Cách sửa đề xuất (chưa làm):** sửa ở phần dựng môi trường test. Có hai hướng:
- Cho `TestMain` chạy test từ một thư mục tạm, để việc dò lên thư mục cha không bao giờ chạm tới thư mục nhà thật. Cần kiểm tra trước xem có test nào dùng đường dẫn tương đối tới `testdata`.
- Hoặc cho việc dò lên thư mục cha dừng ở thư mục nhà thật.

Hướng đầu gọn hơn. Tôi chưa kiểm tra người dùng thật có gặp lỗi này không, nhưng khả năng thấp: khi HOME đúng là `/home/vantt`, code nhận ra đó là thư mục nhà nên không coi các file trên là cấu hình dự án.

CI trên GitHub cho commit `185b75d` (phần thông báo "update waiting for review" trên web) **đã qua hết**. Kết quả gồm bước Web UI, bộ test Verify trên Ubuntu, macOS và Windows, lint, fuzz, kiểm tra installer, và build chéo cho 6 nền tảng.

# `momentry config --project`: per-project settings through the config command

Date: 2026-11-05. Branch `worktree-agent-aefd62d6c55487f8d`, commit `de173ef` on top of `main` 8a6a8e0.

## Outcome

`momentry config show|get|set|unset --project` (current repo, or `--repo DIR`) reads and changes every per-project
setting. Each key goes through the writer the web UI already calls, so there is no second implementation.
`pause`/`resume` are kept as shortcuts and now call the same writer as `config set paused true|false --project`.
No `init --box` was added.

## Keys

| Key (`--project`) | Writer (shared with UI) | Stored in | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `box` | `setProjectBox` | inside repo: `.momentry.json` (relative); outside: `projects.json` | `.`, `..`, `../x`, repo itself, folders containing it refused; leading `~` expanded; unset removes the machine folder first, then the repo file's |
| `repo` | `write({scope:'project'})` | `.momentry.json` | needs an observed repo |
| `budget.dailyUsd` | `setProjectBudget` | user config `budget.projects[root]` | number >= 0; unset falls back to the general budget (shown as `…, chung mọi dự án`) |
| `private` | `setPrivateProject` | user config `privacy.privateProjects` | true/false (1/0) |
| `paused` | `Projects.setPaused` | `projects.json` | `true` needs an observed repo (same rule as `pause`) |

Sources shown by `show --project`: `repo`, `dự án trên máy này`, `người dùng`, `mặc định`, `env MOMENTRY_BOX`.
Writes into `.momentry.json` (box inside, repo) are refused for a repo that is not on (`not-observed`, fix
`momentry init`), so config never turns a repo on by side effect. A machine folder for `box` can be set before init.

Other errors: a shared key with `--project` gives `config-not-project`; a typo gives `config-unknown-key` with a
suggestion; a project key without `--project` gives `config-project-only`; `path`, `default` and `privacy-add` with
`--project` exit 2. Writers got an optional `dryRun` so `--dry-run` validates and reports the target file without
writing.

## Examples

```sh
momentry config set box ~/Documents/momentry-chuyen --project
momentry config set budget.dailyUsd 1 --project --repo ~/code/du-an
momentry config show --project --json
momentry config unset box --project --dry-run
momentry config set paused true --project      # same as: momentry pause
```

## One behaviour change beyond the CLI

`budget.dailyUsd` was added to `USER_ONLY` in `lib/config.mjs`. Before, a cloned repo's `.momentry.json` could set
`budget.dailyUsd` and raise the general daily cap while working in that repo, which contradicts the existing rule
that a repo cannot raise what it may spend. It is now dropped from the repo file and reported in `cfg.ignored`. The UI
only ever wrote it to the user config, so nothing that the UI produced is affected.

## Files

- `lib/config-cmd.mjs`: `PROJECT_KEYS`, `showProject`, `writeProject`, `--project` routing in `runConfig`, a `dryRun` option on the three writers, and a hint on project-only keys.
- `lib/cli.mjs`: `config` passes `--project`; `pause`/`resume` call `writeProject`.
- `lib/commands.mjs`: `--project` flag, help, examples, exit codes; the pause/resume summaries name the config key.
- `lib/config.mjs`: `budget.dailyUsd` user-only.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` (regenerated), `docs/installation.md` (per-project table and examples under "Khoá cấu hình"), `docs/development.md` (new "Cài đặt" rule: every setting goes through `momentry config`, and the UI uses the same writers).
- `test/config-project.test.mjs`: 9 tests. They cover each key (set/get/unset/show, source), box inside and outside the repo, refusals, dry run, the repo file being unable to set machine-only keys, the pause shortcut matching the config key, and the UI and CLI seeing each other's writes.

## Verification

`node --test test/*.test.mjs` passes 335 of 335 (326 existing and 9 new).

    feat(config): per-project settings through momentry config --project
    
    `config show|get|set|unset --project` (current repo or --repo DIR) covers
    box, repo, budget.dailyUsd, private and paused, each through the writer the

id_prefix: CFG
title: Config, state, secrets & migrations (mechanics; UX is in 05-user-experience)
tier: 1-ux
applies_when: tool has persistent config, data, cache or secrets
---

# Config & state (CFG)

- **CFG-01** MUST · Keep config, state and cache separate, using OS conventions:
  - Linux: XDG, honoured only if the value is absolute.
  - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support` (what Go's `os.UserConfigDir` returns).
  - Windows: `%APPDATA%` for config, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` for state and cache.
- **CFG-02** MUST · One override env var per root (`<APP>_CONFIG_DIR`, `<APP>_STATE_DIR`), each with one meaning; tests use them.
- **CFG-03** MUST · `paths --json` is the single source; installers, uninstall and docs use it.
- **CFG-04** MUST · Documented precedence: flag > env > project > user > default.
- **CFG-05** MUST · The binary owns the defaults (`config default`). No hand-kept example file that can drift.
- **CFG-06** MUST · Atomic writes that keep the existing file mode; the dir is 0700 when it holds anything sensitive.
- **CFG-07** MUST · Secrets live outside the config (0600 / owner-only DACL), and the binary refuses loose permissions. Service units and agent configs reference the secret's path, never its value. Generated secrets are printed once.
- **CFG-08** MUST · A corrupt config is an error (CMD-10), never silent defaults.
- **CFG-09** SHOULD · Decide on unknown keys deliberately: preserve them for user-edited files shared across versions, deny them for security config. Renamed keys are accepted through aliases.
- **CFG-10** SHOULD · An upgrade only adds missing keys: back up first, validate, and run it in the new binary.
- **CFG-11** SHOULD · Version data migrations, or put the schema version in the filename (`registry-v4.db`) so old and new binaries can coexist. Migrating a legacy dir fails closed if both the old and new dirs exist.
- **CFG-12** MAY · A committed project config can't set machine or secret keys: the schema marks keys `global-only` or `secret` (forgent).
- **CFG-13** MUST · Insecure overrides (non-loopback bind, auth off) print a warning. Never ship a fixed default token.

common/00-principles.md:29:- **PRN-08** SHOULD · Respect privilege: no user-scoped steps as root; never widen permissions; secrets 0600, outside the main config.

Avoid: forgent `setup` writing rc lines, config, hooks and skills that `doctor --fix` doesn't know about.

common/05-user-experience.md:3:title: Ease — fast install, fast update, few dependencies, config easy to understand and edit
common/05-user-experience.md:13:- **UX-03** MUST · It works right after install. The command runs in a new shell, or the installer prints the one line that fixes PATH. `--version` and the first real command work with zero config.
common/05-user-experience.md:16:- **UX-04** MUST · Updating is one command (CMD archetype table). The user never re-runs the installer, downloads by hand or edits config; the config is migrated silently.
common/05-user-experience.md:26:- **UX-10** MUST · Zero-config by default; most users never open the file.
common/05-user-experience.md:27:- **UX-11** MUST · When a config file exists, it explains itself:
common/05-user-experience.md:28:  - The binary generates it (`config default`).
common/05-user-experience.md:32:- **UX-12** SHOULD · Store only what differs from the defaults; `config explain <key>` shows the effective value and which layer set it.
common/05-user-experience.md:35:## Config: easy to change (when a config file exists)
common/05-user-experience.md:36:- **UX-14** MUST · `config edit` opens `$VISUAL`, else `$EDITOR`, else `vi` or `notepad`. On save it validates, shows each error with file:line and a fix, and offers to re-open. `config set` and `config unset` cover one-liners and agents.

**Chưa có đủ.** Skill `cs-packaging-distribution` mới có các mảnh rời về config. Quy tắc chính của momentry là *"mọi cài đặt chỉ đổi qua `config`, kể cả cài đặt riêng từng dự án"* thì skill chưa có.

**Quy tắc mới bên momentry**

Quy tắc được thêm ở commit `de173ef` hôm nay, ghi trong mục "Cài đặt" của `docs/development.md`:
1. **Chỉ một cửa:** mọi cài đặt đổi qua `momentry config show|get|set|unset`. Không thêm cờ lẻ ở lệnh khác, ví dụ không có `init --box`. Khoá mới khai báo trong schema (cài đặt chung) hoặc trong `PROJECT_KEYS` (cài đặt riêng dự án).
2. **Cài đặt riêng dự án dùng cùng bộ lệnh, chỉ thêm cờ:** `--project`, hoặc `--repo DIR` để chỉ định repo. `show --project` in từng khoá kèm nơi đặt giá trị: repo, máy này, người dùng, mặc định hay biến môi trường. Lỗi có mã riêng, ví dụ khoá chỉ dành cho dự án mà quên `--project` thì báo `config-project-only`; gõ sai tên khoá thì báo `config-unknown-key` kèm gợi ý.
3. **Giao diện web gọi đúng các hàm ghi của CLI.** Không có bản ghi thứ hai, nên mỗi quy tắc chỉ nằm ở một chỗ.
4. **Lệnh tắt chỉ là lối vào khác của khoá config.** `pause`/`resume` gọi đúng hàm ghi của `config set paused true|false --project`, và phần help ghi rõ tên khoá.
5. **Khoá chỉ của máy không bao giờ ghi vào file của repo.** `.momentry.json` có ghi `paused`, `private` hay `budget` cũng bị bỏ qua, nên repo clone về không tự nâng ngân sách được.
6. **Config không tự bật dự án.** Ghi vào repo chưa `init` thì bị từ chối, kèm lời gợi ý chạy `momentry init`.

**Đối chiếu với skill**

| Ý của momentry | Skill hiện có | Đánh giá |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Chỉ một cửa `config`, không cờ lẻ | Khối lệnh chuẩn có `config path\|show\|get\|set\|unset\|edit\|…`; UX-14 nói `set`/`unset` dùng cho lệnh một dòng và cho agent | **Thiếu** quy tắc cấm cờ lẻ và lệnh riêng cho từng cài đặt |
| 2. Cài đặt dự án qua `--project`/`--repo`, `show` ghi nguồn | CFG-04 có thứ tự ưu tiên flag > env > project > user > default; UX-12 có `config explain <key>` cho biết tầng nào đặt giá trị | **Thiếu** cú pháp phạm vi `--project` và mã lỗi khi dùng sai phạm vi |
| 3. Giao diện gọi đúng hàm ghi của CLI | UX-17 (mức MAY): giao diện ghi *cùng file, cùng cách kiểm tra* | **Yếu hơn**: cùng file không bảo đảm cùng code |
| 4. Lệnh tắt gọi cùng hàm ghi, help ghi tên khoá | Không có | **Thiếu** |
| 5. Khoá của máy không vào file repo; repo không nâng được giới hạn | CFG-12 (mức MAY): config dự án không đặt được khoá của máy hay bí mật | **Có, nhưng mức quá thấp**, và chưa nói tới việc repo nâng giới hạn |
| 6. Config không tự bật dự án | CMD-01 nói chung là không lệnh nào ghi trạng thái cài đặt ngoài `doctor` | **Thiếu** câu cụ thể cho `config` |
| `--dry-run` cho thấy file sẽ bị ghi; gợi ý khi gõ sai khoá | CMD-07, UX-15 | Đã có |

**Đề xuất bổ sung (chưa sửa skill)**

Theo `CONTRIBUTING.md`, cú pháp lệnh chỉ được định nghĩa ở `07-command-surface.md`.
- **CMD-22 MUST:** mọi cài đặt đổi qua `config`. Các lệnh khác không nhận cờ cài đặt. Lệnh tắt như `pause` chỉ là bí danh gọi cùng hàm ghi và phải ghi tên khoá trong help.
- **CMD-23 SHOULD:** phạm vi dự án dùng cùng các động từ cộng `--project [--repo DIR]`. `show` in nguồn của từng khoá. Dùng sai phạm vi thì báo lỗi kèm cách sửa.
- **Nâng CFG-12 từ MAY lên MUST** và mở rộng: khoá của máy, khoá bí mật và khoá giới hạn chi tiêu không bao giờ được ghi vào hay đọc từ file của repo; khoá bị bỏ qua thì phải báo ra. Thêm: config không tự bật dự án.
- **Sửa UX-17:** giao diện gọi đúng hàm ghi của CLI, không chỉ ghi cùng file.
- **`references.md`:** thêm dòng momentry với `lib/config-cmd.mjs`, `lib/ui-api.mjs` và `test/config-project.test.mjs`.

Một điều cần lưu ý: `CONTRIBUTING.md` chỉ ghi nhận cách làm đã chạy thật với người dùng. Commit `de173ef` đã nằm trên `main` của `vantt/momentry` nhưng chưa có bản phát hành nào chứa nó.

```

## 3. The init / doctor model — one engine
- **CMD-01** MUST · `doctor` is the only engine that reaches the desired state. Every desired state — config file, data store, hooks, skills, MCP entries, PATH, service, permissions — is a **doctor check with a fix**. No verb writes setup state outside this engine. Avoid: forgent `setup` writing rc lines, config, hooks and skills that `doctor --fix` doesn't know about.
- **CMD-02** MUST · `doctor` is read-only. `doctor --fix` repairs what exists but has drifted or broken. It never **creates** a new workspace or project: checks that create one are marked `creates` and only run under `init`, just as `git status` never runs `git init`.
- **CMD-03** MUST · `init` = `doctor --fix` with `creates` checks enabled, then "✓ Ready" and the next step (ONB-10). It is idempotent, so re-running it is always safe. For agent tools, it detects installed hosts and connects them; with `--yes` it uses project scope. So `init --yes` alone yields a working setup.
- **CMD-04** MUST · There is no `setup` verb. Keep an old one only as a hidden alias of `init` for a deprecation window.
- **CMD-05** SHOULD · `status` runs the fast subset of the same checks and ends with exactly one next command.

## 4. Conventions
- **CMD-06** MUST · Both `--version` and `version` work; `version --json` returns the full fingerprint (VER-04).
- **CMD-07** MUST · Global flags mean the same thing on every verb: `--json`, `-y/--yes`, `--dry-run`, `-q/--quiet`, `-v/--verbose`, `--no-color` (and honour `NO_COLOR`), `-c/--config <file>`.
- **CMD-08** MUST · Exit codes, the same for every verb:
  - `0` ok;
  - `1` problems found or failed;

# cs-packaging-distribution

## ⚑ PRIORITY ORDER — the owner's rule; it overrides everything below

1. **User experience (paramount)**
   - **First contact:** intro, install, quick start, first success.
   - **Command syntax:** one surface, the same in every project — `init` the first time, `doctor` when something's wrong, `update` for a new version.
   - **Agent-native:** `--help` and `--json` are enough for an agent to install, set up and repair the tool.
   - **Ease:**
     - one-command install and update;
     - minimal dependencies;
     - config that is easy to understand and edit;
     - errors that include the fix.
2. **Safety:** integrity checks, change only what we own, keep user data, least privilege.
3. **Correctness:** single source of truth, idempotent, atomic, rollback, tested.
4. **Fast & light:** small static binaries, quick startup, nothing slow on the hot path.

How to apply it:
- **Tier 1 first.** Handle tier 1 first and present it first.
- **Lower tiers stay invisible.** A lower-tier measure that adds friction is made automatic and invisible, not dropped.
- **When tier 1 yields.** A higher tier gives way only when it would break a lower-tier **MUST**.
- **Proven ways first.** If `references.md` has a working implementation from the owner's projects, adapt it rather than redesign; write down the reason for any deviation. Record every new proven way (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Layout — discover by listing; files starting with `_` are templates
- `common/NN-*.md`: language-agnostic rules. Frontmatter `tier` and `applies_when`; the read order is in `00-principles.md`.
- `languages/<lang>.md`: overlays (frontmatter `detect` = marker file).
- `channels/<channel>.md`: package managers, plugin marketplaces.
- `references.md`: which project to start from, plus rule → real code.
- `templates/`: `project-checklist.md` (output) and `install.sh` (tested skeleton).

Rules are one line each, with permanent ids (`CMD-03`) and a level: **MUST**, **SHOULD** or **MAY**.

## Workflow
1. **Profile** the project:
   - languages;
   - kind: CLI, daemon, MCP server, agent tool;
   - platforms;
   - whether it has config, secrets or a long-running process.
2. **Choose the archetype** (`07-command-surface.md` §1). A is a single binary with `update`; B is a manager plus a runtime. Then open the **"Start from"** row of `references.md` for the closest proven project.
3. **Select files.**
   - In `common/`, follow the read order in `00-principles.md` and keep files whose `applies_when` matches.
   - Add every language overlay whose `detect` file exists, plus `polyglot.md` if there is more than one language.
   - Add the channels in use.
   - If a language has no overlay, say so and use the common rules.
4. **Decide** using the checklist template's table, UX first:
   - tagline;
   - quick-start promise;
   - archetype and verbs;
   - install one-liner;
   - dependency budget;
   - config format.

   Then the rest. Ask only about what you can't infer.
5. **Audit.** List every MUST plus each SHOULD you adopt, with the status `done`, `todo` or `gap`. Collapse rules that don't apply to one line per file ("n/a: no daemon").
6. **Plan** tier-1 gaps first. Build order may follow dependencies (a release must exist before an installer can fetch it), but never postpone a tier-1 item for a lower tier.
7. **Write** `docs/packaging-checklist.md` in the project from the template.
8. **Implement** on request. For each rule, open its `references.md` entry and adapt that code (and `templates/`). Cite rule ids where useful.
9. **Verify** (below), update the checklist statuses, then **feed back** lessons per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
   When auditing an existing project, run Verify first to learn where it stands.

## Verify — run these yourself; each failure is a `gap` on that rule
Work in a temp HOME (`HOME=$(mktemp -d)`) so the user's real setup is never touched. `x` is the binary.

| # | Run / inspect | Pass when | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | README first screen | tagline about user pain/gain; quick start before internals; promise "from nothing to … in N min, you need …" | ONB-01/04/06 |
| 2 | `tail -1 install.sh`; `grep -n 'set -eu' install.sh`; `sh -n install.sh`; `sh install.sh --help` | `main "$@"` is last; strict mode; parses; help exits 0 | INS-02/04 |
| 3 | `x --version`; `x version --json` | both work; JSON has the fingerprint | CMD-06 |
| 4 | `x`; `x --help` | task-ordered "Get started" steps; an "Agents / automation" section | CMD-15/19 |
| 5 | `x init --help`; `x doctor --help`; `x update --help`; `x uninstall --help` | each covers: what it changes, flags + defaults, examples incl. non-interactive, exit codes, next step | CMD-16 |
| 6 | `x --bogus; echo $?` | exit 2 + "did you mean" / help hint | CMD-08/12 |
| 7 | `x init --yes --json </dev/null` | finishes without waiting; JSON envelope `{schema,ok,data,error,next}`; nothing but JSON on stdout | CMD-03/09/11/17 |
| 8 | `x doctor --json; echo $?` then `x doctor --fix --yes` | read-only first; exit 0 only when healthy; `fix` / `next` are runnable commands | CMD-02, DOC-02 |
| 9 | `x init --yes` again | idempotent: "nothing to do", no changes | CMD-03, PRN-05 |
| 10 | `x update --check; echo $?` (A) or `<ctl> --version` + `<ctl> upgrade --help` (B) | update path exists, exit codes per CMD-08 | CMD §1 |
| 11 | release workflow | checksums job needs all builds; tag == version gate; actions pinned by SHA | REL-06/10, VER-02 |
| 12 | **Agent-native test:** start a fresh subagent with no README access and only the instruction "install x from <release url> and get it working, using only its --help and --json output" | it reaches `doctor` ok without asking anyone | TST-04 |

Steps 1 and 12 need judgment; the rest are mechanical. Report results as a table (rule, pass/gap, evidence).
